The Georgia Restaurant Association (GRA) is proud to announce the finalists for the 2026 Georgia Restaurant Association Crystal of Excellence (GRACE) Awards. Celebrating its 18th year, the GRACE Awards recognize the people and organizations whose leadership and talent continue to strengthen Georgia’s restaurant and hospitality industry. Peers nominate finalists, giving members of Georgia’s hospitality community the opportunity to recognize those making a meaningful impact across the industry. The GRACE Academy, an independent panel of former GRACE honorees, along with current and former GRA board and advisory board members and GRA corporate partners, selects winners. “Every year, the GRACE Awards give us the opportunity to recognize the extraordinary people behind Georgia’s hospitality industry,” said Stephanie Fischer, president and CEO of the Georgia Restaurant Association. “This year’s finalists represent the talent and spirit of service that make our industry so special. From seasoned leaders to the next generation of hospitality professionals, each finalist is helping shape the future of hospitality in Georgia.” The 2026 GRACE Awards Gala will be held on Monday, Dec. 7, 2026, at the Georgia Aquarium in Atlanta, with George McKerrow returning to serve as master of ceremonies. The annual celebration brings together restaurant owners, operators, chefs, industry partners, and hospitality leaders from across the state for an evening dedicated to recognizing excellence throughout Georgia’s restaurant community. This year, the GRACE Awards will recognize finalists and honorees across a range of categories, including Restaurateur of the Year, Emerging Restaurateur of the Year, Chef of the Year, Future of Hospitality, Restaurant Manager of the Year, Restaurant Employee of the Year, the GRA Hall of Fame, Chairman’s Honor, and the Georgia on My Mind People’s Choice Awards. The evening will also honor this year’s GRACE Lifetime Achievement recipient. “What makes the GRACE Awards so meaningful is that these individuals are being recognized by the hospitality community they serve alongside every day,” added Fischer. “Their stories reflect the hard work that defines this industry. articles.title: Aba-Ra to open second London site in Soho
articles.titleKo: Aba-Ra to open second London site in Soho
articles.originalSummary: Georgian-inspired restaurant Aba-Ra, founded by Lia Walsh, will open a second London location in Soho in November. The new venue will be divided across three spaces: a 40-cover ground-floor restaurant, including eight seats at an open kitchen counter; an 18-cover lower-ground-floor lounge; and an 18-cover wine cellar and private dining room. The cellar will offer a dedicated tasting menu presenting a more refined interpretation of Georgian cuisine. The menu will draw on traditional Georgian dishes and cooking techniques, with freshly baked khachapuri, the country’s cheese-filled bread, served in smaller formats with cheese, meat and vegetable fillings. Handmade khinkali dumplings, soups served in clay pots beneath freshly baked bread, and meat skewers cooked over an open charcoal grill will also feature.

articles.titleKo: 100 Days In, Dakota Manchester Airport Established as a Stylish Destination For Travellers Both Near and Far
articles.originalSummary: The UK’s first luxury airport hotel at Manchester Airport has proven to be a hit with air travellers and local residents alike in its first 100 days. Dakota Hotel Group’s stylish, luxury hotel welcomed over 15,000 guests in the opening 100 days, including new guests experiencing the brand for the first time. Guests range from business travellers staying ahead of early morning domestic flights, alongside leisure guests heading to destinations across the globe. Recent guests have travelled on to New York, Los Angeles, Barbados, Singapore and Bangkok, as well as domestic and European routes. The hotel offers a luxury experience with ultimate comfort, to ensure travellers get a great night’s sleep before embarking on their journeys around the globe. Dakota Manchester Airport has seen strong demand throughout the week, with Thursdays and Fridays proving to be particularly busy as guests set off on long weekend breaks or prepare for early flights. The hotel’s parking packages have been extremely popular from the outset. Guests appreciate the convenience of leaving their vehicle at the hotel and being transferred directly to their airport terminal in comfort by Dakota’s concierge team. It also provides guests with the added reassurance of knowing their vehicle is parked in a secure hotel environment while they are away. It’s not just air travellers that are visiting Manchester Airport’s new luxury hotel, local residents and businesses have been enjoying the hotel’s stylish food and beverage offerings alongside hotel residents. At the heart of the hotel sits The Grill where the menu reflects true Dakota style, centering on bold, flavour-led dishes made with high-quality produce and generous portions. There are premium steaks, indulgent sides, and a carefully curated wine list, delivering a memorable dining experience. Steak has long been at the heart of the Dakota table, and the 28-day dry-aged fillet remains the best-selling dish across every Dakota restaurant, Manchester Airport included. Truffle Parmesan Fries and Tenderstem Broccoli sautéed in Garlic, Chilli and Soy are the most popular accompaniments, and Dakota’s signature Sticky Toffee Pudding, served in a rich butterscotch sauce with Madagascan Vanilla Ice Cream continues to be the dessert of choice. Many guests choose to start their holiday with a glass of Taittinger Champagne, making it a popular choice for celebrations and special occasions. In The Bar, the Hugo Spritz, Classic Margarita and a range of brunch-favourite cocktails continue to be among the best-selling drinks, helping guests relax and begin their travels in style. Matt Townley, Group Operations Director, said: “With Dakota Manchester Airport, we’re bringing something different to the airport market, combining the luxury, style and service that our guests know and trust with the convenience of an airport location. It’s also an exciting milestone as our second hotel in Manchester, strengthening our presence in a city that continues to be incredibly important to us. “It’s been an incredibly busy and successful start, and we’ve loved seeing familiar faces from our other Dakota hotels alongside so many new guests experiencing the brand for the first time. “We’re welcoming travellers from around the world, corporate guests and local residents alike. Fueled by strong Live Más Café performance, the brand is kicking off the concept’s next chapter with new sips, new markets and more ways to explore what fans want to drink next. On October 15, Taco Bell will introduce four new horchata-inspired sips at Live Más Café locations, bringing its take on the beloved flavor to three distinct formats. From the creamy, frozen Purple Horchata Chiller to the coffee-forward Chocolate Horchata Cold Brew Float, and the fruity, refreshing Strawberry and Vanilla-Spiced Horchata Refrescas, the four-drink lineup offers something for every kind of beverage craving. At the same time, Live Más Café is growing alongside its menu. Later this year, the concept will make its debut in the greater Indianapolis area, expand its Southern California footprint, and introduce a first-of-its-kind flagship in Las Vegas. The expansion marks an important next chapter for Live Más Café, which has quickly evolved from a single test location into a powerful business driver for Taco Bell. Whether fans want something frozen and indulgent, coffee-forward, or fruity and refreshing, there’s a sip for that. articles.title: The £95 Restaurant Ripple Effect: How Dining Out Drives Spending Beyond the Bill
articles.titleKo: The £95 Restaurant Ripple Effect: How Dining Out Drives Spending Beyond the Bill
articles.originalSummary: For more than 25 years, OpenTable has worked alongside restaurants to help them fill tables, connect with diners and grow their businesses. Its 2026 Restaurant Impact Report explores the vital role restaurants play in local economies, communities and everyday life, as well as how diners can help them thrive. The findings demonstrate that restaurants contribute far more than dining alone. They drive spending and footfall for surrounding businesses while creating spaces where people can come together and reconnect. The report explores the challenges restaurants face, including the impact of no-shows, and how small actions from diners can make a meaningful difference. Among the findings: Dining out has an economic ripple effect: 56% of UK diners spend at neighbouring businesses before or after their meal, spending an average of £95. Restaurants bring people together: 98% say local restaurants are important to their community, while 71% of Gen Z diners are likely to book a meal out to feel better or reconnect when they feel stressed or low. Supporting restaurants goes beyond the bill: Among Gen Z diners who made a restaurant reservation in the past year, 57% admit to having failed to show up at least once. A no-show for a table of two costs £55.70 on average, according to restaurant workers,² while 48% say understanding the financial impact of a no-show would make them more likely to honour or cancel a booking. “Restaurants are so much more than places to eat, they create jobs, bring people together and play an important role in the life of communities across the UK,” explains Sasha Shaker, Senior Director of Restaurant Sales and Service, OpenTable UK and Ireland . “This report showcases the industry’s wider impact and highlights why restaurants matter and why OpenTable is dedicated to advocating for their success.” Restaurants Fuel Employment and Local Economies More than half (56%) of UK restaurant diners said they spent money on other activities the last time they ate out locally.¹ Those who spent elsewhere alongside their meal spent £95.20 on average, rising to £126 among Gen Z and £118 among Millennials.¹ Restaurants see this impact first-hand, with 51% of hospitality workers saying their restaurant drives footfall or spending at nearby businesses. According to UKHospitality, hospitality is the UK’s third-largest employer, with restaurants employing 1.3 million people and contributing £44 billion to the economy annually. Restaurants Drive Community and Personal Wellbeing Restaurants provide spaces where people meet, celebrate and connect. More than half (56%) of UK diners are likely to book a meal out to feel better when stressed or low, rising to 71% among Gen Z diners.¹ If their favourite local restaurant disappeared tomorrow, 53% would miss the atmosphere and character it brings. Dr Martha Newson, Associate Professor of Psychology at the University of Greenwich , explains: “Sharing a meal at a restaurant is one of the oldest ways of bringing people together, because sitting around a table lets us focus on each other. Our research with over 10,000 people worldwide found face-to-face contact remains a strong predictor of wellbeing, as social bonds deepen through eye contact and shared experiences.” The Balancing Act for Restaurants While restaurants support their local areas, they are also navigating significant pressures. OpenTable’s research found that if VAT were reduced from 20% and restaurants passed the savings on through lower menu prices, 39% of diners would eat out more often, while a further 22% would spend more when they did. The report also explores how restaurants could use potential VAT savings. According to the research, 42% would primarily use a reduction to protect or increase staff wages and hours, 31% would lower menu prices for customers and 30% would reduce how often they need to raise prices. Fried chicken and mashed potatoes are a classic combination and Lee’s Famous Recipe Chicken is giving guests another reason to enjoy them on National Mashed Potato Day. On Sunday, October 18, Lee’s is celebrating with a free side of Famous Mashed Potatoes and gravy at participating restaurants, along with a special social media giveaway. For one day only, guests can enjoy a free regular side of Lee’s famous mashed potatoes and gravy with any $5 in-store purchase at participating restaurants. Lee’s is serving up more than just free mashed potatoes this National Mashed Potato Day. The brand is also teaming up with its longtime partners at Idahoan Foods to give fans a chance to win one of 10 exclusive chicken-and-potato-themed prize packs featuring Lee’s merchandise and other surprises. Fans can enter by commenting on the designated giveaway post on Lee’s Instagram page on October 18. An award-winning master of Cantonese cuisine whose distinguished career has seen him helm some of the city’s most respected Chinese dining establishments, Chef Lau brings a fresh perspective, two decades of experience and vibrant energy to the kitchen. Blending both innovation and tradition, his core culinary philosophy is grounded in three essential chapters – craft, heritage and memory – that unite to expand the possibilities and showcase the evolution of Cantonese cuisine. These fundamentals underpin a newly unveiled à la carte menu which retains signature classics for convivial celebrations, reimagines family favourites with nostalgic warmth, and introduces inventive creations that heighten the excitement of fine Chinese dining. This early realisation that delicious food brings happiness and nostalgia nourishes the soul ignited his lifelong passion for cooking. articles.title: Delmonico’s Hospitality Group Opens Boogie Bakery & Bistro in New York City’s Washington Heights Neighborhood
articles.titleKo: Delmonico’s Hospitality Group Opens Boogie Bakery & Bistro in New York City’s Washington Heights Neighborhood
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Delmonico’s Hospitality Group (DHG), parent company of the historic Delmonico’s restaurant, today opened Boogie Bakery & Bistro, a new all-day bakery and bistro at 4015 Broadway in Washington Heights. The restaurant serves breakfast, lunch, and dinner six days a week, with sourdough baked fresh on site at the heart of the menu. Boogie Bakery & Bistro marks the U.S. restaurant debut of Boogie Lab, a well-known European sourdough brand. The space is built for the people who live and work nearby: a place to pick up a warm loaf in the morning, grab a sandwich at lunch, or sit down for dinner and a drink. Under the culinary direction of DHG’s Executive Chef Adam Plitt, the menu puts sourdough first, with fresh breads and focaccia, sandwiches, sourdough pasta, and other bakery and bistro dishes. Bread is baked by hand all day in the open kitchen, where guests can watch the team shape and bake each loaf from the counter. “We built Boogie to be a neighborhood restaurant first,” said Dennis Turcinovic, owner and executive culinary partner, Delmonico’s Hospitality Group. “You walk in, you smell the bread, and you know it was made here today. Real sourdough has always come down to flour, water, salt, and time. Time has always been the hard part. It’s what makes good sourdough slow to make and costly to buy. Our process removes that barrier without cutting corners, so we can bake fresh all day and keep prices fair. But hospitality is not just about the food, it’s about people. Our job is to give this neighborhood a place they want to come back to, with good bread and a team that gets to know them.” Every loaf starts with three things: flour, water, and salt. Boogie’s own patented fermentation method, developed in Europe, allows the team to make true sourdough in about three to four hours, with no commercial yeast or additives. The result is consistent: bread that tastes the same on a busy Saturday as it does on a quiet Tuesday, baked in small batches and always fresh off the rack. The opening is part of Boogie’s wider growth in the U.S. The company has entered the wholesale market and plans to open a New Jersey production plant this fall to supply bread at scale. The Washington Heights restaurant will continue to bake its bread by hand, on site, every day. Boogie Bakery & Bistro is located at 4015 Broadway, New York, NY 10032. The bakery is open daily from 6:45 a.m. to 7 p.m., while the bistro is open Monday through Saturday from 5 p.m. to 10 p.m. For more information, visit www.boogielabnyc.com. Caitlin Mateo is an anthropologist turned chef, though for her, the two are inextricably linked. articles.title: QSR’s Next Battleground Isn’t Speed—It’s Feeling
articles.titleKo: QSR’s Next Battleground Isn’t Speed—It’s Feeling
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . According to Qualtrics' 2025 Consumer Trends Report, 66 percent of fast-food consumers reduce or stop spending after a single poor experience. QSR was built on efficiency, and it delivered on that promise for decades. Now, consumers want more than fast. They want fast and a good experience. Drive-thrus shaved to the second, digital ordering eliminating the queue, AI now rewriting the entire service model in real time. Speed has become table stakes. We said as much in our own research: efficiency alone no longer wins loyalty, consumers have come to expect it, which means it’s stopped being the thing that sets one brand apart from another. When every QSR is fast and highly digital, these things become the cost of doing business, not the source of competitive difference. And in chasing efficiency above all else, we’ve done something we didn’t intend. We’ve stripped time of any meaning. Fast is Table stakes. Felt is the Differentiator. Think back to a meal you can genuinely remember, one that made an impact on you. Did you note how quickly the food came out? Or was it the warmth of the person who served you? The smell when you walked in? The sound of a busy kitchen? That small, unexpected moment of human connection that you weren’t even expecting? Memory doesn’t form around speed. It forms around feeling. QSR’s are spending an enormous amount of energy to make things faster. But why aren’t they putting the same energy into making time well spent? The commercial stakes of getting this wrong are real. According to Qualtrics’ 2025 Consumer Trends Report, 66 percent of fast-food consumers reduce or stop spending after a single poor experience—more than any other sector. That’s a revenue problem. And it won’t be solved by shaving another ten seconds off the drive thru. How Do You Design “Time Well Spent?” The guest journey has four natural moments where brands can shift from transactional to memorable: Order, Wait, Pick-Up, and Return. Most brands invest heavily in the first, but the best ones invest intentionally across all four. ORDER : Make it Co-Creation, Not a Transaction Ordering is, by design, an act of cognitive efficiency. But there’s a more generous version, one that reduces overwhelm without stripping out warmth. Cava does this well. Their live, step-by-step build transforms ordering into something collaborative. Staff guide, suggest, build in front of you. The menu stops being a wall of decisions and becomes a conversation. You leave feeling like that meal was made for you. Because in a sense, it was. WAIT : Turn Awkward into Anticipated Where wait time can be cut, cut it. Where it can’t, transform it. Sweetgreen has understood this for years. Open kitchens and visible assembly do more than signal transparency, they signal craft. Watching your food being built stimulates appetite and makes the wait feel like part of the experience, not time stolen. Add sensory cues, smell, motion, sound, and impatience shifts into anticipation. People don’t mind waiting when they feel something worth waiting for is happening. PICK-UP : Not Confirmation of Completion, Confirmation of Care The pick-up moment is probably the most underrated touchpoint in the entire journey. It’s when the promise lands, and almost every brand treats it as an administrative handover. Number called. Bag passed. Done. Starbucks figured out something the rest of the industry hasn’t fully caught up with yet. Writing a name on a cup, adding a few words of encouragement like “you got this”‘” or “‘”have a great day,” shifts the entire feeling from transaction complete to this was made for you. A tiny thing with a disproportionate impact. RETURN : Give Them a Reason to Come Back Getting someone through the door once is a marketing challenge but getting them back is an experience challenge. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Pryze helps companies like Burger King, Amazon, Paris Baguette, and Sky Zone. Pryze, the mobile app that rewards hourly employees for staying focused and completing goals during their shifts, announced the launch of a fully redesigned version of its platform. The update addresses growing demand for real-time insights into revenue, retention, productivity, and focus, giving operators a shift-by-shift view of how teams are performing. Pryze helps companies like Burger King, Amazon, Paris Baguette, and Sky Zone across quick service restaurants, hospitality, and the public sector turn their employees into a competitive advantage through rewards, recognition, and competition. “We are thrilled to give our customers an upgraded app that gamifies business goals and turns raw data into actionable behavior patterns.” said Natalia Micheletti, CEO and Co-Founder of Pryze. “Operators want focused teams and great customer experiences. Employees want to feel seen and rewarded. This will bridge the gap between what operators want and what employees actually do.” With Pryze, employees begin each shift by selecting goals set by management, such as upselling desserts or increasing the average ticket, and then “lock in” to a focus session. They earn points for time spent focused and for goals completed, and lose points when they check their phones. At the end of each shift, employees bank their points and can redeem them for real rewards. By combining its proprietary behavioral data with revenue metrics, Pryze shows managers what drives results and helps them change employee behavior in real time. To view a demo of the new app and management dashboard or to schedule a live walkthrough, visit www.pryzeapp.com. The post Pryze Launches Fully Redesigned Platform appeared first on FSR magazine .

articles.title: Bar Prince Unveils Mythical Legends: A New Cocktail Menu Inspired By Scotland’s Most Enchanting Folklore
articles.titleKo: Bar Prince Unveils Mythical Legends: A New Cocktail Menu Inspired By Scotland’s Most Enchanting Folklore
articles.originalSummary: Following the success of last year’s Connected Icons , Bar Prince at The Balmoral invites guests into a world of myth, magic and storytelling with the launch of its newest cocktail menu, Mythical Legends . Launching this autumn, Mythical Legends draws inspiration from Scotland’s most enduring folklore, transforming legendary creatures and ancient tales into an immersive cocktail experience. From unicorns and selkies to witches, dragons and kelpies, the menu celebrates the stories that have captivated imaginations for generations. Overseen by Head Bartender Mattia Rovaris, each signature cocktail has been individually created by Bar Prince’s mixologists, with every serve inspired by a different Scottish legend. Guests are invited to discover the inspiration behind each creation, with every drink offering its own connection to Scotland’s rich mythical heritage. The theme extends beyond the cocktails themselves. Bespoke illustrations bring each character to life, transforming the menu into a contemporary storybook. Each copy has been meticulously handcrafted by Edinburgh’s Crawford Bookbinders, whose traditional techniques and attention to detail add another layer of craftsmanship, echoing Scotland’s long tradition of storytelling and artistry. Enhancing the experience further is a bespoke Mythical Legends Scent Mist, inspired by Scotland’s ancient forests, mist-covered lochs and legendary landscapes. Blending notes of cedarwood, chamomile and sandalwood with Scots pine, citrus and warming spice, it has been designed to transport guests into the world that inspired the cocktails. Capturing the spirit of Scotland’s wild landscapes and folklore through new techniques and evocative flavour combinations, highlights include The Untamed One , a shimmering tribute to Scotland’s national animal, the unicorn, blending Scottish vodka with coconut water, white chocolate, banana and lime leaf for an elegant serve. Double Identity , inspired by the selkie’s existence between land and sea, reimagines the whisky sour with coastal Scotch whisky, honey, citrus and warming spice. Meanwhile, Kingdom’s Cauldron draws on the tale of the Witch of Fife, combining whisky, botanicals, chocolate, vanilla and caramel into a rich and mysterious after-dark cocktail. Elsewhere, guests can discover the inspiration behind Messy-Nessie , a bright and herbaceous whisky highball inspired by Scotland’s most famous monster, or enjoy Fairy Queen , a decadent take on the Mai Tai featuring aged rum, roasted Brazil nuts and dark cacao. More than a cocktail menu, Mythical Legends is an invitation to explore Scotland’s legendary past through flavour, artistry and imagination. Continuing Bar Prince’s commitment to innovative cocktail storytelling, each drink reveals a new chapter in Scotland’s rich folklore. Mattia Rovaris, Head Bartender at Bar Prince, said: “Building on the success of Connected Icons, Mythical Legends gave our team the opportunity to tell a new chapter of Scotland’s story through the lens of folklore. Each cocktail has been created by a different member of the bar team, making the menu a true collective of ideas, creativity and personal interpretation. Paired with bespoke illustrations and scent, we’ve created an experience that invites guests to discover something new with every serve.” Discover the stories, flavours and aromas behind Scotland’s most captivating folklore at Bar Prince at The Balmoral. Mythical Legends launches this autumn. For more information or to reserve a table, visit: https://www.roccofortehotels.com/hotels-and-resorts/the-balmoral-hotel/dining/bar-prince/cocktail-menu/

articles.title: Walk-On’s Gives In-Depth Look at Newest Prototype
articles.titleKo: Walk-On’s Gives In-Depth Look at Newest Prototype
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Walk-On’s is offering a closer look at its next-generation restaurant prototype, a smaller, more flexible sports bar model aimed at reducing development costs and opening new real estate opportunities for franchisees. The company unveiled interior renderings of the prototype, which will range from 3,500 to 4,500 square feet, compared with the brand’s traditional restaurants of 7,000 to more than 8,000 square feet. The first location is scheduled to open in early 2027 on Perkins Road in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, measuring approximately 3,688 square feet with seating for 125 guests. Developed with Madrid-based restaurant firm Livit, the prototype uses a modular “kit of parts” that allows franchisees to customize certain features according to their market, available real estate, and operating preferences. The smaller footprint represents a significant departure from Walk-On’s traditional sports bar format, which has relied on expansive dining rooms and large gathering spaces. The company is seeking to preserve its full-service experience and sports-focused atmosphere within a restaurant that requires substantially less space. The prototype includes a redesigned kitchen equipped with clamshell grills and other equipment intended to simplify employee training, improve food consistency, and reduce ticket times. Despite the smaller kitchen, Walk-On’s plans to maintain its full menu. The restaurant will also feature a peninsula-style bar that can be adapted to different floor plans, a large television wall, and upgraded audiovisual equipment. A flexible lounge area will accommodate groups and game-day gatherings or provide additional dining capacity when needed. Off-premises business is another consideration. Dedicated pickup cubbies near the host stand will provide a designated area for DoorDash, Uber Eats, and other delivery orders, separating pickup traffic from the dining experience. Walk-On’s is also incorporating local sports memorabilia, including high school jerseys and athlete displays, to connect individual restaurants with their communities. Other features include an outdoor television wall and a host stand that doubles as a merchandise station. “We wanted to rethink what the Walk-On’s experience can look like without losing what makes us Walk-On’s,” CEO and cofounder Brandon Landry said in a statement. “The new design gives our franchisees more flexibility in where and how they build, while keeping the energy, hospitality and community connection our guests know and love.” The company previously announced that it was targeting development costs below $2 million for the new format, a key consideration as restaurant construction expenses continue to challenge franchise expansion. The prototype also draws on the performance of Walk-On’s approximately 3,700-square-foot restaurant at The Battery in Atlanta. According to the company, that location demonstrated the feasibility of operating its full menu and sports bar experience in a smaller, inline restaurant. articles.title: How Long Should a Menu Price Live?
articles.titleKo: How Long Should a Menu Price Live?
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . In 2024, Trader Joe’s raised the price of a banana from 19 cents to 23 cents . Normally, a four-cent price increase wouldn’t attract much attention. This one made national news. There was a reason. Trader Joe’s had sold bananas for 19 cents for more than two decades. The price had become familiar enough that changing it meant more than charging four additional cents for a piece of fruit. Nineteen cents had become part of what customers associated with Trader Joe’s value proposition. That raises an important question for quick-service restaurants. At a time when digital menu boards, apps, sophisticated analytics and AI make it increasingly easy to change prices, how do restaurants decide which prices should actually move? Pricing researcher Utpal Dholakia recently explored the idea that every price has a “life.” In “ What Decides the Life of a Price ?” he argues that some prices survive for years or decades while others disappear within hours, and that their appropriate lifespan depends on more than the technology or economics of changing them. It also depends on what those prices mean to customers. For QSRs, that distinction matters because not all menu prices play the same role. Some Prices Are More Memorable Than Others Consider the difference between the price of a Big Mac, a new limited-time product and a temporary offer in an app. All three are prices, but they occupy very different places in the customer’s mind. Someone who has bought Big Macs for years may not know the exact price at the restaurant down the street, but has had many opportunities to develop a sense of what a Big Mac should cost. A new product has no such history, while a temporary offer may be evaluated once and quickly forgotten. That suggests a continuum. Some prices are essentially forgettable. Others become reference prices, where customers may not remember the exact amount but develop expectations about what the product should cost. And a small number become iconic prices, where the price itself becomes part of what the brand represents. Costco’s $1.50 hot dog and soda combination, unchanged since 1985 , is perhaps the ultimate example. The further a price moves along that continuum, the more complicated changing it becomes. QSR Customers Have Long Memories Customer memory is especially important in QSR because of purchase frequency. A leisure traveler might stay at a particular hotel once or twice a year, encountering different dates, room types and market conditions each time. Hotel customers have also been trained for decades to expect prices to vary, so there may be no obvious answer to what a particular hotel room “should” cost. Now consider a customer who buys the same lunch from the same QSR two or three times a week. That customer has dozens of opportunities each year to observe the price of the same product. Over time, that familiar price becomes a reference point. A price increase can communicate more than the additional amount the customer has to pay. It can signal that the customer’s understanding of the brand’s value is no longer accurate. And when the price changes, the old price doesn’t simply disappear. Customers remember it, consciously or not, and compare the new price against it. The Value Wars Were Really About Reference Prices McDonald’s experienced this very publicly in 2024. After social media posts about an $18 Big Mac meal attracted widespread attention, McDonald’s USA President Joe Erlinger published an open letter addressing perceptions about the company’s prices . He reported that average menu prices had increased about 40 percent since 2019, while the average Big Mac had risen 21 percent, from $4.39 to $5.29. Dhiren Karnani noticed a guest behavior that’s become a common tale in QSR. Beverages are often now a price of entry. Yet how does that manifest at a legacy chain like KFC, as synonymous with its hero product (not drinks) as any retail operation in the country? Karnani, who elevated to the role of senior director, global head of food and experience at KFC Global in May, promoting from global director, next generation KFC and new concepts, says the aim started from the first observation and found its way to the second. Could KFC get customers to come for drinks and stay for chicken? Earlier in the year, the company began materially expanding “Kwench by KFC,” a specialty beverage extension that first ran across 38 stores. Success led to visions through the U.K. and Ireland over the summer and, as Yum! Brands shared in Q4, a 3,000 or so restaurant outlook by calendar-end 2026. Kwench appreciated a splashy “thirst-trap” Canadian launch in August, and, more recently, backed by a £38m investment from corporate, set course for Scotland. The Middle East and other global markets are lining up, too. Fueling Kwench are those same outset points. One, the market, from upstarts to drive-thru coffee concepts to large fast-food enterprises such as Taco Bell and McDonald’s, is responding to a surge of a specialty options capturing demand from energy to dirty sodas to refreshers. The other note is more than 90 percent of Kwench users in tests said they “loved” the new drinks and about half shared they’d visit KFC specifically for them. So, as Karnani and the brand hoped, customers came for Kwench, even if they weren’t, perhaps, showing up for chicken. That opened possibilities. “That’s actually what we’re seeing laid out,” says Karnani, who joined Yum! in 2017 as a senior brand manager for KFC U.K. and Ireland, “where this is definitely creating a halo and overall transaction growth. And that’s creating a lot more confidence to the system when it comes to Kwench. So, we’re really going deep on building this.” As Kwench matures, it’s broadening innovation. KFC added Matcha about a month ago, made with PerfectTed ceremonial grade tea and vanilla syrup, strawberry puree, and shortcake crumb. Karnani says matcha has become a category, like iced coffee was for younger consumers, needed by brands to signal you’re a beverage destination, especially later in the day. It’s evolved toward less of a menu alternative and more of a complement. Kwench, largely speaking, aims to “create the favorite version of the drink they already love,” Karnani says. With an item as buzzy as matcha, it meant partnering with a company like PerfectTed and delivering satisfaction on something familiar. “The reaction on social has been amazing,” he says. “People are like … ‘I can’t believe I am getting this matcha quality from KFC.’ And that’s exactly what we would want.” Karnani adds Kwench will keep tinkering with categories—today the brand has shakes, lattes, like an Iced Tiramisu, sparkling lemonades, and boba. A key, he explains, being to keep Kwench’s focus relatively narrow. “How do we really go deep in the categories where we have a clear right to play?” Karnani says. KFC developed Kwench so restaurants could move quickly as preferences do. Meanwhile, Kwench will create new news for categories people recognize. Currently, its Krunch Shake, caramel milkshake drizzled with caramel sauce, and topped with a krunchy speculoos crumb, is the brand’s top seller. Playing off a “Downright Dirty Meal” that arrived in the U.K. with “dirty items,” from loaded fries to a Louisiana burger, Kwench spun the item into a “Dirty Millionaire” version with chocolate cookie crumbs and chocolate and caramel sauces. “That’s another way we’re bringing new news into the platform, where it’s fully integrated into the menu concepts,” Karnani says. Family-friendly wing spot Jefferson’s is bringing back its “Coach of the Year” program once more, launched in celebration of National Coaches Day on Oct. 6. Now in its fourth year, the program has, in the last few years, honored dozens of coaches across all five states where Jefferson’s has locations: Kansas, Missouri, Tennessee, Alabama, and Georgia, resulting in an outpouring of support for the many beloved local coaches in Jefferson’s communities. The Jefferson’s Coach of the Year program celebrates coaches from any sport who exemplify compassionate leadership, community spirit, and dedication to their players. Coaches can be nominated by athletes, parents and guardians, school officials, neighbors, or anyone who has witnessed their impact. This year, the program will also launch at several new Jefferson’s locations that opened their doors in the last year, including restaurants in Bellevue, Tenn., Hartselle, Ala., and Weiss Lake, Ala., giving even more communities an opportunity to recognize a coach who goes above and beyond. How It Works: The nomination period is open now and will close at 11:59 p.m. on Oct. 18. Coaches of any sport, working with athletes of all ages, are eligible for nomination. Winners from each location will receive a $500 Jefferson’s gift card and their names added to the “Jefferson’s Coach of the Year” plaque displayed prominently at their respective restaurant. “Coaches have an incredible ability to shape not only athletes, but the communities around them,” said Brandon Graham, president of Jefferson’s Restaurants. “We’re proud to bring the Coach of the Year and establish it as a Jefferson’s tradition—and expand it to our newer locations. As Jefferson’s continues to grow, it’s important that we continue building relationships with the people and organizations that make each of our communities special.” 2025 Recap: Last year’s winners were chosen from an incredible pool of community leaders . Winners can be found on the individual location’s page. If you know of a life-changing coach in a Jefferson’s community, you can submit a nomination through the official Jefferson’s website, active now through 11:59 p.m. CST on Oct. 18. Sauce, a leading first-party ordering, delivery and retention platform for restaurants, today announced a strategic partnership with Grubhub, a leading U.S. food-ordering and delivery marketplace. Through the partnership, Sauce will become a direct ordering and delivery partner available to Grubhub merchants, enabling restaurants to support direct sales while leveraging Grubhub’s nationwide delivery network for fulfillment. Together, Sauce and Grubhub will provide restaurants with a seamless solution that pairs Sauce’s high-converting direct ordering platform with Grubhub’s nationwide fulfillment network. This partnership enables merchants to drive direct orders and retain ownership of customer relationships, all while leveraging Grubhub’s reliable delivery infrastructure. Through this joint offering, Sauce powers the customer-facing ordering and data tools, while Grubhub connects merchants with drivers for reliable last-mile delivery fulfillment. “Restaurants deserve online order and delivery technology that grows their business, strengthens connections with their customers, and delivers a best-in-class ordering experience,” said Li-ran Navon, CEO and Co-Founder of Sauce. “We’re excited to partner with Grubhub to give restaurant operators a powerful direct ordering solution backed by one of the most trusted delivery networks in the industry. Together, we’re making it easier for restaurants to support direct sales while building lasting customer loyalty.” Through the partnership, eligible restaurants will gain access to: Sauce’s high-converting branded online ordering platform Direct ordering websites optimized for mobile and SEO Integrated loyalty, marketing and AI-powered customer engagement tools Ownership of customer data and relationships Seamless delivery fulfillment powered by Grubhub’s nationwide logistics network Exclusive promotional opportunities and onboarding incentives “We’re excited to partner with Sauce to bring together direct ordering technology and delivery capabilities in a seamless experience for restaurants,” said Rachel Winkelman, Vice President, Enterprise Partnerships at Grubhub. “This partnership reflects our shared commitment to helping restaurants support their business and better serve their customers. Following the success of its first Together For Teachers campaign, TSG Restaurants is celebrating the meaningful impact the initiative has made in classrooms across Texas, Oklahoma, and Kansas. Created to recognize outstanding local educators while investing directly in the communities TSG Restaurants serves, the campaign invited teachers from communities surrounding its 79 McAlister’s Deli locations to share their stories and the difference they make in their classrooms every day. Local restaurant teams selected three Spotlight Teachers from each community, whose stories were featured on their local McAlister’s Deli Facebook pages as community members rallied behind them through social media engagement. One teacher from each participating location received a $250 classroom grant, resulting in $19,750 invested directly into local classrooms to help educators purchase supplies and educational resources ahead of the new school year. While the campaign generated exceptional engagement across social media, its greatest success can now be seen inside classrooms. Teachers used their grants to launch student-run vocational programs, purchase flexible seating, create more welcoming learning environments, provide school supplies for every student, expand music education programs, and invest in instructional resources that will benefit students throughout the school year. One recipient, Erika N., used the funds to help launch Leopard Brew, a student-run classroom coffee shop where students practice vocational and life skills including customer service, communication, money management, and following directions. “Leopard Brew will provide my students with hands-on opportunities to practice important vocational and life skills… giving our students a meaningful way to build confidence and independence while serving our school community.” Another recipient, Jennifer F., invested in podcasting equipment that will allow students to tell their stories, debate ideas, and strengthen communication and public-speaking skills. “This opportunity will help them build confidence, strengthen communication and public-speaking skills, and learn how to formulate and express their thoughts effectively.” For first-year teacher Paige T., the grant helped transform an empty classroom into a welcoming environment for students. “Starting the year with a classroom that feels like home not only for myself but all of my students… has been a huge blessing.” “At TSG Restaurants, serving our communities extends far beyond the four walls of our restaurants,” said Stephen Lee, President of TSG Restaurants. “Together For Teachers was created to celebrate educators and invest directly in the classrooms where future generations are shaped every day. Seeing how these teachers transformed a simple gift into opportunities that will benefit hundreds of students has been incredibly rewarding, and it reinforces our belief that supporting local communities is one of the most meaningful ways we can live out our purpose.” The Together For Teachers campaign reflects TSG Restaurants’ ongoing commitment to community involvement and keeping people at the heart of its mission. From supporting educators and nonprofits to partnering with local organizations and schools, the company continues to invest in initiatives that create lasting, meaningful impact in the neighborhoods its restaurants proudly serve. She’s published multiple cookbooks, appeared on countless television specials, and told the story of her culinary rise time and time again. But it’s the story beneath the accolades—the one about grief, fire, and rebirth—that defines her most. No identity is more sacred to Dahl than that of being a mother. Even after the devastating loss of her son, Justin, in 1994, she never stopped being one. His death lit a flame inside her, one that has never gone out. Everything she did then, and continues to do today, carries Justin’s legacy forward. In 1995, she felt guided to Sedona, a desert town nestled in the northern Verde Valley of Arizona. She didn’t arrive to build a culinary empire; she came to escape her heartbreak. Immersed in the red-rock canyons, turquoise waterfalls, and the fiery glow of the desert sun, she began to heal. Decades later, that same sun would still find her standing over an open flame. “Sedona is indescribable. When I arrived, I started hiking every day. I was healing in nature because I was very raw and fearful, and I’ve never moved to a place where I didn’t know a soul,” Dahl says. “I asked myself, ‘What am I doing here? When the doors of Dahl & Di Luca Ristorante Italiano opened later that year, something unlocked inside Dahl. It became an energizer for the town—Sedona had never seen a fine-dining restaurant of this caliber before. It was warmly welcomed by the community, and in that welcome, she found healing. “I was in the early stages of recovery from the loss of Justin when Dahl & Di Luca was born,” Dahl says. “Through the process of engaging with people, it became a community hub, and it was amazing because we could be charitable and immerse ourselves in this town as givers.” What would become her signature philosophy began to take form: “When you cook with love, you feed the soul.” As she opened more concepts throughout Sedona—from Mariposa’s Latin-inspired fine-dining grill to Pisa Lisa’s casual, artisanal wood-fired pizzas—her ability to serve others with love and intention was magnified. Chubby Cattle will assume restaurant-level operating responsibilities and lease obligations as it takes over each location. GEN Korean BBQ has signed a binding letter of intent to sell operations at 47 U.S. restaurants to Chubby Cattle Group in a $100 million transaction that would effectively shift the publicly traded company away from restaurant operations and toward its growing CPG business. The agreement, unanimously approved by GEN’s board of directors, calls for Chubby Cattle to take over the restaurants in four phases over 12 months. The companies are working to finalize the transaction within the next 30 days. GEN will retain ownership of its Korean BBQ brand and its entire CPG business. The company also plans to keep approximately three restaurants, including its Cerritos, California, location, to support product development, training, and staffing. Chubby Cattle will assume restaurant-level operating responsibilities and lease obligations as it takes over each location. The company plans to introduce wagyu-focused menus and fund restaurant conversions and buildouts using its own capital. The announcement does not specify whether all 47 restaurants will be rebranded under Chubby Cattle’s existing concepts. READ MORE : Gen Korean BBQ Considers $100M Sale of Restaurant Business Gen Korean BBQ Sees $100 Million Retail Opportunity Beyond Restaurants The transaction could substantially reduce GEN’s financial obligations. The company currently carries approximately $160 million in restaurant lease liabilities, which it expects to decrease as leases transfer to Chubby Cattle. “Securing a binding LOI with Chubby is a major milestone for GEN as part of the Company’s continued evolution into a premier CPG brand,” GEN chairman and CEO David Kim said in a statement. “We know Chubby through a partnership that is already delivering operating progress. This transaction would substantially reduce our restaurant lease obligations while giving GEN the option to participate in Chubby’s growth. We are moving quickly toward closing and believe this is the right next step for GEN and our shareholders.” Founded in 2016, Chubby Cattle operates more than 70 restaurants across over 25 brands, including Chubby Cattle, NIKU X, Wagyu House, and The X Pot. Its business spans fine dining, casual dining, and fast casual. Chubby Cattle reported $233 million in revenue in 2025, more than 10 times its revenue in 2021. The company also recently completed a capital raise at a $500 million valuation and is targeting 100 operating restaurants and one million Chubby Club members in 2026. The acquisition would give Chubby Cattle access to an established restaurant network and existing customer base as it expands its national presence. “Acquiring these 47 restaurants gives Chubby an established, high-traffic platform to accelerate our national growth,” Chubby Cattle founder David Zhao said in a statement. “GEN has built one of the leading Korean BBQ brands in the U.S. As we take over operations, we will build on the Korean BBQ experience these guests know with a wagyu-forward menu, and we are committed to completing this acquisition and executing a disciplined, phased transition.” Under the proposed transaction with Chubby Cattle, GEN will remain publicly traded, and its corporate infrastructure will be restructured to support the retail business. Senior staff will focus on expanding the company’s branded products rather than operating a national restaurant system. The agreement builds on an existing relationship between the companies. Earlier this year, GEN formed a joint venture with Chubby Cattle involving five restaurants that would transition to the Chubby Cattle brand. This release follows last fall’s launch of Salt & Straw’s Cinnamon Ancho Tacolate , which was crafted in collaboration with Taco Bell, and immediately went viral and sold out during its initial launch weekend last year. The Strawberry Pretzel Cheesecake Tacolate marks the first line extension of the Tacolate since its launch last year, and is available in the freezers, alongside the original Cinnamon Ancho Tacolate, of all Salt & Straw shops across the country (find your local shop here ) on Friday, October 16th. Both Tacolate flavors stand as elevated odes to everyone’s favorite childhood treat, and – in true Salt & Straw fashion – utilize innovative flavors and ingredients dreamed up by Co-Founder and Head Ice Cream Maker Tyler Malek . These sweet, salty, tangy tacos will be served alongside a silky, vanilla bean cheesecake sauce. “We’re obsessed with strawberry cheesecake in the Salt & Straw test kitchen, and the Strawberry Tacolate lets us take that combination to another level, ” said Tyler Malek, cofounder and head ice cream innovator of Salt & Straw ice cream. “We pair fresh Pacific Northwest strawberry ice cream with cream cheese, white chocolate, and a salty pretzel crumble, all finished with a liquid cheesecake drizzle. The expanded ramen lineup follows the breakout success of Chili Garlic Ramen, one of the most successful menu launches in Noodles & Company history. No one knows noodles like Noodles & Company. After more than 30 years of serving noodle dishes inspired by flavors from around the world, Noodles & Company is putting its own spin on another beloved noodle: ramen. Starting today, ramen noodles officially earn a permanent place on the Noodles & Company menu, launching with three bold, brothless bowls designed to deliver distinctly different flavor experiences. Gochujang Carbonara Ramen Noodles brings together Korean heat and Italian comfort, Sweet Sesame Steak Ramen Noodles balances savory and sweet flavors, and Spicy Korean Steak Ramen Noodles reimagines one of the brand’s longtime favorites with ramen noodles. The launch marks the beginning of a new permanent ramen category for Noodles & Company, giving the brand another way to showcase its noodle expertise while continuing to explore new flavors, combinations, and ramen creations over time. The expanded ramen lineup follows the breakout success of Chili Garlic Ramen, one of the most successful menu launches in Noodles & Company history. The limited-time dish brought more than 150,000 new guests to the brand, reinforcing what Noodles has known for more than 30 years: There are endless ways to experience a great bowl of noodles. “We’ve spent more than 30 years exploring what’s possible with noodles, and ramen gives us another incredible canvas for flavor and creativity,” said Tina Massey, vice president of culinary R&D at Noodles & Company. “What I love about this lineup is that each bowl delivers a completely different experience. From the creamy heat of the Gochujang Carbonara Ramen Noodles to the savory sweetness of Sweet Sesame Steak Ramen Noodles and the familiar bold flavor of Spicy Korean Steak Ramen Noodles, we’re showing just how versatile ramen can be while giving each dish a distinctly Noodles spin.” Three Distinct Ways to Ramen The new lineup showcases the versatility of ramen noodles through three brothless bowls featuring globally inspired sauces, fresh vegetables, and satisfying proteins: Gochujang Carbonara Ramen Noodles : Korean heat meets Italian comfort in an unexpected fusion featuring ramen noodles sautéed in a creamy gochujang-Parmesan carbonara sauce with bacon, napa cabbage and red cabbage, finished with grated Parmesan, Asian spice blend, and parsley. Sweet Sesame Steak Ramen Noodles : Savory meets sweet with ramen noodles sautéed with marinated steak, carrots, and red peppers, then finished with sesame seeds and cilantro for a satisfying balance of flavor and texture. Spicy Korean Steak Ramen Noodles : A ramen twist on the longtime guest favorite Spicy Korean Steak Noodles, this brothless bowl pairs ramen noodles with marinated steak, napa cabbage, red cabbage, and spinach in a sweet and spicy Korean-style gochujang barbecue sauce, topped with cucumber, scallions, and cilantro. “The incredible response to Chili Garlic Ramen showed us that our guests are hungry to see what Noodles can do with ramen,” said Dwayne Chambers, interim chief marketing officer at Noodles & Company. “Ramen gives us an exciting new way to build on 30 years of noodle expertise, bringing guests the comfort they love while continuing to surprise them with bold flavors and unexpected twists. Making ramen a permanent part of our menu is just the beginning of what we can do with this incredibly versatile noodle.” Noodles & Company’s new ramen menu is available starting today at restaurants nationwide, through the Noodles Rewards app and online at noodles.com . Gochujang Carbonara Ramen Noodles and Sweet Sesame Steak Ramen Noodles are available for a limited time, while ramen will remain a permanent menu category with new creations continuing to evolve the lineup. articles.title: California Pizza Kitchen Announces Collection of Salad Kits and Single-Serve Salads
articles.titleKo: California Pizza Kitchen Announces Collection of Salad Kits and Single-Serve Salads
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . The new CPK collection will feature restaurant-inspired recipes, elevated ingredients, and bold California flavors. California Pizza Kitchen (CPK), the iconic restaurant brand that revolutionized pizza, in partnership with FiveStar Gourmet Foods, North America’s largest producer of fresh single-serve foods, announced the launch of a premium collection of CPK-inspired salad kits and single-serve salads. The first CPK fresh retail products are expected to launch nationwide in 2027, with broader distribution and additional innovation planned as the partnership grows. The collaboration taps CPK’s long-standing legacy of culinary innovation in pizzas, pastas, and salads along with FiveStar’s expertise in premium fresh food to upgrade grocery’s refrigerated salads section, giving shoppers high-quality, exciting, and affordable options in fresh foods. “Salads have been a cornerstone of CPK since the beginning, from our BBQ Chicken Chopped to our Thai Crunch,” said Michael Beacham, President of California Pizza Kitchen Global. “Bringing that creativity, bold flavor and California approach to the fresh aisle is a natural next step, and FiveStar Gourmet Foods is the right partner to help us deliver the quality our guests expect, wherever they find us.” Restaurant Credibility Meets Retail Scale FiveStar Gourmet Foods, creator of Simply Fresh, brings nearly three decades of fresh-food expertise, national manufacturing capabilities, and large-scale retail execution to the partnership. “This category doesn’t need another ordinary salad,” said Tal Shoshan, Founder and CEO of FiveStar Gourmet Foods. “Retailers need products that give consumers a reason to come back with excitement and confidence. CPK brings something very different: a loved restaurant brand known for delicious, creative food.” “We started with the salads our guests already love and worked with FiveStar to translate them for the fresh aisle,” said Paul Pszybylski, Executive Chef and Vice President of Culinary Innovation at California Pizza Kitchen. “The goal is simple: when you open one at home, it should taste like something you’d order at our table.” The new CPK collection will feature restaurant-inspired recipes, elevated ingredients, and bold California flavors designed to differentiate at shelf and rebuild excitement in the fresh salad category. Products will be produced by FiveStar and feature the CPK brand alongside “Crafted by Simply Fresh.” Beyond Salads: A Platform for Growth While launching with salads, the partnership is designed for expansion. CPK and FiveStar plan to explore additional opportunities across refrigerated prepared foods, dressings and other categories as they build a broader retail platform together. The strategy complements CPK’s plan announced earlier this year to expand its frozen offerings beyond signature pizzas and into appetizers and entrees inspired by its restaurant menu. The brand is also expanding into non-traditional channels through the deployment of up to 1,000 automated retail kiosks nationwide over the next three years, expanding the brand into airports, universities, hospitals and other high-traffic locations. “When we began looking at the right strategic partner for CPK, FiveStar stood out for reasons that went well beyond manufacturing,” said Cory M. Baker, Founder and Managing Partner of Consortium Brand Partners. “Tal has built an organization with the infrastructure of a major national prepared foods company while retaining the speed, creativity, and entrepreneurial mindset that built the business. That combination is rare, and it gives us tremendous confidence in what we can build together.” For more information, visit www.cpk.com and follow @cpk on Instagram, @calpizzakitchen on TikTok or @calpizzakitchen on X. articles.title: BoomBozz Celebrates 28 Years with Special Offers and Free Pizza
articles.titleKo: BoomBozz Celebrates 28 Years with Special Offers and Free Pizza
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . What began as a 14-seat pizza restaurant in St. Matthews in 1998 has become one of Louisville’s recognizable homegrown restaurant brands. On Tuesday, October 20, BoomBozz will celebrate its 28th anniversary with free pizza, special offers, a Beat the Clock contest and the grand reopening of its remodeled Highlands restaurant. The anniversary theme is “28 YEARS. 28 SECONDS. FREE PIZZA FOR A YEAR.” At BoomBozz Highlands, 1448 Bardstown Road, dine-in guests can receive a free small one-topping pizza from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. The restaurant will also showcase its refreshed interior, bar and patio. From 3 p.m. to close, Highlands will offer $10 Medium Famous Pizza Pies. $2 Boom Brew beers and the Beat the Clock contest will be available throughout the day. Other participating Louisville-area BoomBozz locations will offer $10 Medium Famous Pizza Pies, $2 Boom Brew beers and Beat the Clock throughout their regular operating hours. A 28-Second Challenge with Pizza for a Year at Stake Each dine-in guest gets one attempt to start and stop a digital timer. Stop it at exactly 28.00 seconds and win Free Pizza for a Year – one small one-topping pizza each week for 52 weeks. Each participating location will award one grand prize. Guests who stop the timer at exactly 27.99 seconds win a $100 gift card; 27.98 seconds wins $50; and 27.97 seconds wins $25. There is no limit on the number of qualifying gift-card winners. Exact times are required, and each dine-in guest is limited to one attempt. A Louisville Original, 28 Years Later From its modest 14-seat beginnings, BoomBozz has built a following for award-winning pizzas, creative Famous Pizza Pies and a neighborhood sports-bar atmosphere. The anniversary recognizes the Louisville customers, employees and communities that have supported the brand across nearly three decades. The celebration also marks a new chapter for BoomBozz Highlands, which has undergone renovations to its dining room, bar and patio. The October 20 event is its official grand reopening. Anniversary Event at a Glance Tuesday, October 20, 2026 | BoomBozz Highlands, 1448 Bardstown Road, Louisville Highlands: Free small one-topping pizza, dine-in, 11 a.m.-3 p.m.; $10 Medium Famous Pizza Pies, dine-in, 3 p.m.-close; $2 Boom Brew and Beat the Clock all day. Other participating Louisville-area locations: $10 Medium Famous Pizza Pies, $2 Boom Brew and Beat the Clock during regular operating hours. The $10 Medium Famous Pizza Pie offer is dine-in only, limited to one per table/check, with no substitutions or combination with other discounts. Additional promotional rules apply. articles.title: Wingstop Announces Wings Flavored with Sour Patch Kids Glaze
articles.titleKo: Wingstop Announces Wings Flavored with Sour Patch Kids Glaze
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Halloween has a way of bringing unlikely duos together, and this year, Wingstop and the Sour Patch Kids candy may be the most unexpected yet. This Halloween, Wingstop is taking its flavor expertise somewhere no one saw coming, teaming up with the SOUR PATCH KIDS brand to create SOUR PATCH KIDS Wicked Punch. The SOUR PATCH KIDS brought the SOUR THEN SWEET mischief, and Wingstop made it saucy. The result is the ultimate candy-meets-wings crossover, one of Wingstop’s wildest flavor creations yet. Created by Wingstop’s Flavor Experts, Wicked Punch features a mischievous SOUR THEN SWEET REDBERRY glaze finished with SOUR PATCH KIDS Bitz for a wickedly fun twist, available across all proteins. Halloween has a way of bringing unlikely duos together, and this year, Wingstop and the SOUR PATCH KIDS candy may be the most unexpected yet. It’s surprising, a little unhinged and exactly the kind of flavor experience only Wingstop could pull off – a mashup that is equal parts trick, treat and dare. “Candy on wings? We know exactly what you’re thinking. But no, seriously, it has no business being this good,” said Michael Skipworth, President and CEO of Wingstop. “SOUR PATCH KIDS Wicked Punch wings bring sour and sweet together in a way only Wingstop can. It may sound unexpected, but one bite is all it takes to understand why this one is a treat.” “For the SOUR PATCH KIDS brand, Halloween usually means owning the candy bowl. This year, the SOUR PATCH KIDS brand decided candy wasn’t enough,” said Lauryn McDonough, Senior Director, Candy at Mondelēz International. “This is the first taste of the SOUR PATCH KIDS 13 Days of Mischief program, and transforming our signature SOUR THEN SWEET flavors into a wing flavor is exactly the kind of unexpected mischief our fans love. It brings both brands together in a way that is surprising, playful and delicious.” The Halloween mischief hits the menu Oct. 23, when Club Wingstop members get the first taste of SOUR PATCH KIDS Wicked Punch through exclusive early access. On Oct. 27, the flavor expands to Wingstop menus nationwide, just in time for Halloween week. Bring it to a costume party, break it out during a scary-movie marathon or serve it after trick-or-treating for one final Halloween dare. For Halloween fans ready to embrace the mischief, SOUR PATCH KIDS Wicked Punch can be ordered through the Wingstop app or Wingstop.com. But like Halloween itself, the chaos won’t last forever. Wicked Punch disappears after Nov. 5, so try it before the SOUR PATCH KIDS take it back. *Available for a limited time only at participating locations in the U.S. While supplies last. Guests can order beverages and food from the new, limited-time menu beginning November 2 in participating coffeehouses. Caribou Coffee is bringing the warmth and coziness of the most wonderful time of the year to life with the launch of its 2026 holiday menu. Beginning Monday, Nov. 2, guests can discover the sweet taste of Cookie Butter, welcome back beloved beverages only available this time of year and pair their favorite seasonal sip with a collection of festive bites at participating Caribou coffeehouses nationwide while supplies last. New to this year’s menu is the Cookie Butter White Mocha, bringing together the caramelized, spiced notes of the classic flavor with the smooth sweetness of Caribou’s signature mocha crafted with real white chocolate chips and cookie crumbles. With a variety of beverage styles to customize each sip, guests can enjoy the new limited-time flavor as a traditional hot or iced mocha, a blended Cookie Butter White Mocha Cooler or a Cookie Butter White Mocha Espresso Shaker made with fresh espresso, shaken over ice and finished with a splash of oatmilk. Cookie Butter may be new to the menu, but several fan favorites are making their annual return. The classic Ho Ho Mint Mocha pairs real chocolate and rich espresso with a refreshing touch of mint, while the Spicy Mocha turns up the warmth featuring chocolate with ancho chile and cinnamon spices. The Cranberry Dark Chocolate collection also makes a comeback, bringing together rich chocolate with bright, tart cranberry flavor. As always, guests can modify their handcrafted beverages with non-dairy milk at no additional charge. The holiday flavors continue in the bakery case with the new Warm Spice Morning Bun, a flaky, buttery pastry rolled in a fragrant blend of cinnamon, cardamom, coriander and ginger. It joins returning limited-time menu items, including the decadent Chocolate Truffle Brownie topped with chocolate truffle ganache. Caribou’s holiday cups also have a fresh look this year, featuring hand-illustrated designs reminiscent of cozy sweaters, blankets, wrapping paper and all the familiar touches that make this time of year feel special. Each design reflects the personal touch that has long been part of the Caribou experience, from the artwork on the cup to the handcrafted beverage inside. “One of the things we love most about this time of year is seeing guests reconnect over seasonal favorites while discovering new beverages to match their holiday mood,” said Carrie Sazama, Director of Product, Caribou Coffee. “We wanted to create a collection that celebrates the many tastes of the season, and cookie butter felt like a perfect addition because its caramelized sweetness and warm spice pair beautifully with our signature White Mocha. Alongside returning classics like Ho Ho Mint Mocha, Cranberry and Spicy Mocha, these distinct flavor profiles come together in a menu that captures the coziness of the holidays and feels unmistakably Caribou.” Meet the new Cookie Butter lineup Cookie Butter White Mocha (NEW) : The warm, spiced flavor of cookie butter comes together with melted real white chocolate, rich espresso and steamed milk. Served hot and finished with whipped cream and crumbled cookie butter cookies. Iced Cookie Butter White Mocha (NEW) : White chocolate and cookie butter flavor are combined with espresso and milk, then poured over ice for a cool and creamy way to enjoy the warm, spiced sweetness of cookie butter. Cookie Butter White Mocha Espresso Shaker (NEW) : Fresh espresso and cookie butter flavor are shaken over ice, then finished with a splash of oatmilk for a smooth, espresso-forward seasonal sip. Cookie Butter White Mocha Caribou Cooler Blended Beverage (NEW) : A creamy, blended combination of real white chocolate, cookie butter flavor and coffee. Topped with whipped cream and crumbled cookie butter cookies. We

Slice House by Tony Gemignani, the highly successful crafted fast-casual pizza franchise by world renowned pizzaiolo Tony Gemignani, is proud to announce the October 17, 2026 opening of its first Contra Costa County location in Brentwood. Located at 2523 Sand Creek Road in The Streets of Brentwood outdoor mall, the new pizzeria will welcome guests to experience Gemignani’s award-winning pizza in a community-driven setting. Opening day events, which begin at 11 a.m., include a Slice House t-shirt giveaway for the first 50 guests and a raffle for the chance to win free pizza for one year. Nitin and Mansi Bhatia, the brand partners behind the new location, bring a strong local perspective to Slice House Brentwood. They chose the city for their first restaurant because of its close-knit community, growing dining scene, and family-friendly nature. As business owners invested in Contra Costa County, they are focused on creating local jobs, giving back to the community, and offering a welcoming place where residents can gather over handcrafted pizza made with premium, from scratch ingredients. “It has been such a pleasure working with dedicated partners like Nitin and Mansi to further expand Slice House’s footprint in the San Francisco Bay Area and bring our pizzas to the incredible community of Brentwood,” shares founder Tony Gemignani. “We are excited to open the doors to this location, and I look forward to welcoming guests from across Contra Costa County to enjoy our artisan pizza during the grand opening celebration and in the years to come.” Slice House Brentwood features an expansive menu of Gemignani’s acclaimed New York, Sicilian, Grandma, and Detroit-style pizzas, available by the slice or as whole pies. Staying true to Gemignani’s approach, the menu places an emphasis on artisanal, from-scratch preparation and high-quality ingredients, with house-made components and thoughtfully sourced products from trusted purveyors. The menu also includes pasta, wings, fresh salads, and options for gluten-free, vegan, and vegetarian diners, complemented by a beverage selection of craft beers, premium wines, and non-alcoholic offerings. As is tradition with every new Slice House brand partner, Slice House Brentwood features two signature pizzas created by Gemignani in partnership with the Bhatias. Both are New York-style pies built around local Brentwood corn, a nod to the city’s deep farming roots, and available by the slice only. articles.title: Alexandria Restaurant Partners Names Nazia Millwala President
articles.titleKo: Alexandria Restaurant Partners Names Nazia Millwala President
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . As president, Nazia Millwala will oversee ARP’s operations, finance, people and culture, marketing, and food and beverage execution. Alexandria Restaurant Partners (ARP), a leading Northern Virginia-based restaurant group that owns and operates concepts across Northern Virginia and Orlando, has appointed Nazia Millwala as president. Millwala most recently served as ARP’s chief financial officer and brings extensive experience across finance, marketing, development and organizational leadership to her expanded role. Millwala joined ARP in January 2022 as vice president of finance and was promoted to chief financial officer in August 2024. Her appointment as president marks the latest step in her progression within the company and an important new chapter for the Alexandria-based restaurant group. The appointment is part of a planned leadership evolution as ARP partners Dave Nicholas, David Clapp and Scott Shaw shift their focus away from day-to-day management. As president, Millwala will oversee ARP’s operations, finance, people and culture, marketing, and food and beverage execution. Her first-year priorities include ensuring a smooth transition, building an expanded executive leadership team and establishing a strong operational structure for the company’s future. “Scott, David and I are incredibly proud of what our team has built, and we believe this is the right time to transition day-to-day leadership to Nazia,” said Dave Nicholas, co-founder and partner of Alexandria Restaurant Partners. “She has earned the trust and respect of our team through her thoughtful leadership, broad business perspective and genuine commitment to our people. We look forward to remaining involved and supporting her as she leads ARP forward.” Building on more than a decade of growth, Millwala’s strategy will focus on ARP’s people, management development and community involvement. Over the next 18 months, she plans to develop the company’s next generation of managers and leaders, create new opportunities for employees and deepen ARP’s connections throughout Alexandria and Orlando. Her strategy will also include growing sales channels such as catering, strengthening marketing efforts and continuing to evolve the company’s concepts and guest experiences. “ARP’s greatest strength is the people who bring our restaurants to life every day,” said Millwala. “My priority is to give our teams the clarity and support they need to do their best work. We have an incredible opportunity to build on what makes our restaurants special, find new ways to serve our guests and contribute even more to the communities we call home.” Millwala’s people-first, guest-focused philosophy defines hospitality as a genuine human connection between restaurant teams and their guests, an approach that will guide ARP’s next chapter. Before joining ARP, Millwala spent 12 years with Yum! Brands, holding leadership roles across finance, marketing and development for KFC and Pizza Hut in Canada, the Middle East, North Africa, Pakistan and Turkey. Her responsibilities ranged from business analysis and regional marketing strategy to franchise development, market expansion and portfolio growth. Millwala began her career at KPMG, where she worked with Fortune 500 companies and developed a strong foundation in financial analysis, risk assessment and strategic planning. Born and raised in Dubai, she earned a degree in commerce from the University of Wollongong in Australia and an International MBA from IE Business School in Madrid, Spain. Smalls Sliders is making sure its local impact extends well beyond the Can. Smalls Sliders and its local franchisees have recognized individuals and organizations making a meaningful difference in the communities they serve through its Smalls Town Hero program. Since its inception in 2024, the fast-growing slider brand has contributed more than $60,000 to local causes across its growing footprint Built into the brand’s approach to entering new communities, the programgives local franchisees an opportunity to identify and celebrate a person or organization whose work embodies the spirit of their community. Honorees are recognized around each Can’s grand opening, often accompanied by a charitable contribution supporting their continued impact. “Opening a new Can is about more than bringing Smalls to another market. It’s about becoming part of that community from day one,” said Brandon Landry, founder of Smalls Sliders. “There are incredible people and organizations already doing meaningful work in every town we enter, and this program gives us an opportunity to celebrate them and help make their day, and their community, a small bit better.” Throughout 2026, Smalls Town Hero honorees have supported causes spanning food insecurity, youth development, veteran services, education and family assistance. Honorees have included Boot Campaign in Tyler, Texas; PORCH Marietta in Marietta, Georgia; Boys & Girls Club of the Permian Basin in Odessa, Texas; Joshua House in Lutz, Florida; and community leader Al Holdren in Muncie, Indiana, among others—extending the impact of each new Can beyond its opening and into the communities Smalls serves.
