articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Cicis Pizza, the original all-you-can-eat pizza buffet known for delivering TBPVA (The Best Pizza Value Anywhere), has appointed Kimberly Thompson as Executive Vice President of Development. Bringing over a decade of franchise development leadership experience across some of the restaurant industry’s most recognizable brands, Thompson will help identify new opportunities for expansion nationwide. Thompson joins Cicis following franchise development leadership roles with Bonchon, Walk-On’s Sports Bistreaux, Jack in the Box, Del Taco and Philly Pretzel Factory. Throughout her career, she has worked closely with single- and multi-unit operators, guiding franchise development strategies, evaluating new markets and helping qualified candidates navigate the franchise ownership process. “As we look toward the next chapter of Cicis’ growth, we’re focused on being intentional about where we expand, who we grow with and how we support our franchisees along the way,” said Jeff Hetsel, President of Cicis Pizza. “We see tremendous opportunity to build on the brand’s established presence while introducing Cicis to new communities across the country. Kimberly brings the leadership and strategic perspective to help us pursue that vision while maintaining the relationships and support that have been central to Cicis’ success.” In her new role, Thompson will focus on expanding Cicis’ franchise development pipeline, identifying qualified operators and supporting strategic growth across priority markets. Working alongside the brand’s leadership, operations and real estate teams, she will help prospective franchisees evaluate development opportunities while leveraging Cicis’ established training, site selection and supply chain resources. “When you look at Cicis, you have a brand that families have known and loved for decades, a value proposition that resonates with today’s consumers and a business model that gives operators multiple ways to serve their communities,” said Thompson. “What excites me most is the opportunity ahead. We have an established foundation, strong franchisee support and strong potential to introduce Cicis to new markets. Our goal is to double the brand’s footprint over the next five years, and I’m looking forward to connecting with ambitious operators who want to be part of that growth.” The appointment comes as Cicis continues investing in restaurant operations, technology and guest engagement. The brand offers multiple revenue opportunities through its signature all-you-can-eat buffet, carryout, catering, delivery and arcade game rooms, supported by national marketing resources, franchisee training, real estate expertise and its distribution partner, JMC Restaurant Distribution. With nearly 300 restaurants across more than 23 states, Cicis is pursuing new development opportunities in Texas, the Carolinas, Georgia, Alabama, and Florida. For more information about franchise opportunities with Cicis Pizza, visit https://www.cicis.com/franchising. Corner Bakery Cafe’s began in 1991 with artisan bread-making in Maggiano’s kitchens in Chicago. As its menu expanded to breakfast, lunch and dinner, the brand maintained its bakery foundation, emphasizing quality ingredients, thoughtful preparation and welcoming hospitality. Beginning today, Corner Bakery is offering a complimentary surprise dessert sample every day from 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. and 5 to 7 p.m. at all corporate-owned cafes. Timed for a sweet treat around lunch or dinner, the program features seven treats, including custom butter cakes and a lemon tart developed especially for Corner Bakery. “Guests often come in knowing exactly what they want, and it’s easy to overlook something new when you already have a favorite,” said Erin Hasselgren, president of Corner Bakery Cafe. “We wanted to give them a chance to try a treat before committing to an order. It also gives our cafe teams a reason to start a conversation, hear what guests think and help them discover more of the menu.” The custom desserts were developed with French Gourmet and ShellsbyDesign, including butter cakes, which Datassential identified as the fastest-growing dessert. “The advantage of a custom recipe is that the brand gets a say in the dessert itself, beyond simply choosing something from a catalog,” said Don Smith, CEO of French Gourmet/ShellsbyDesign. “For Corner Bakery, we want these butter cakes and tarts to become something guests stop in for, even when they weren’t planning to stay for a meal.” The sampling lineup includes Tuxedo Butter Cake, Lemon Tart, Salted Brown Butter Crispy Bar, Almond Butter Cake, Pecan Chocolate Chunk Bar, Fudge Brownie and Chocolate Peanut Butter Cake. Guests can check Corner Bakery Cafe’s social media daily to discover the surprise sample of the day. To explore the full menu and find their nearest cafe, visit cornerbakerycafe.com. Stonefire Grill, a premier fast-casual family dining destination for more than 25 years, serving generous portions of scratch-made, classic American-inspired dishes, has introduced a new lineup of seasonal menu offerings featuring comforting flavors and fresh takes on familiar favorites. Available starting today at all Stonefire Grill locations throughout Southern California, the menu features six new dishes, from scratch-made soups and satisfying sides to fresh salads and pizzas. The new lineup arrives at a time when gathering around the table takes on special meaning, giving families and friends more opportunities to share a meal, reconnect and enjoy Stonefire Grill together. “Seasonal menus give us the chance to build on the dishes our guests already know and love while bringing the flavors of special times of the year to the table,” said David Youngberg, CEO of Stonefire Grill. “We’re intentional about creating seasonal menus that feel familiar, approachable and comforting, while still giving families something new to discover. That balance is central to the Stonefire Grill experience. Every seasonal launch carries our ‘Happy to Serve’ approach and gives our guests one more reason to gather around the table and share a meal.” Stonefire Grill’s scratch-made seasonal menu additions include: Baked Potato Soup — Creamy potato and bacon soup topped with shredded cheddar cheese and green onions. Margherita Pizza — Classic combination of margherita sauce, fresh mozzarella and fresh basil. Harvest Salad — Seasonal salad featuring mixed greens, butternut squash, candied walnuts, feta cheese, dried cranberries and apple chips, tossed in a maple vinaigrette. Bacon Cheddar Loaded Mashed Potatoes — Stonefire Grill’s signature Garlic Mashed Potatoes, made from scratch with roasted garlic, butter, sour cream, cream cheese and cheddar cheese, loaded with bacon and topped with green onions and cumin crema. Chili Loaded Mashed Potatoes — Stonefire Grill’s signature Garlic Mashed Potatoes, made from scratch with roasted garlic, butter, sour cream, cream cheese and cheddar cheese, topped with tri tip chili, green onions and cumin crema. Italian Sausage Pizza — Savory pizza topped with Italian sausage, then finished with oregano and parmesan cheese. Other fall menu updates give guests more ways to enjoy Stonefire Grill favorites, including the popular protein-packed Mediterranean Market Salad, which debuted as part of the summer menu and is now a permanent offering. Stonefire Grill is also expanding its signature burger offering by giving guests the option to enjoy a Classic Cheeseburger or BBQ Bacon Cheddar Burger as a single or double patty, with either one 4-ounce patty or two 4-ounce patties. The Classic Cheeseburger features melted cheddar cheese, fresh lettuce, juicy tomato, caramelized onion, crisp pickles and Stonefire Grill’s special sauce, while the BBQ Bacon Cheddar Burger features crisp bacon, melted cheddar cheese, Stonefire Grill’s Signature BBQ sauce and Stonefire Grill’s special sauce. Both burgers are served on a potato brioche bun with kettle chips. These updates reflect Stonefire Grill’s continued focus on an evolving menu based on guest preferences while maintaining the quality and familiar flavors guests have come to expect. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Potbelly, the iconic neighborhood sandwich shop, is expanding its Central Florida footprint with a new shop opening Tuesday, Oct. 13, at Corta Commons in southwest Ocala. The opening marks the brand’s entry into Marion County and joins more than 15 shops currently operating across Florida. Situated within the Shoppes of Corta Commons, a growing, Sprouts-anchored, mixed-use destination along the State Road 200 corridor, the new location puts Potbelly amid an expanding mix of retail, dining and residential development in one of southwest Ocala’s active growth areas. Experienced multi-unit restaurant operator and Potbelly franchisee Danish Alidino is behind the new Corta Commons shop. Alidino and his partners at Deli Management LLC own and operate multiple restaurant concepts throughout Central Florida, bringing extensive experience leading teams and serving communities across the region. After opening his first Potbelly shop in Lady Lake, Florida in 2025, Alidino is continuing to grow with the brand while expanding his longstanding presence in the Ocala market. “I’ve been part of the restaurant community in Ocala for years, so I’ve had a front-row seat to how much this area has grown and evolved,” said Alidino. “Bringing Potbelly here gives us another way to serve a community we already know well. Our goal is for this shop to feel like part of the neighborhood from day one.” To celebrate the opening, Potbelly will host a Grand Opening celebration on October 24 from 10 a.m. to 12 noon, where the first 50 people in line will win Free Potbelly for a Year. A ribbon-cutting and other festivities will also be available for all attendees to enjoy. The Corta Commons shop will serve the brand’s signature lineup of toasty sandwiches and wraps, fresh salads, hand-dipped shakes and freshly baked cookies. Regular operating hours are 10 a.m. to 9 p.m. daily. Guests can order ahead or place catering orders through Potbelly.com or the Potbelly App. Delivery will also be available through Potbelly and participating third-party services. Opening in Ocala is part of a broader Potbelly Florida growth strategy, with more than 80 shops under development agreements across the state, including Tampa, Sarasota-Bradenton, Fort Myers-Naples, Broward County, Fort Lauderdale, West Palm Beach, Gainesville, Ocala and Panama City Beach. For exclusive offers and rewards, Potbelly invites guests to join the Potbelly Perks program, where members can unlock free sandwiches, cookies and special offers throughout the year. To sign up, visit www.potbelly.com/perks. For more information about the new Potbelly location, visit www.potbelly.com. The post Potbelly Opens in Ocala, Florida appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: Huey Magoo’s Opens in Independence, Missouri
articles.titleKo: Huey Magoo’s Opens in Independence, Missouri
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Huey Magoo’s, the fast-casual brand known for its bold flavors and handcrafted chicken tenders, is bringing its fan-favorite tenders to Independence with the grand opening of its newest location. The opening marks Huey Magoo’s 93rd restaurant nationwide, further expanding the brand’s commitment to bold flavors, fresh ingredients and made-to-order meals. Every tender starts with the best 3 percent of the chicken, the tenderloin, and is served hand-breaded, 24-hour marinated and grilled or “sauced” and tossed in buffalo, sweet red chili, lemon pepper or garlic parmesan. The 2,200-square-foot restaurant features a drive-thru, curbside pickup, a pickup window and patio seating, offering guests a variety of convenient ways to enjoy their meals, including dine-in, takeout, catering and online ordering through the Huey Magoo’s mobile app, website and third-party delivery services, including DoorDash, Uber Eats and Grubhub. The location is operated by Midwest Restaurant Group, which brings 10 years of restaurant industry experience and a passion for delivering an exceptional guest experience. It is the group’s first of ten planned Huey Magoo’s restaurants. “We are thrilled to open our first Huey Magoo’s restaurant and introduce the Independence community to the brand’s premium chicken tenders and welcoming hospitality,” said a Midwest Restaurant Group spokesperson. “Our team looks forward to drawing on its restaurant experience as we grow with Huey Magoo’s and establish a strong presence in the market.” The menu includes a robust selection of customizable options, including fresh-made salads, sandwiches, wraps and the most popular choice, tender meals. Guests can also enjoy hand-spun chips, freshly prepared coleslaw, banana pudding and house-made specialty dips, including Magoo’s, Spicy Magoo’s and Ranch, showcasing the brand’s commitment to quality and freshness. Six additional signature dips – Buffalo, Honey Mustard, BBQ, Garlic Parmesan, Sweet Red Chili and Bleu Cheese – and a variety of sides are available to customize every meal. There’s even more to love with the recent launch of the Magoo’s Rewards™ loyalty program , where members earn points toward free food with every purchase. New users receive a Buy One Get One Free 10-piece Tender Bites meal with a beverage purchase to redeem within 30 days. Members earn 10 points per $1 spent, with catering orders earning one point per $1, making every meal—whether a quick bite or a group gathering—more rewarding. The Huey Magoo’s mobile app makes ordering, tracking rewards, and accessing exclusive offers easier than ever. “Midwest Restaurant Group brings a decade of restaurant experience, strong operational expertise and a shared commitment to exceptional hospitality,” said Mike Sutter, Chief Operating Officer of Huey Magoo’s. “They are an ideal partner to lead our continued growth in Missouri, and we are thrilled to support them as they open their first Huey Magoo’s and introduce the brand to the Independence community.” Huey Magoo’s Independence is now open at 4049 Little Blue Parkway, Independence, MO 64057. Hours of operation are Sunday through Thursday, 10:30 a.m. to 10 p.m.; Friday and Saturday, 10:30 a.m. to midnight. For more information, visit HueyMagoos.com, to download the app, click here or contact the restaurant directly at 816-393-0465. articles.title: Crisp & Green to Buy and Convert 33 MAD Greens and Snappy Salads Locations
articles.titleKo: Crisp & Green to Buy and Convert 33 MAD Greens and Snappy Salads Locations
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The acquisition will introduce Crisp & Green to Phoenix and Austin and expand its existing presence in Denver and Dallas. Crisp & Green announced Tuesday an agreement to acquire 33 MAD Greens and Snappy Salads restaurants from the Coors family’s Salad Collective, a deal that positions the fast-casual chain to reach 100 locations by the end of 2026. The Minneapolis-based company, currently with roughly 60 units, plans to convert the acquired restaurants to the Crisp & Green brand over time. Combined with previously scheduled openings, the transaction would bring the chain to the 100-unit milestone just a decade after its founding in Minnesota. As part of the agreement, the Coors family will become a strategic minority partner in Crisp & Green. Financial terms were not disclosed, nor did the company provide a timeline for completing the restaurant conversions. The acquisition will introduce Crisp & Green to Phoenix and Austin and expand its existing presence in Denver and Dallas. The deal also marks a significant expansion for a brand that has grown through company-operated restaurants, franchising, and investments from friends and family without institutional capital. “We’ve spent the last decade proving that you can build a nationally recognized restaurant brand with a disciplined approach to growth, exceptional franchise partners and people who believe in what you’re building,” Steele Smiley, Crisp & Green founder and executive chairman, said in a statement. “Reaching 100 restaurants is a tremendous milestone, but what’s even more meaningful is how we’ve gotten here. We’ve built this business without institutional capital, and this transaction represents an exciting next chapter in our story.” Founded in 2016, Crisp & Green has focused much of its development on the Midwest and other markets throughout the middle of the country instead of concentrating on major coastal cities. The company has positioned itself around convenient, health-conscious dining, with a menu featuring made-from-scratch salads, grain bowls, wraps, sandwiches, and smoothies. Its wellness identity also extends outside its restaurants through community events and fitness programming. Smiley said the brand’s geographic strategy has allowed it to capitalize on demand for healthier restaurant options in communities that may have fewer established competitors in the category. “Consumers everywhere are looking for food that fits the way they want to live, and that demand isn’t limited to New York, Los Angeles or other major coastal cities,” Smiley said. “We’ve built our business by recognizing the opportunity in communities across the middle of the country, where guests want fresh, convenient food and a wellness community that accompanies it.” Darden Coors, chairman of Salad Collective, said the agreement aligns with the company’s vision for the health-conscious restaurant category. “Bringing MAD Greens and Snappy Salads together with Crisp & Green is a natural continuation of our strategy at Salad Collective,” Coors said in a statement. “We’re excited to partner with Crisp & Green and are confident in our shared vision.” Following the acquisition, Crisp & Green plans to continue opening restaurants through new development and franchise partnerships as it integrates the acquired locations into its system. The company has not disclosed how many of the 33 restaurants will be converted before the end of 2026 or how many additional openings are scheduled for the remainder of the year. “They bring together the right brand, seasoned leadership, and passionate franchise partners to execute the next phase of that vision,” Coors said. articles.titleKo: Domino’s New CEO Has a Plan to Reignite Growth
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Domino’s is attracting more customers, gaining market share, and expanding its delivery reach. But those successes are not translating into the sales growth the pizza giant wants, creating an immediate challenge for new CEO Joe Jordan. The chain reported U.S. same-store sales growth of just 0.3 percent in the third quarter, despite higher order counts across delivery and carryout. Customers are still purchasing pizza, including lower-income consumers facing financial pressure, but they are ordering fewer items per transaction. According to Jordan, who recently succeeded Russell Weiner as CEO, the priority is turning that customer traffic into higher sales and stronger franchisee profitability. “I believe growing orders is the most important thing a brand can do in the current environment,” Jordan said during the company’s third-quarter earnings call. “Consumers remain under pressure, but they continue to choose Domino’s. More orders bring more customers into our system, support our franchisees and create opportunities to drive greater frequency over time.” READ MORE : Why Domino’s Sees Order Counts as its Primary Growth Engine Domino’s CEO Russell Weiner to Retire, Joe Jordan Named Successor Domino’s Says Pizza Rivals Can’t Sustain Value War Domino’s U.S. retail sales increased 2.1 percent during the quarter, supported primarily by new restaurant openings. Carryout same-store sales rose 1 percent, and delivery declined 0.3 percent. Pricing increased 1.2 percent, but smaller transactions offset some of those gains. CFO Sandeep Reddy said the decline in items per order became more pronounced during the third quarter, particularly across carryout and first-party delivery. Although average ticket trends improved sequentially, the company expects consumer spending pressures to persist through the remainder of 2026. Jordan said lower-income customers continue to respond to Domino’s value offerings, suggesting demand has not disappeared. The challenge is encouraging those customers to purchase additional items without compromising affordability. Register today for the jam-packed Prosper Accelerate Conference in Dallas! The company has continued using its Best Deal Ever promotion to drive traffic, recently incorporating stuffed crust pizza to introduce customers to a higher-priced product. Jordan said the promotion has encouraged repeat purchases, potentially creating opportunities to improve average checks. Domino’s is also investing in more targeted promotions through its website and loyalty program. The company wants to move existing loyalty members into higher-frequency purchasing groups, encouraging additional visits through personalized offers. “Our loyalty program continues to work really hard for us,” Jordan said. “And a big focus there now with the scale that we have on that program is continuing to move our customers up in frequency bands.” One of Jordan’s biggest opportunities involves expanding the occasions in which customers consider Domino’s. The company recently introduced the Domino—a Detroit-style personal pizza. It’s product aimed at what Jordan calls the “me/we” occasion, where customers eat together but prefer individual meals. Traditionally, pizza has benefited from group orders. However, Jordan sees opportunities to compete with other quick-service categories by accommodating individual preferences without sacrificing the communal experience. The Domino launched during the final week of the third quarter, leaving little time to influence results. Nevertheless, the company sees it as an important opportunity to attract customers who might otherwise choose burgers, sandwiches, or other individual meals. articles.title: Savory Closes $200 Million Fund III, Sets Sights on More Growth
articles.titleKo: Savory Closes $200 Million Fund III, Sets Sights on More Growth
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Fund III continues Savory's strategy of partnering with profitable, emerging, founder-led restaurant concepts and pairing capital with a full operating platform. Savory Fund, the private equity firm behind the breakout growth of restaurant category leaders Swig and Mo’ Bettahs, announced the final close of Savory Fund III at $201.5 million, surpassing its $200 million target. The fund drew a mix of returning and new limited partners, including the country’s leading financial institutions, and has already deployed 35 percent of its capital. “Raising a fund is a vote of confidence, and our investors voted loudly,” said Andrew K. Smith, co-founder and Managing Director of Savory Fund. “The majority of our third fund’s LPs invested with us in Fund I or II. They’ve been here as we’ve helped scale 13 restaurant brands across the country, from Detroit-style pizza to Nashville-style hot chicken to dirty soda, and I don’t take it for granted that they came back. Seeing major banks join them was a proud moment for us. It tells me people are starting to see restaurants the way we always have: these are real businesses that create jobs, anchor neighborhoods, and give people a place to gather. And when they’re run well, they are also strong, profitable investments. We’ve got four standout brands in Fund III already, and we’re just getting started.” Fund III continues Savory’s strategy of partnering with profitable, emerging, founder-led restaurant concepts and pairing capital with a full operating platform led by CEO Clay Dover . The fund will ultimately include eight to nine portfolio companies across the quick-service, fast-casual, and casual dining segments. Four investments are already in place: South Block , a better-for-you acai and smoothie brand expanding beyond its home market in the Washington, D.C. area Bonrue Bakery , a European-style patisserie with a devoted Utah following Hawkers Asian Street Food , a Michelin Guide-recommended concept outperforming its category in AUVs and guest frequency Zao Asian Grill , a fast-casual leader posting nearly 20% percent same-store sales growth “Capital is the part of our business that’s easiest to explain, but it isn’t what sets Savory apart,” said Shauna K. Smith, co-founder and Managing Director of Savory Fund. “What our investors are really backing is the team behind the checks: operators who have opened restaurants, built playbooks, and know what it takes to scale without losing what made a brand special. Fund III gives us the runway to bring that expertise to more founders who are ready for their next chapter.” Since its founding in 2018, Savory has grown to a portfolio of 13 restaurant brands spanning 400+ restaurants across 27 states. Its track record includes two of the most talked-about restaurant brands in the West. Under Savory’s partnership, Swig grew from 17 to 46 locations before Savory sold a majority stake to The Larry H. Miller Company in 2022. Mo’ Bettahs grew from six to 56 locations, more than nine times its original footprint, before Savory sold a majority stake to Blue Marlin Partners and Trive Capital in 2024. Savory remains a minority owner of both brands, and Andrew K. Smith continues to serve on both boards. articles.title: Dillas Quesadillas Promotes Michael Mabry to Chief Operating Officer
articles.titleKo: Dillas Quesadillas Promotes Michael Mabry to Chief Operating Officer
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The promotion comes as Dillas prepares to accelerate expansion following nearly two years focused on strengthening its operations. Dillas Quesadillas has promoted restaurant industry veteran Michael Mabry to chief operating officer as the North Texas-based company strengthens its leadership team for its next phase of growth. Effective Oct. 7, Mabry will oversee day-to-day operations, marketing and franchise sales across the 11-location brand. The newly created position will allow co-founders Kyle and Maggie Gordon to focus on growth strategy and capital as Dillas works toward its goal of 50 locations by 2028. Mabry joined Dillas in August 2025 as head of franchise development, but his relationship with the Gordons spans more than a decade. He brings more than 30 years of restaurant industry experience, including serving as president and COO of MOOYAH Burgers, Fries & Shakes, chief development officer of Fuzzy’s Taco Shop and president of Famous Toastery. “Michael knows Dillas, knows us and understands what it takes to scale a restaurant brand,” said Kyle Gordon, co-founder and CEO of Dillas Quesadillas. “We have six restaurants in the DFW franchise pipeline and additional growth underway in Louisiana. Having someone with Michael’s experience leading the day-to-day business gives us confidence that we can grow while continuing to support our teams, franchise partners and guests.” The promotion comes as Dillas prepares to accelerate expansion following nearly two years focused on strengthening its operations. The company has simplified its menu, invested in technology and streamlined restaurant processes to prepare the business for growth. Dillas also recently opened its first nontraditional location inside Brookshire Grocery Arena in Bossier City, Louisiana. “Dillas is at an exciting point in its growth,” said Mabry. “We’ve built a strong operational foundation, and my focus now is making sure our operations, marketing and franchise development stay aligned as we add restaurants. Growth only works if our teams and franchise partners have the systems and resources to support it.” Founded in Plano in 2013 by Kyle and Maggie Gordon, Dillas has grown to 11 locations across Texas and Louisiana. The company expects to approach $20 million in systemwide sales in 2026 and is targeting 50 locations by 2028. articles.title: Ruby makes its French debut with the opening of Ruby Lilou in Marseille
articles.titleKo: Ruby makes its French debut with the opening of Ruby Lilou in Marseille
articles.originalSummary: Ruby , an urban lifestyle hotel and part of IHG Hotels & Resorts, opens Ruby Lilou in Marseille, marking the brand’s debut in France. Opening alongside Ruby Workspaces in France, Ruby Yani introduces Ruby Workspaces to the French market. Inspired by Marseille’s distinctive blend of Mediterranean ease and rebellious creativity, Ruby Lilou reflects the brand’s signature approach to creating hotels deeply connected to their destination. Set between the historic Vieux Port and the creative energy of La Joliette, the new hotel pairs thoughtful design with laid-back social spaces, a sun-drenched rooftop terrace, and the warm, easy-going spirit that defines a stay with Ruby. Located just moments from charming Le Panier, Marseille’s oldest quarter, Ruby Lilou places guests at the heart of one of the city’s most exciting districts. The hotel offers easy access to cultural landmarks, the waterfront and the city’s thriving business district. With vibrant cafes and the harbour in close proximity, Ruby Lilou is perfectly placed for exploring Marseille’s art, culture and Mediterranean lifestyle, or heading to the Calanques for a sun-drenched escape. Joliette metro station is just a three-minute walk away, Marseille Saint-Charles railway station can be reached in five minutes by metro, and Marseille Provence Airport is approximately 45 minutes away by public transport. Michael Struck, Founder and CEO of Ruby Group, said: “Opening Ruby Lilou marks an important milestone for us as we debut the Ruby brand in France. Marseille is a city with a strong sense of identity, creativity, and authenticity, making it a natural fit for Ruby. Together with Ruby Yani Workspaces, we have created a destination that reflects the character of the city while offering guests, workspace members and locals a place to stay, work and connect. We are excited to become part of Marseille’s vibrant community and look forward to welcoming many guests.” Lauren Krostue, Vice President, Global Brand Management, Ruby, said: “Marseille is a city that thrives on contrast, where heritage meets creativity, and laid-back Mediterranean living sits alongside a bold independent spirit. With Ruby Lilou, we wanted to capture that unique energy, creating a place that feels deeply rooted in its surroundings while offering the thoughtful design, comfort and character guests expect from Ruby.” La Belle Re-Belle Marseille has always followed its own rhythm. As France’s oldest city and largest port, it has been shaped by centuries of movement, cultural exchange and creative reinvention. While the nearby Côte d’Azur is known for polished glamour, Marseille has built its identity on raw harbour energy and the easy warmth of Provence. That spirit inspired the design of Ruby Lilou. Soft tones drawn from lavender fields, sun-bleached stone and the Mediterranean Sea are layered with graphic patterns, bold colours and unexpected references to the city’s rebellious creative culture. The result is a hotel that feels unmistakably Marseille while staying true to Ruby’s character-rich, design-led approach. Ruby Lilou features 237 rooms across the Nest, Cosy, Lovely and Wow categories, combining intelligent use of space with premium comfort. Inspired by luxury yacht design, every room offers oversized beds, walk-in rainfall showers, blackout curtains and carefully curated interiors that reflect Marseille’s maritime heritage and creative spirit. Ruby Lilou reflects the brand’s focus on soulful, city-centre stays for cosmopolitan, lifestyle-focused travellers, combining central locations, distinctive design and seamless, tech-enabled experiences. Music is woven throughout the experience, from curated sound programmes to live acts in the evening and in-room Marshall amplifiers and Bluetooth speakers, connecting guests more closely to the city’s creative culture. articles.titleKo: Cuisine Cuisine at The Mira Welcomes Newly Appointed Chinese Executive Chef Lau Sze‑yau, Presenting Cantonese Cuisine Reimagined Through Craft, Heritage and Memory
articles.originalSummary: Michelin-recommended contemporary Cantonese restaurant Cuisine Cuisine at The Mira , Tsim Sha Tsui, welcomes Lau Sze-yau as its new Executive Chef. An award-winning master of Cantonese cuisine whose distinguished career has seen him helm some of the city’s most respected Chinese dining establishments, Chef Lau brings a fresh perspective, two decades of experience and vibrant energy to the kitchen. Blending both innovation and tradition, his core culinary philosophy is grounded in three essential chapters – craft, heritage and memory – that unite to expand the possibilities and showcase the evolution of Cantonese cuisine. These fundamentals underpin a newly unveiled à la carte menu which retains signature classics for convivial celebrations, reimagines family favourites with nostalgic warmth, and introduces inventive creations that heighten the excitement of fine Chinese dining. Uniting Chef Lau’s culinary ingenuity with modern aesthetics in the restaurant’s elegant setting, the menu presents an exquisite feast designed to engage all the senses. With over two decades of culinary experience, Executive Chef Lau Sze-yau’s gastronomic journey was first sparked in childhood during family reunion dinners. Watching elders transform simple, fresh ingredients into a banquet of rich flavours – and seeing the joy it brought to loved ones – deeply moved him. This early realisation that delicious food brings happiness and nostalgia nourishes the soul ignited his lifelong passion for cooking. Chef Lau’s career in Cantonese gastronomy spans leading hospitality brands including The Hong Kong Bankers Club, Hong Kong Parkview and the Clearwater Bay Golf & Country Club. He honed his expertise at the Chinese Culinary Institute under the Vocational Training Council, completing advanced master classes and the Master Chef Course in Chinese Cuisine, where he was honoured as Outstanding Trainee of the 10th programme. His talent has earned widespread industry recognition, with consecutive gold and silver awards at the Vocational Training Council’s Asian Culinary Exchange from 2017 to 2019. Dedicated to promoting Cantonese culinary culture, he serves on the committees of the Asia Art of Cuisine Society and the Hong Kong Chinese Chefs Association, and was a judge at the 2019 Hong Kong International Culinary Classic. I am thrilled to join Cuisine Cuisine at The Mira and to share my contemporary vision of Cantonese cuisine, conceived through craft, heritage and memory, with multi-generational families of Hong Kong gourmands and guests from around the world,” says Executive Chef Lau Sze‑yau. “Grounded in authentic Cantonese flavours, my creations are elevated with modern touches in refined and often surprising presentations, ingredient pairings and culinary techniques. In harmony with the restaurant’s elegant concept, my goal is to curate memorable dining journeys that captivate through taste, aroma and visual beauty. Under the leadership of Chef Lau, Cuisine Cuisine at The Mira unveils nine new signature creations spanning appetisers, main courses and desserts – each testament to his versatility and creativity. This flavour journey unfolds across three chapters: infusing dynamic new life into traditional Cantonese frameworks, honouring time‑tested craftsmanship, and evoking cherished memories at the table. articles.title: NAYA Celebrating National Shawarma Day with $5 Offer
articles.titleKo: NAYA Celebrating National Shawarma Day with $5 Offer
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . NAYA, the Middle Eastern fast casual brand founded by Hady Kfoury, is celebrating National Shawarma Day on Thursday, October 15, with a $5 shawarma entrée offer at every location and a giveaway of free shawarma for a year. Shawarma accounts for 63% of all guest orders at NAYA, and chicken shawarma is the brand’s best-selling protein. NAYA marinates chicken thighs overnight in a spice blend from Lebanon of garlic, clove, cardamom and turmeric, then finishes them on the flat top for crisp, charred edges. Its braised beef shawarma, which launched as a fall LTO in 2025 and earned a permanent spot on the menu, is slow-braised for six hours with nutmeg, cinnamon and cardamom. “Shawarma is one of the first items a lot of our guests order and the reason they come back. We marinate our chicken overnight and braise our beef for six hours because there’s no shortcut to that flavor, even when you’re serving it in minutes,” said Hady Kfoury, Founder and CEO of NAYA. On October 15, from 3 to 5pm, guests at every NAYA location can order a chicken or braised beef shawarma entrée for $5, in restaurant only, limit one per person. Through October 19, guests can also enter to win Free Shawarma for a Year: 52 entrée cards, one shawarma a week, redeemable at any NAYA location. To enter, guests follow @eatnaya on Instagram, like the giveaway video and tag a friend in the comments. The winner will be announced October 19. articles.title: Chili’s Unleashes Chicken Parm Big Crispy
articles.titleKo: Chili’s Unleashes Chicken Parm Big Crispy
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Chili’s is introducing the new Chicken Parm Big Crispy chicken sandwich. The Big Crispy is getting a cheesy and pull-worthy upgrade. Since Chili’s Grill & Bar introduced the Big Crispy chicken sandwich earlier this year with six different variations, chicken sandwich orders have jumped 175 percent. Now, Chili’s is combining two fan favorites to create the new Chicken Parm Big Crispy. The new sandwich puts an unmistakably Chili’s spin on Chicken Parm by bringing together two guest favorites: Chili’s Big Crispy chicken sandwich and Fried Mozzarella layered with marinara sauce. The sandwich is served with fries, white cheddar mac & cheese, and sides of marinara and Chili’s house-made ranch. “We’ve loved seeing how guests responded to the Big Crispy, and it got us thinking about how we could build on that with flavors we know they already love,” said George Felix, chief marketing officer and executive vice president of Brinker International. “A Big Crispy topped with our fan-favorite Fried Mozz and marinara is craveable, over the top in all the right ways and unmistakably Chili’s. You won’t find a Chicken Parm with a better cheese pull than this.” Chicken Parm isn’t actually Italian, and neither is Chili’s. But Florence, Rome and Venice sound pretty Italian. Close enough. Beginning Oct. 13, Chili’s restaurants in Florence, Ky.; Rome, Ga.; and Venice, Fla. will offer guests an exclusive first taste of the new Chicken Parm Big Crispy before it is available nationwide. The three Chili’s restaurants will also feature fun surprises for guests to enjoy for a limited time, such as an Italian mural booth photo opp in Florence and commemorative plates for the first 150 guests that try the sandwich at each location. In a full commitment to the bit, Chili’s enlisted reality TV icon Nicole “Snooki” Polizzi, who, like the sandwich, is not actually Italian, for a tourism video filmed in Florence, Ky. Because when you have a not-actually-Italian sandwich in a not-actually-Italian Florence, there’s only one person to call. Not in Florence, Rome or Venice? Good news: starting Oct. 20, guests nationwide can get a taste of the Chicken Parm Big Crispy — but they have to know to ask for it through a Chili’s team member. articles.title: One Year In, Michael McDermott is Writing Chi-Chi’s Next Chapter
articles.titleKo: One Year In, Michael McDermott is Writing Chi-Chi’s Next Chapter
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Chi-Chi's was founded by Michael McDermott's father Marno McDermott. For Michael McDermott, the resurgence of Chi-Chi’s is personal. As the son of co-founder Marno McDermott, he grew up running around in the restaurants before going on to build concepts like Kona Grill. Quick history lesson: His father co-founded Chi-Chi’s alongside former Green Bay Packers player Max McGee in 1975. They took the brand public just four years later, and Chi-Chi’s grew to more than 200 locations across the country at its peak in the mid-1980s and 1990s. But the brand collapsed into bankruptcy in the early 2000s, and all locations closed by 2004 . Then, last year on October 6, Chi-Chi’s made its triumphant return with the opening of its first new location in Minneapolis suburb St. Louis Park, Minnesota. But reviving a legacy brand with this much history comes with a delicate balancing act. Longtime fans show up eager for the nostalgia of chips and salsa, Mexican pizza, and chimichangas, but sustainable growth requires winning over a new generation that never actually set foot in an OG location. Over the past year, McDermott’s commitment to listening to guests has shaped choices like introducing modernized menu items like birria and short rib tacos to rolling out a value-engineered lunch menu with smaller portions and accessible price points. Heading into its one-year mark, Chi-Chi’s expanded its offerings with a $10 to $15 lunch lineup and the return of fan favorites like the Twice Grilled BBQ Burrito, Seafood Nachos, and Margarita Chicken Tacos. The rollout showcases McDermott’s strategy of pairing scratch-made nostalgia with modern, accessible everyday value. McDermott notes he’s in talks with developers along the East Coast and throughout the Midwest, though he’ll likely open a few more strategic corporate stores to prove out this next model of Chi-Chi’s before officially announcing any franchise deals. Why was now the right time for Chi-Chi’s to make its comeback? I believe in divine timing. A couple of years ago, I was considering transforming one of the concepts we owned because I felt it had run its course. I had a few ideas, but nothing seemed quite right. Then one morning during meditation, the thought came to me: bring Chi-Chi’s back. I ran the idea by a few people, and they thought it was a great one. The rest is history. What made the idea especially meaningful is that my connection to Chi-Chi’s is deeply personal. I was around the company when I was nine or ten years old, before my family moved to Arizona. While I don’t remember every detail, I certainly remember the chips and salsa. More importantly, I understand the responsibility that comes with continuing what my father started. We wanted longtime fans to recognize and reconnect with the brand they remember, while also creating a restaurant that feels relevant today. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . A big meal called for a much bigger bag. Chipotle Mexican Grill is giving its iconic to-go bag a Big Ass upgrade. The limited-edition Big Ass Chipotle Bag is a larger-than-life take on a brand staple, created to celebrate Family Meals, Chipotle’s digital-exclusive group offering. Chipotle’s limited-edition Big Ass Chipotle Bag is a larger-than-life take on the brand’s iconic to-go bag, created to celebrate Family Meals, its digital-exclusive group offering designed to serve four to six people. How to Get a Big Ass Chipotle Bag Beginning today, Chipotle will give Rewards members in the U.S. the chance to win a Big Ass Chipotle Bag through a multi-week digital sweepstakes. Each week, winners will be selected from Rewards members who purchase a Family Meal through the Chipotle app or Chipotle.com automatically entered for a chance to win. The Biggest Bag in Chipotle History A big meal called for a much bigger bag. With a 170-liter capacity, the Big Ass Chipotle Bag measures 36 inches wide, 24 inches tall and 12 inches deep. “A Big Ass Meal deserves a Big Ass Bag,” said Fernando Machado, Chief Brand Officer at Chipotle. “We took one of the most recognizable parts of the Chipotle experience, gave it an outsized upgrade, and created something that’s impossible to miss. It’s fun, it’s ridiculous and it’s exactly the kind of thing we knew our fans would want to get their hands on.” Chipotle for the Whole Crew Previously known as Build-Your-Own Chipotle, Family Meals give groups everything they need to build their own Chipotle entrees. Guests can create bowls, tacos, salads, nachos and more with their choice of proteins, toppings and sides. “Group occasions are a growing part of our business, and Family Meals give guests more ways to enjoy Chipotle together,” said Stephanie Perdue, Senior Vice President, Brand Marketing at Chipotle. “With enough food to serve four to six people, it’s a convenient option for dinner, game days and all the moments when everyone wants something a little different.” At less than $10 per person, Family Meals offer abundant portions with convenient pickup or delivery. Guests can order through the Chipotle app, Chipotle.com or Chipotle.ca, with pickup available in as few as 10 minutes. Behind the Big Ass Bag The Big Ass Chipotle Bag will star in a new national advertising campaign, marking Chipotle’s first major work with agency partner GUT. The campaign gives Chipotle’s iconic takeout bag a high-fashion treatment, pairing it with unexpected items including a trumpet, Christmas tree and Chipotle chair to emphasize its outsized proportions. The idea taps into the power of fandom, turning a familiar piece of packaging into a cultural artifact that fans can experience, share and keep long after their meal is over. “The fun of this idea is how little explaining it needs,” said Ricky Casal, Chief Creative Officer at GUT Miami. “You see this ridiculously oversized Chipotle bag and immediately get the joke. articles.title: Bar Prince Unveils Mythical Legends: A New Cocktail Menu Inspired By Scotland’s Most Enchanting Folklore
articles.titleKo: Bar Prince Unveils Mythical Legends: A New Cocktail Menu Inspired By Scotland’s Most Enchanting Folklore
articles.originalSummary: Following the success of last year’s Connected Icons , Bar Prince at The Balmoral invites guests into a world of myth, magic and storytelling with the launch of its newest cocktail menu, Mythical Legends . Launching this autumn, Mythical Legends draws inspiration from Scotland’s most enduring folklore, transforming legendary creatures and ancient tales into an immersive cocktail experience. From unicorns and selkies to witches, dragons and kelpies, the menu celebrates the stories that have captivated imaginations for generations. Overseen by Head Bartender Mattia Rovaris, each signature cocktail has been individually created by Bar Prince’s mixologists, with every serve inspired by a different Scottish legend. Guests are invited to discover the inspiration behind each creation, with every drink offering its own connection to Scotland’s rich mythical heritage. The theme extends beyond the cocktails themselves. Bespoke illustrations bring each character to life, transforming the menu into a contemporary storybook. Each copy has been meticulously handcrafted by Edinburgh’s Crawford Bookbinders, whose traditional techniques and attention to detail add another layer of craftsmanship, echoing Scotland’s long tradition of storytelling and artistry. Enhancing the experience further is a bespoke Mythical Legends Scent Mist, inspired by Scotland’s ancient forests, mist-covered lochs and legendary landscapes. Blending notes of cedarwood, chamomile and sandalwood with Scots pine, citrus and warming spice, it has been designed to transport guests into the world that inspired the cocktails. Capturing the spirit of Scotland’s wild landscapes and folklore through new techniques and evocative flavour combinations, highlights include The Untamed One , a shimmering tribute to Scotland’s national animal, the unicorn, blending Scottish vodka with coconut water, white chocolate, banana and lime leaf for an elegant serve. Double Identity , inspired by the selkie’s existence between land and sea, reimagines the whisky sour with coastal Scotch whisky, honey, citrus and warming spice. Meanwhile, Kingdom’s Cauldron draws on the tale of the Witch of Fife, combining whisky, botanicals, chocolate, vanilla and caramel into a rich and mysterious after-dark cocktail. Elsewhere, guests can discover the inspiration behind Messy-Nessie , a bright and herbaceous whisky highball inspired by Scotland’s most famous monster, or enjoy Fairy Queen , a decadent take on the Mai Tai featuring aged rum, roasted Brazil nuts and dark cacao. More than a cocktail menu, Mythical Legends is an invitation to explore Scotland’s legendary past through flavour, artistry and imagination. Continuing Bar Prince’s commitment to innovative cocktail storytelling, each drink reveals a new chapter in Scotland’s rich folklore. Mattia Rovaris, Head Bartender at Bar Prince, said: “Building on the success of Connected Icons, Mythical Legends gave our team the opportunity to tell a new chapter of Scotland’s story through the lens of folklore. Each cocktail has been created by a different member of the bar team, making the menu a true collective of ideas, creativity and personal interpretation. Paired with bespoke illustrations and scent, we’ve created an experience that invites guests to discover something new with every serve.” Discover the stories, flavours and aromas behind Scotland’s most captivating folklore at Bar Prince at The Balmoral. Mythical Legends launches this autumn. For more information or to reserve a table, visit: https://www.roccofortehotels.com/hotels-and-resorts/the-balmoral-hotel/dining/bar-prince/cocktail-menu/

articles.title: Searcys Names Searcys Events Team Winners of Chef of the Year Competition
articles.titleKo: Searcys Names Searcys Events Team Winners of Chef of the Year Competition
articles.originalSummary: Searcys has announced the winners of its Chef of the Year competition, held in partnership with Laurent-Perrier. The competition showcases culinary talent from across the Searcys estate while celebrating excellence in food and Champagne pairing. Harry Wilson, General Manager, and Samuel Seedhouse, Head Chef, both of Searcys Events and Guards Polo Club, were named this year’s winners after impressing judges with a menu that combined creativity, technical skill and strong Champagne pairings. Their menu opened with three canapés including “Forêt Sauvage.” a mushroom parfait coated in white mushroom powder gel to create the illusion of a fresh mushroom, served on a forest-scape canapé tray with dry ice; “Éclair de la Mer” , butter-poached langoustine with choux pastry, lemon, tarragon and chives, served on a platter of shells; and “Canard Impérial” , duck rillette with watercress and nasturtium mousse and a caramelised onion wafer, served on an oyster platter. The starter, “Or des Marées” , featured hand-dived scallops, Chardonnay-infused grapes, charred globe artichoke, a Blanc de Blanc butter sauce and rose harissa oil, followed by the main course, “L’Oiseau Truffé” , consisting of guinea fowl stuffed with truffle, served with a coq au vin jaune sauce, rainbow chard and smoked pancetta. To finish, the dessert “Fraise, Fleur & Brisure” combined a white chocolate and pink peppercorn disk with a strawberry and elderflower parfait, clotted cream and honeycomb ice cream. The competition was open for the first time to all Searcys team members rather than just Chefs, 12 teams entered, and went through a series of rounds before culminating in a live final, where four shortlisted teams prepared and presented their menus to a judging panel comprising of senior Searcys chefs and Laurent-Perrier ambassadors. Judges included Paul Jackson, Managing Director of Searcys; Richard Lewis, UK Sales Director at Laurent-Perrier; and two-Michelin-starred chef Alex Dilling of Hotel Café Royal. “As a judge for the Chef of the Year Competition, it’s a real privilege to see the incredible talent and creativity across Searcys. The competition gives our chefs an opportunity to push their boundaries, showcase their technical skills, and create dishes that work alongside the Laurent-Perrier cuvées. It’s a fantastic celebration of culinary excellence and innovation.” “What stands out most about Chef of the Year is the commitment and pride our chefs bring to the competition. Judging their dishes is a great opportunity to see the high standards, creativity and attention to detail that define Searcys.” Said Alex Dilling. British-American chef Alex Dilling, behind London’s two-Michelin-starred restaurant at Hotel Café Royal. Dilling’s involvement in this year’s competition comes after the launch of ASCEND by Alex Dilling at Horizon 22, the venue’s first collaboration with a Michelin-starred chef. The annual Chef of the Year competition forms part of Searcys’ commitment to developing culinary talent and encouraging innovation across its venue portfolio. As the bespoke catering arm of the business, Searcys Events curates and delivers distinctive events across an impressive portfolio of partner venues, including Guildhall, Horizon 22, London Transport Museum, Royal Hospital Chelsea and Moco Museum. The team is also proud to be the catering partner at Guards Polo Club and has been entrusted with delivering hospitality at major events such as the Farnborough International Airshow, SailGP and a five-day cricket festival, showcasing its expertise across everything from intimate gatherings to large-scale, world-class occasions.

articles.originalSummary: To celebrate World Architecture Day (5th October), Harcourt Developments, the owners of Stanley Dock Liverpool, have today announced a new restaurant, that is set to open later this winter in the former Victorian pumphouse at Stanley Dock. Stanely Dock’s Grade II-listed Hydraulic Pumphouse and Accumulator Tower is set to become a stunning new 120-seat pizzeria following a £1.5 million transformation. Called 1848 Stanley Dock the name celebrates the year that Stanley Dock, designed by Jesse Hartley, opened. Operated by the Titanic Hotel Liverpool and owned by Harcourt Developments, the 4,400 sq. ft (410 sq. m) restaurant will create a new destination dining venue in the city’s iconic waterfront and historic docks. The 1848 Stanley Dock will combine the character of the original Victorian pumphouse with contemporary design. Taking centre stage will be a glass-walled extension, with 18.5 ft-tall ceilings and glazed doors, that that overlooks the dock and provides access to a waterfront dining terrace. Connecting the glazed extension with the original brick boiler room will be a 23ft-high atrium, creating a central space for dining and a cocktail bar. A new galleried mezzanine will add further seating, with feature brick walls on the lower level and a more intimate private dining area and lounge space above. Brian Connor, Titanic Hotel Liverpool general manager, says “ 1848 is an exciting addition to Stanley Dock and provides an opportunity to give another one of the site’s historic buildings a new lease of life. “The venue has such a distinctive character, and as with Titanic Hotel, retaining its original features while creating a contemporary space has been a key priority throughout the redevelopment. We’re looking forward to welcoming guests to 1848 Stanley Dock later this year and introducing a new dining experience to Liverpool.” Stanley Dock officially opened in 1848, with the pumphouse added shortly after in 1855. Housing the hydraulic pumping systems that powered the dock gates, capstans, cargo cranes and tobacco presses across both the North and South Warehouses for decades. The decline of Liverpool’s maritime trade led to Stanley Dock’s closure in 1985, until Harcourt Development bought the site in 2010. 1848 Stanley Dock is the latest phase of the ongoing £250 million regeneration plan for the area and is due to open to the public later this year.

articles.title: Subway® Unveils Blueprint, a Reimagined Restaurant and Brand Experience for EMEA
articles.titleKo: Subway® Unveils Blueprint, a Reimagined Restaurant and Brand Experience for EMEA
articles.originalSummary: Subway® today unveiled Blueprint, a reimagined restaurant and brand experience that modernises how guests order and eat to support growth across Europe, the Middle East and Africa (EMEA). From 1 January 2027, every new Subway restaurant and remodel in the region will be built to Blueprint, the centrepiece of the company’s multi-year business strategy. For more than 60 years, Subway has been built around customisation: every meal made to order exactly the guest’s way. Blueprint extends that customisation beyond the food to the rest of the experience. The concept began with listening to guests and franchisees. The result is a blueprint for how Subway and its restaurants will look, work and feel as the brand continues to grow. Blueprint covers three areas, each designed to give existing guests more reasons to return and new guests a reason to choose Subway: The restaurant. A fresh look and feel in a digitally connected space that flexes around guests and their choices. Expanded occasions . A new breakfast and coffee offer, Grab & Go, and Subway After Dark, an evening experience with a different menu and mood. The brand. Get Your Own Way, a new brand position and campaign for EMEA, giving Subway one consistent voice. “Guests want to eat their way, on their own schedule, and Blueprint is how we deliver on that,” said Tracy Gehlan, President, Subway EMEA . “We celebrate our guests’ individual choices, from how they order to when they visit to what they want in their meal, always with great food, great service and a great environment. For our franchisees, it means stronger restaurant economics and a stronger brand built for the long term.” Restaurants designed for today’s guests Blueprint restaurants are warmer, more modern, digitally connected spaces. Well-organised layouts and clearer information make the experience more intuitive for guests and easier for Sandwich Artists to manage, so they can give their full attention to the food and the guest in front of them. Choice and freshness take centre stage throughout the design, with salad ingredients, sauces and freshly baked bread showcased at the heart of the restaurant. Guests choose how they order, with every way designed for a seamless experience and every guest getting the same freedom to build a meal exactly their way. At the customisation counter, guests order with a Sandwich Artist, choosing their favourites as they go. Self-order kiosks let guests explore the full menu and customise at their own pace. Subway app and delivery make ordering favourites from home, work or on the move even simpler. An order-ready screen shows each order as it is completed, and a clearly marked collection point makes pick-up quick and easy. Cookies and coffee sit within reach for a last-minute craving. More moments for guests, from morning to evening As guests’ needs change throughout the day, so does the restaurant, with a menu, mood and experience to match. Mornings bring a new breakfast range and coffee offer, made with 100% Arabica beans and served the way each guest wants it, with a morning playlist setting the tone. A new Grab & Go option, available in fast-moving locations such as transport hubs, offers its own menu of meals made fresh in restaurant and ready to take straight away, for the moments when every second counts. Subway After Dark, now being piloted in the Netherlands, is a whole new dining concept for the evening. At the stroke of six, the lighting warms, an evening playlist takes over, Sandwich Artists pull on dedicated After Dark wardrobe and the digital menu boards reveal a more indulgent, customisable menu. Options include items such as Mac ‘n’ Cheese, footlong pizzas and loaded waffle fries, all made to order, alongside drinks and desserts. New brand proposition and campaign in EMEA Blueprint comes to life for guests through Get Your Own Way, a long-term brand platform that celebrates the individual tastes and choices guests have always brought to Subway. articles.title: Starbucks Confirms it is Not Buying Chipotle
articles.titleKo: Starbucks Confirms it is Not Buying Chipotle
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . A potential acquisition attracted attention largely because of Starbucks CEO Brian Niccol's history with Chipotle. Starbucks confirmed Monday that it is not pursuing an acquisition of Chipotle, putting an end to speculation surrounding what could have been the largest merger in restaurant industry history. “As a matter of policy, we don’t comment on rumors and speculation, but we want to be clear we are not buying Chipotle,” Starbucks told Reuters. The statement comes four days after the Financial Times reported that Starbucks had worked with advisers in recent months on a potential takeover proposal for the fast-casual chain. The publication, citing people familiar with the matter, said it was unclear whether a formal offer had been submitted and cautioned that a transaction might never materialize. A potential acquisition attracted attention largely because of Starbucks CEO Brian Niccol’s history with Chipotle. He served as CEO of the burrito chain from 2018 until August 2024, overseeing its recovery from food-safety challenges and leading an expansion of digital ordering and drive-thru Chipotlanes. Such a transaction would have easily surpassed Burger King’s $11.4 billion acquisition of Tim Hortons in 2014, the largest takeover in restaurant industry history. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Blueprint restaurants feature warmer interiors, streamlined layouts, and an expanded digital ordering experience. Subway is introducing a new restaurant prototype across Europe, the Middle East, and Africa (EMEA) as the sandwich giant looks to nearly double its footprint in the region over the next five years. The new concept, called Blueprint, introduces digitally connected restaurants, expanded ordering options, and new menu offerings designed to attract customers throughout the day. Beginning January 1, all new Subway restaurants and remodels in EMEA will adopt the format. The initiative is a key component of Subway’s multiyear growth strategy, which focuses on modernizing the guest experience and improving restaurant economics for franchisees. “Guests want to eat their way, on their own schedule, and Blueprint is how we deliver on that,” Tracy Gehlan, president of Subway EMEA, said in a statement. “We celebrate our guests’ individual choices, from how they order to when they visit to what they want in their meal, always with great food, great service and a great environment. For our franchisees, it means stronger restaurant economics and a stronger brand built for the long term.” Blueprint restaurants feature warmer interiors, streamlined layouts, and an expanded digital ordering experience. Customers can continue ordering directly from employees at the customization counter or use self-service kiosks to browse the menu and build their meals. Mobile ordering and delivery are also integrated into the format. The updated design puts greater emphasis on freshness, with vegetables, sauces, and freshly baked bread prominently displayed. Order-ready screens and designated pickup areas are intended to simplify the experience for guests and employees. Arguably he biggest change is Subway’s effort to capture additional dining occasions outside its traditional lunch business. The company is introducing an expanded breakfast menu and coffee program featuring 100 percent Arabica beans. A new Grab & Go offering, intended for high-traffic locations such as transportation hubs, features freshly prepared meals available for immediate purchase. Subway is also experimenting with a new evening dining experience called Subway After Dark, currently being piloted in the Netherlands. Beginning at 6 p.m., participating restaurants transition to warmer lighting, a different music playlist, and dedicated employee uniforms. Digital menu boards switch to a more indulgent lineup that includes mac and cheese, footlong pizzas, and loaded waffle fries, along with drinks and desserts. The evening concept represents an effort to position Subway as a destination for dinner and late-night occasions, potentially creating new sales opportunities beyond its core sandwich offerings. The Blueprint initiative also introduces a new regional marketing platform called “Get Your Own Way,” which focuses on customization and individual preferences. The campaign will appear across advertising, social media, packaging, digital platforms, and restaurants. The first Blueprint restaurants opened this summer in the Netherlands and U.K., and the new marketing campaign is already active across EMEA. Additional features, including Subway After Dark and Grab & Go, will be introduced based on individual market conditions and restaurant demand. The rollout follows a year of positive sales performance and restaurant growth in the region, according to the company. Subway is working with franchise partners and operators to nearly double its EMEA restaurant footprint over the next five years, a growth target that also includes India, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka. Subway operates more than 35,000 restaurants worldwide, with locations independently owned and operated by franchisees. The restaurant marks the first franchise location for Traci Micheau and business partner Jay Fowler, who will mark the occasion with additional community activities onsite. To kick things off, the first 50 guests in line ages 18 and older will receive free wings for a year — the equivalent of six free wings a week for 52 weeks. Members of the local community are expected to be onsite as a part of the event. Opening day is the payoff of a longtime goal for Micheau, who transitioned from a nearly 20-year corporate career with Buffalo Wild Wings and Inspire Brands to franchise ownership with Fowler, a former Marine and fellow small-town native. “While Buffalo Wild Wings GO is designed for the convenience of takeout and delivery, we felt it was important to create a space where guests can choose to stay and enjoy their meal,” said Micheau. “In a close-knit community like Wauseon, creating a place where friends, families, coworkers and neighbors can effortlessly gather is important. Whether stopping in for a quick lunch, picking up dinner for the family or simply digging into their favorite B-Dubs menu items, our Wauseon team is ready to deliver.” The menu centers on Buffalo Wild Wings favorites — bone-in and boneless wings, chicken dippers, burgers, sandwiches, wraps, fries and 26 signature sauces and dry rubs — with digital ordering and quick pickup built for busy weeknights and game days. This is an important new chapter for Southern Rock, and we look forward to growing the Hawaiian Bros brand with a sharp focus on great teams and strong leadership.” The agreement is one of Hawaiian Bros’ largest development commitments and establishes a significant growth pipeline in a new state. “Entering Florida is a highly anticipated milestone for Hawaiian Bros, and we couldn’t ask for a more experienced group to help establish our presence in the state,” said Grant Kreutzer, Senior Vice President of Franchise Development at Hawaiian Bros. “Max knows these Florida markets extremely well, and Southern Rock has an impressive track record of building and operating successful multi-unit restaurant businesses at scale. Their strong infrastructure makes them exactly the kind of operator we want growing alongside Hawaiian Bros.” Hawaiian Bros’ menu is intentionally simple and prepared with zero freezers, fryers, or microwaves, which also encourages consistent execution, operational efficiency, and a focus on fresh, high-quality ingredients. The brand serves island-inspired plate lunches featuring juicy chicken or pork glazed with sweet, savory, or spicy sauces, paired with fluffy steamed white rice and macaroni salad or vegetables, all of which are prepared in-house. Now in its 21st year, Coffee for a Cure has become The Human Bean’s largest and most anticipated fundraiser each year. It’s a single day each October when every food and beverage order placed at every location becomes a direct act of community care. Since launching the program in 2005, The Human Bean has raised over $4.7 million for breast cancer causes, including a record-breaking $575,640 in 2025 alone. Over twenty years after our first event, it still means so much to come together in this way.” The spirit of that community support is something breast cancer survivor Jacqueline Little knows firsthand. “Coffee for a Cure has meant so much,” she says. “The eagerness and willingness to support a stranger blew me away. The openings span Jacksonville, Florida; Nashville; Salt Lake City; McLean, Virginia; Minnesota’s Mall of America; and Princeton, New Jersey. They include the company’s first East Coast sweetlane drive-thru and a smaller grab-and-go restaurant, demonstrating how Sweetgreen is adapting its real estate strategy to different customer needs. But the activity doesn’t signal an imminent acceleration in development. Sweetgreen is taking a more measured stance on expansion, with greater scrutiny of construction costs, restaurant formats, and long-term returns. Chief development officer Ryan Slemons says the priority is ensuring each new restaurant has the right economics and fits the surrounding community. “We’re maintaining a really high discipline right now on growth,” Slemons says. “What we say is we want to walk now so we can sprint later, and so we’re going to be very disciplined on the trajectory that we’re on and making sure that we’re getting the returns on our investment, and that’s of utmost importance.” That discipline comes during a challenging period for the company. Sweetgreen’s same-store sales declined 6.2 percent in the second quarter, including a 2 percent drop in transactions and a 4.2 percent decline attributable to product mix. Revenue increased approximately 4 percent to $192.7 million. The company finished the quarter with 287 restaurants, including 35 equipped with its automated Infinite Kitchen system. It opened four locations and closed two during the period. Sweetgreen has also lowered its full-year outlook following consumer concerns surrounding a cyclospora outbreak that the company said was not connected to its restaurants. It now expects comparable sales to decline between 7 and 8 percent for the year. Those challenges have put additional pressure on Sweetgreen to ensure its development pipeline contributes to profitability without adding unnecessary financial strain. The company’s real estate strategy involves introducing Sweetgreen to new markets and adding restaurants in established territories where demand can support additional locations. In evaluating potential sites, Slemons says demographics are among the most important considerations. The development team studies the characteristics of surrounding communities, customer behavior, and requests for new restaurants. Visibility and accessibility also factor into the decision. The standards don’t change substantially between a first restaurant in a new city and an additional location in an established market. “We’re trying to pick the best locations that are convenient for customers to visit our restaurants, whether it’s the first restaurant in the market or whether we’re densifying within existing markets. But as you know, in the restaurant space, site selection is critical, and so we want to make sure that for customers, it’s easy for them to shop at a restaurant, there’s good visibility—all that type of stuff when we’re making these decisions,” Slemons says. Recent openings in Jacksonville, Nashville, and Salt Lake City have provided encouraging early indicators. Slemons says Sweetgreen has been particularly pleased with evening and weekend traffic. The company expects to continue adding restaurants in those markets as it evaluates opportunities to build density around its existing footprint. The opening in McLean offers another look at how Sweetgreen is pursuing suburban customers. articles.title: Fresh Dining Concepts Rebrands as Green Shoot Brands
articles.titleKo: Fresh Dining Concepts Rebrands as Green Shoot Brands
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Fresh Dining Concepts, a multi-brand franchisee of iconic, category-leading food and beverage brands, today announced that it has rebranded as Green Shoot Brands (GSB). The new name reflects the company’s growth from 40 Auntie Anne’s locations in 2019 to 388 locations across eight brands in 21 states and Washington, D.C. Green Shoot Brands’ portfolio includes Auntie Anne’s, Carvel, Cinnabon, Dave’s Hot Chicken, Jamba, Little Caesars Pizza, Nothing Bundt Cakes, and PopUp Bagels. The company expects to reach more than $500 million in system sales on a year-end 2026 run-rate basis and ranks among the 30 largest franchisees in the United States. “Our new name better reflects the company we have become: a diversified, multi-brand operator partnering with iconic, category-leading brands, built on evergreen capital and focused on longterm growth,” said Kevin Bush, Founder and Executive Chairman of Green Shoot Brands. “A green shoot is the first sign of growth, and that is exactly what we’re about. We are building for decades, not quarters, for our brand partners, our team members, and the communities we serve.” Unlike traditional private equity, Green Shoot Brands is an evergreen capital holding company with an unlimited time horizon and no exit timeline. That structure lets the company invest longterm in its restaurants, its people, and its brand partners. Its operating standard centers on three commitments to every guest: perfect product, amazing hospitality, and great value. “Our new name doesn’t change how we show up in our restaurants every day,” said Mike Evans, Chief Executive Officer of Green Shoot Brands. “Our general managers and their teams deliver for every guest, every visit, and that is why our brand partners trust us to grow with them. Our goal is to be the franchisee of choice for every brand we operate and the partner of choice for every brand we add.” The rebrand does not affect the company’s ownership, leadership, or existing franchise relationships. Green Shoot Brands will continue to pursue growth through new development and acquisitions across its existing brands and with new brand partners.
