articles.title: Lauren Crowley Joins Sweetgreen as Chief People Officer
articles.titleKo: Lauren Crowley Joins Sweetgreen as Chief People Officer
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Lauren Crowley has more than 20 years of experience leading people organizations through growth and transformation at consumer and technology brands. Sweetgreen, the mission-driven restaurant brand serving healthy food at scale, today announced the appointment of Lauren Crowley as Chief People Officer, effective October 26, 2026. Crowley will report directly to Co-Founder and CEO Jonathan Neman. Lauren Crowley has more than 20 years of experience leading people organizations through growth and transformation at consumer and technology brands, including Expedia Group, Starbucks, Whole Foods Market and Dell. Most recently, she served as Senior Vice President of Human Resources at OC Sports & Entertainment, where she led the people function. During her seven years at Expedia Group, she led enterprise-wide talent programs supporting 16,500 employees across 56 countries, and at Starbucks, she led U.S. retail HR operations supporting more than 200,000 partners across more than 15,000 stores. “What drew me to sweetgreen is its unique combination of purpose, ambition and a genuine commitment to its people,” said Lauren Crowley, Chief People Officer of sweetgreen. “I look forward to partnering with the leadership team and our restaurant teams to build on the strong foundation already in place and create an environment where our people can grow their careers and help shape what’s next for the company.” “Lauren brings the exact blend of strategic vision, operational rigor and people-first leadership that sweetgreen needs at this stage of our journey,” said Jonathan Neman, Co-Founder and CEO of sweetgreen. “She has a deep understanding of how to build strong cultures and people organizations at scale, and I’m thrilled to welcome her to the team. I know she will be an incredible partner to our leaders and our restaurant teams as we continue to evolve and grow.” Adrienne Gemperle, who has served as Chief People Officer through an extraordinary period of growth and change for sweetgreen, will transition out of her role while working alongside Crowley through the end of the year to support a seamless transition. “Adrienne has been an extraordinary leader, partner and champion for our people, and I’m deeply grateful for everything she has given to sweetgreen,” said Jonathan Neman. “She helped build and scale our people organization, and her impact can be seen across our culture, our leadership team and our restaurants.” These leadership changes reflect sweetgreen’s continued investment in its team members and its commitment to establishing a people organization equipped to support the company’s next stage of growth. articles.title: Tender Greens Introduces New Hodo Tofu Dishes
articles.titleKo: Tender Greens Introduces New Hodo Tofu Dishes
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The Fall/Winter menu will be available Oct. 7 for a limited time at all of Tender Greens’ locations. Tender Greens is introducing new dishes that put seasonal vegetables and thoughtfully sourced produce at the center of the menu. Leading the lineup are two limited-time dishes featuring Hodo tofu, the family-owned, Bay Area-based company known for crafting premium, organic tofu with simple ingredients and traditional techniques. The Vegan Tofu Katsu Bowl gives Hodo tofu a crispy treatment, pairing fried tofu with Japanese BBQ sauce, sushi rice, pickled cucumber, carrots, mizuna and cabbage. Sesame and ginger dressing brings the bowl together with a balance of sweet and bright flavors. The result is a completely vegan bowl with crisp tofu, hearty sushi rice and fresh, crunchy vegetables. The Beet & Burrata Salad brings Hodo tofu into a vegetable-forward salad with roasted golden beets, creamy burrata, charred purple Napa Savoy cabbage, whipped tofu and furikake sourdough crisps. Ponzu dressing ties together the sweet roasted beets, rich cheeses and tofu with a savory finish. “Hodo tofu has a great texture and clean flavor, which gave us a lot of room to work it into the menu in different ways,” said Oliver Plust, corporate executive chef at Tender Greens. “We wanted to show what tofu can do beyond a traditional plant-based bowl, from the crispy katsu preparation to the whipped tofu in the Beet & Burrata Salad. At the same time, the fall menu is really about letting the ingredients shine, with mushrooms, squash, carrots and other produce bringing variety to each dish.” Beyond the new seasonal additions, Tender Greens is introducing a menu refresh built around ingredients like cauliflower, mushrooms, winter squash and carrots. Longevity Bowl has a reimagined recipe, featuring roasted mushrooms, fingerling potatoes and Tokyo turnips with olive oil labneh, available with sea bass or braised Romano beans. The bowl is served alongside a winter panzanella made with caramelized apples, delicata squash and golden balsamic vinaigrette. Fall/Winter Harvest Salad combines roasted winter squash, Bosc pears, grapes, pepitas, Laura Chenel goat cheese and caramelized onions with baby lettuces and golden balsamic vinaigrette. California Bowl , available with salmon or chipotle chicken, gets an update with roasted butternut squash salsa, cilantro lime brown rice, cabbage slaw, queso fresco, pepitas and lime crema. Happier Vegan boasts falafel, harissa sauce, farro wheat, carrot hummus with extra virgin olive oil, heirloom cherry tomatoes, pickled cucumbers, onions, roasted peppers, baby lettuces and sherry vinaigrette. Carrot Hummus Toast pairs carrot hummus and whipped feta with shaved carrots, dill, parsley, mint and zaatar on grilled Larder sourdough, finished with golden balsamic vinaigrette. Pomegranate Ginger Agua Fresca brings a bright, fruit-forward option to the beverage lineup. The Fall/Winter menu will be available Oct. 7 for a limited time at all of Tender Greens’ locations. articles.title: Hawaiian Bros Signs Lease in Downtown Atlanta
articles.titleKo: Hawaiian Bros Signs Lease in Downtown Atlanta
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Hawaiian Bros Island Grill, the island-inspired restaurant concept known for its Hawaiian plate lunches and aloha spirit, has signed a lease for its first brick-and-mortar location in Georgia. The restaurant is expected to open in early 2027 and will be located at 112 Courtland St NE adjacent to Georgia State University, marking a key milestone in the brand’s Southeast expansion. The new Hawaiian Bros restaurant will be situated in One12 Courtland, a well-known mixed-use retail, restaurant and student housing development. It will be a convenient neighborhood restaurant for students and downtown workers, who will be able to dine in, order for delivery or pick-up. The brand’s attractive fast-casual setting fosters speed and convenience without sacrificing quality. Menu offerings include a variety of juicy chicken and pork glazed with sweet, savory or spicy sauces, macaroni salad, fluffy steamed white rice, vegetables and tropical Dole Soft Serve®. This location will be owned and operated by MRCO, a seasoned multi-unit franchise group with more than 45 years of restaurant experience and an extensive portfolio of nearly 90 Taco Bell locations. MRCO is leading the brand’s growth across North Carolina, West Central Georgia and North Alabama following a recently signed 34-unit development agreement. Recently, the group expanded its development areas to include 10 more restaurants in the coming years in the contiguous markets of Birmingham, AL, Columbus and Macon, GA, and Auburn, AL. “Bringing Hawaiian Bros’ first physical location to Georgia comes with tremendous pride for us. It will mark a new milestone for the brand and we’re ready to share the island-inspired plate lunch, with more Atlantans,” said Imaan Ferdowsi, CEO of MRCO. “In the heart of Atlanta, this new restaurant will be a natural fit with locals who will appreciate menu items that are prepared fresh in house with high-quality ingredients. We look forward to bringing our aloha spirit to the area as we grow throughout the region.” Slated to open Q1 2027, it reflects a strategic step in the Hawaiian Bros expansion strategy targeting high-growth markets as the brand continues to attract experienced operators like MRCO through its efficient model and strong performance. The new restaurant will join the brand’s ghost kitchen in Decatur that serves Atlanta’s eastside intown neighborhoods. “The southeast is a priority for Hawaiian Bros, and expanding in Georgia with a strong partner like MRCO is an important milestone,” said Grant Kreutzer, Senior Vice President of Franchise Development for Hawaiian Bros. “This location will place the brand in a dynamic, fast-paced environment and sets the stage for continued development.” The Hawaiian Bros franchise opportunity is built for seasoned multi-unit operators with the infrastructure in place to develop and operate multiple locations. Candidates must bring a proven track record in restaurant and hospitality management, with at least 10 years of experience franchising fast-casual, QSR, or casual dining brands. Hawaiian Bros continues to attract established multi-unit groups looking to diversify their portfolios with a unique, fast-growing, high-demand concept. Since launching in 2018, Hawaiian Bros has grown to 80+ restaurants across 14 states, with the majority of locations franchisee owned and operated. There are more than 350 additional restaurants under development agreements spanning 20 states and over 75 markets with 13 multi-unit franchisees. For more information about Hawaiian Bros and its franchise opportunities, including how to apply and claim your territory, visit www.hawaiianbros.com/franchising. articles.titleKo: Secret Burger Kitchen Announces New Locations as it Aims to Become a National, Culture-Driven Burger Chain

Secret Burger Kitchen has signed leases for three new restaurants in Renton, Lynnwood, and Covington, Washington, and is now granting territories to qualified, well-capitalized multi-unit operators. The new locations are under development and will bring the chain from three operating restaurants to six. This announcement marks the next step in the brand’s ambition to build a national, culture-driven burger chain. Secret Burger Kitchen began inside a Tacoma hotel kitchen and now operates in Tacoma, Seattle, and Kirkland. The ownership group is continuing to invest in new restaurants while opening an opportunity for experienced operators to help establish SBK in additional markets. Secret Burger Kitchen’s fresh Angus chuck smash burgers use seasoning beyond salt and pepper, with subtle Punjabi influence designed to create a crave-worthy, umami-rich first bite. Wings, loaded shakes, and interactive sauce syringes extend the meal. A broad, high-energy soundtrack, expressive surroundings, and attentive hospitality make SBK a fun dine-in destination with something for everybody. The company has funded the restaurants and brand development without outside investor capital. The three operating restaurants and franchisor are debt-free. Douglas Fry, David Bloom, and Brad Haley advise Secret Burger Kitchen across operations, development, and marketing. The next three locations will extend Secret Burger Kitchen’s own capital commitment and give the organization more opportunities to refine the operating model as it grows. Secret Burger Kitchen is looking for experienced multi-unit groups to evaluate a brand with operating restaurants, a defined food and guest experience, and an expanding footprint. It’s seeking partners with strong teams, local market knowledge, and the capital to develop thoughtfully. The most important introduction to SBK, however, remains the burger. Fresh Angus chuck meets the grill, develops a seared crust, and comes together with melted cheese, the brand’s own seasoning, and house-made sauces. Founder and CEO Paul Sandhu’s mother’s approach to American and Italian cooking is on display, using the spices she knew from their Punjabi upbringing, which shaped how he thinks about flavor. Sandhu carried that perspective into SBK when, along with his nephew, Mandeep, they began developing the food inside a Holiday Inn kitchen in Tacoma. That origin gives the flavor an honest story, and the original restaurant remains part of the business today. The influence is integrated into a familiar American smash burger. Secret Burger Kitchen wants the guest to enjoy the bite and crave another before thinking about its backstory. It’s a clear distinction: the culinary story is depth of flavor with subtle influence. Wings give guests another reason to visit and groups more ways to order together. Secret Burger Kitchen’s eight flavors span sauces and dry rubs, including Buffalo, Lemon Pepper, Garlic Parmesan, Hot Honey, and Caribbean Jerk. Plant-based availability and a bowl option help accommodate different preferences at the same table. Loaded shakes make dessert part of the occasion. Sauce syringes allow guests to add flavor themselves, giving the meal a recognizable interaction and a moment worth sharing. These details create ways to participate in the experience while keeping the quality of the food at the center. For an operator, it’s a proposition to evaluate across different occasions: a burger-and-fries lunch, a wings visit, a meal with friends or a family outing. More accessible meal choices are part of the chain’s effort to make Secret Burger Kitchen fit ordinary weekdays as well as larger occasions. articles.originalSummary: Following the success of last year’s Connected Icons , Bar Prince at The Balmoral invites guests into a world of myth, magic and storytelling with the launch of its newest cocktail menu, Mythical Legends . Launching this autumn, Mythical Legends draws inspiration from Scotland’s most enduring folklore, transforming legendary creatures and ancient tales into an immersive cocktail experience. From unicorns and selkies to witches, dragons and kelpies, the menu celebrates the stories that have captivated imaginations for generations. Overseen by Head Bartender Mattia Rovaris, each signature cocktail has been individually created by Bar Prince’s mixologists, with every serve inspired by a different Scottish legend. Guests are invited to discover the inspiration behind each creation, with every drink offering its own connection to Scotland’s rich mythical heritage. The theme extends beyond the cocktails themselves. Bespoke illustrations bring each character to life, transforming the menu into a contemporary storybook. Each copy has been meticulously handcrafted by Edinburgh’s Crawford Bookbinders, whose traditional techniques and attention to detail add another layer of craftsmanship, echoing Scotland’s long tradition of storytelling and artistry. Enhancing the experience further is a bespoke Mythical Legends Scent Mist, inspired by Scotland’s ancient forests, mist-covered lochs and legendary landscapes. Blending notes of cedarwood, chamomile and sandalwood with Scots pine, citrus and warming spice, it has been designed to transport guests into the world that inspired the cocktails. Capturing the spirit of Scotland’s wild landscapes and folklore through new techniques and evocative flavour combinations, highlights include The Untamed One , a shimmering tribute to Scotland’s national animal, the unicorn, blending Scottish vodka with coconut water, white chocolate, banana and lime leaf for an elegant serve. Double Identity , inspired by the selkie’s existence between land and sea, reimagines the whisky sour with coastal Scotch whisky, honey, citrus and warming spice. Meanwhile, Kingdom’s Cauldron draws on the tale of the Witch of Fife, combining whisky, botanicals, chocolate, vanilla and caramel into a rich and mysterious after-dark cocktail. Elsewhere, guests can discover the inspiration behind Messy-Nessie , a bright and herbaceous whisky highball inspired by Scotland’s most famous monster, or enjoy Fairy Queen , a decadent take on the Mai Tai featuring aged rum, roasted Brazil nuts and dark cacao. More than a cocktail menu, Mythical Legends is an invitation to explore Scotland’s legendary past through flavour, artistry and imagination. Continuing Bar Prince’s commitment to innovative cocktail storytelling, each drink reveals a new chapter in Scotland’s rich folklore. Mattia Rovaris, Head Bartender at Bar Prince, said: “Building on the success of Connected Icons, Mythical Legends gave our team the opportunity to tell a new chapter of Scotland’s story through the lens of folklore. Each cocktail has been created by a different member of the bar team, making the menu a true collective of ideas, creativity and personal interpretation. Paired with bespoke illustrations and scent, we’ve created an experience that invites guests to discover something new with every serve.” Discover the stories, flavours and aromas behind Scotland’s most captivating folklore at Bar Prince at The Balmoral. Mythical Legends launches this autumn. For more information or to reserve a table, visit: https://www.roccofortehotels.com/hotels-and-resorts/the-balmoral-hotel/dining/bar-prince/cocktail-menu/
koreanSummary: Following the success of last year’s Connected Icons , Bar Prince at The Balmoral invites guests into a world of myth, magic and storytelling with the launch of its newest cocktail menu, Mythical Legends .
Launching this autumn, Mythical Legends draws inspiration from Scotland’s most enduring folklore, transforming legendary creatures and ancient tales into an immersive cocktail experience.
From unicorns and selkies to witches, dragons and kelpies, the menu celebrates the stories that have captivated imaginations for generations.

articles.title: Subway® Unveils Blueprint, a Reimagined Restaurant and Brand Experience for EMEA
articles.titleKo: Subway® Unveils Blueprint, a Reimagined Restaurant and Brand Experience for EMEA
articles.originalSummary: Subway® today unveiled Blueprint, a reimagined restaurant and brand experience that modernises how guests order and eat to support growth across Europe, the Middle East and Africa (EMEA). From 1 January 2027, every new Subway restaurant and remodel in the region will be built to Blueprint, the centrepiece of the company’s multi-year business strategy. For more than 60 years, Subway has been built around customisation: every meal made to order exactly the guest’s way. Blueprint extends that customisation beyond the food to the rest of the experience. The concept began with listening to guests and franchisees. The result is a blueprint for how Subway and its restaurants will look, work and feel as the brand continues to grow. Blueprint covers three areas, each designed to give existing guests more reasons to return and new guests a reason to choose Subway: The restaurant. A fresh look and feel in a digitally connected space that flexes around guests and their choices. Expanded occasions . A new breakfast and coffee offer, Grab & Go, and Subway After Dark, an evening experience with a different menu and mood. The brand. Get Your Own Way, a new brand position and campaign for EMEA, giving Subway one consistent voice. “Guests want to eat their way, on their own schedule, and Blueprint is how we deliver on that,” said Tracy Gehlan, President, Subway EMEA . “We celebrate our guests’ individual choices, from how they order to when they visit to what they want in their meal, always with great food, great service and a great environment. For our franchisees, it means stronger restaurant economics and a stronger brand built for the long term.” Restaurants designed for today’s guests Blueprint restaurants are warmer, more modern, digitally connected spaces. Well-organised layouts and clearer information make the experience more intuitive for guests and easier for Sandwich Artists to manage, so they can give their full attention to the food and the guest in front of them. Choice and freshness take centre stage throughout the design, with salad ingredients, sauces and freshly baked bread showcased at the heart of the restaurant. Guests choose how they order, with every way designed for a seamless experience and every guest getting the same freedom to build a meal exactly their way. At the customisation counter, guests order with a Sandwich Artist, choosing their favourites as they go. Self-order kiosks let guests explore the full menu and customise at their own pace. Subway app and delivery make ordering favourites from home, work or on the move even simpler. An order-ready screen shows each order as it is completed, and a clearly marked collection point makes pick-up quick and easy. Cookies and coffee sit within reach for a last-minute craving. More moments for guests, from morning to evening As guests’ needs change throughout the day, so does the restaurant, with a menu, mood and experience to match. Mornings bring a new breakfast range and coffee offer, made with 100% Arabica beans and served the way each guest wants it, with a morning playlist setting the tone. A new Grab & Go option, available in fast-moving locations such as transport hubs, offers its own menu of meals made fresh in restaurant and ready to take straight away, for the moments when every second counts. Subway After Dark, now being piloted in the Netherlands, is a whole new dining concept for the evening. At the stroke of six, the lighting warms, an evening playlist takes over, Sandwich Artists pull on dedicated After Dark wardrobe and the digital menu boards reveal a more indulgent, customisable menu. Options include items such as Mac ‘n’ Cheese, footlong pizzas and loaded waffle fries, all made to order, alongside drinks and desserts. New brand proposition and campaign in EMEA Blueprint comes to life for guests through Get Your Own Way, a long-term brand platform that celebrates the individual tastes and choices guests have always brought to Subway. articles.title: The Race to Build a Better Drive-Thru
articles.titleKo: The Race to Build a Better Drive-Thru
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The drive-thru was once a convenience attached to the restaurant. For a growing group of limited-service brands, it now serves as the primary dining room, digital pickup counter, and most frequent point of contact with guests. That shift has made the lane a test of nearly every part of the business. Menu complexity shows up in ticket times. Kitchen design determines how many cars a site can process. Digital orders compete for production capacity. Accuracy can decide whether a family returns. Technology can remove delays, but it can also strip away the human connection that gives a brand its identity. For franchise systems, the challenge carries another layer. Any solution must work consistently across hundreds of kitchens, diverse real estate, varied labor pools and different levels of operator experience. Ziggi’s Coffee, Hawaiian Bros, Tropical Smoothie Cafe, and Freddy’s occupy different corners of the quick-service market, but each is working through the same equation, which is that guests want speed, convenience, accuracy, and hospitality in a single visit. Winning more drive-thru occasions requires all four, not a trade of one for another. At Ziggi’s, every restaurant has a drive-thru, and many pair it with a walk-up window. The Colorado-based coffee chain built its system around convenience, but cofounder and CEO Brandon Knudsen does not view the fastest possible transaction as the brand’s ultimate goal. “Speed is not number one at all. I’m not saying it’s not important, but I want to have a really, really authentic relationship. I want there to be a daily routine of coming by to say hi, how are your kids yesterday, how was work, like just total relationship building,” Knudsen says. That conviction influences Ziggi’s technology choices. The company uses tools that help employees learn an expansive menu and find information quickly, including a mobile learning platform that can function as an on-demand reference. Its point-of-sale system supports the transaction, and data helps the chain control staffing. Knudsen sees practical uses for artificial intelligence in corporate analysis and decision-making, but he is reluctant to hand the guest conversation to a machine. “I want Ziggi’s to be a place where they get away from that and they go and interact with people,” he says. Ziggi’s also accepts that a wide range of choices can add seconds. Its drinks are made individually, giving guests the ability to select cold brew, dairy alternatives, decaf, half-caf, and sugar-free options. That creates a more involved production process than systems built around premixed bases. Knudsen considers that flexibility part of the value proposition, not an operating flaw to remove. “We make every drink handcrafted, and that takes more time, right? And so you could look at us in a drive-thru speed report and we’re getting our ass kicked. But at the end of the day, I think that people want what’s important to them. When you go to Ziggi’s, you’re going to have a huge menu. It’s going to take maybe a little bit longer, but you’re going to eat exactly what you want,” Knudsen says. Mobile ordering adds another test. A prepaid drink can turn a visit into a silent handoff, eliminating the exchange Ziggi’s wants to protect. Employees are coached to acknowledge those guests instead of treating the pickup shelf as the end of the service sequence. “Don’t let them pick that drink up without eye contact conversation. ‘Hey, thanks for being here,’” Knudsen says. Hawaiian Bros starts with simplicity. The chain, with roughly 80 restaurants at the time of the interview, has a focused menu and a kitchen built to reproduce a narrow set of plates at volume. Chester’s Express features a streamlined menu of fully cooked items. As Chester’s Chicken approaches its 75th anniversary in 2027, the leading national quick-service restaurant is building on its legacy of delicious, double-breaded chicken with a new format designed to bring the brand to more guests. Chester’s Express, a new grab-and-go model, gives operators with limited kitchen space the opportunity to serve Chester’s signature flavor without a traditional fryer and hood. Chester’s Express features a streamlined menu of fully cooked items, including Chester’s tenders, bites, wings and sandwiches, prepared using a high-speed oven and served hot for customers on the go. The model delivers the brand’s hallmark taste and crunch, creating a flexible foodservice solution for operators with limited kitchen accessibility. “For nearly 75 years, my family has been committed to providing delicious food in surprising places, and Chester’s Express is a natural next step for us,” said Wynn Giles, CEO of Chester’s Chicken. “It gives us another opportunity to grow the brand, offering operators more flexibility while bringing the food our guests love to more communities.” The initial Chester’s Express menu includes three Super Tenders, a fried chicken sandwich, eight chicken bites, six chicken wings, potato wedges, macaroni and cheese and honey butter biscuits. Select locations will also offer breakfast items, including a variety of biscuit sandwiches. “We’re not compromising on quality with Chester’s Express. We’re creating a new way to serve it,” said Alexis Lobodocky, general manager and COO of Chester’s Chicken. “Our operators and teams have prepared thoroughly for this launch, and the enthusiasm across the Chester’s Chicken family reflects what we’re building. Chester’s is doing what we’ve always done best—innovating while staying true to who we are.” Chester’s Express launched at select test locations in August, with additional locations nationwide planned for October and throughout 2027. By adding Express to its existing foodservice offerings, Chester’s can meet the needs of a wider range of operators while continuing to grow its core business and make its signature fried chicken accessible in more locations. The launch follows the introduction of Chester’s 2.0 at NACS in 2025, further demonstrating the brand’s investment in innovation and focus on evolving its foodservice model to meet the changing needs of operators and guests. articles.title: Melba’s Restaurant in Harlem Introduces Braille Menus
articles.titleKo: Melba’s Restaurant in Harlem Introduces Braille Menus
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Melba’s Restaurant, the beloved Harlem restaurant founded by Chef and Owner Melba Wilson, is introducing Braille menus at its flagship location at 300 West 114th Street, expanding accessibility and creating a more independent dining experience for blind and low-vision guests. The launch coincides with Blindness Awareness Month in October. The initiative reflects Melba’s longstanding commitment to making her restaurant a welcoming place for the entire Harlem community. The Braille menus provide guests with the opportunity to independently review the restaurant’s offerings and make their own dining selections without having to rely on a companion or member of the wait staff to read the menu aloud. The menus were developed with David Rockwell and Rockwell Group, bringing thoughtful design and accessibility together in a way that reflects Melba’s belief that an inclusive dining experience should be both welcoming and intentional. Braille production was led by Big Blind Ambition, with production costs for the menus underwritten by EmblemHealth. “Having a Braille menu at Melba’s means inclusion, independence, and dignity. My older cousin losing her sight showed me how much accessibility matters,” said Wilson. “Someone who is blind or visually impaired can walk into Melba’s and feel included, independent, and welcomed. To me, it’s more than just a menu, it is a conscious statement!” “We developed a Braille menu for Melba’s so that the restaurant would be inclusive and inviting to a wider variety of guests — we want everyone to feel welcome,” said David Rockwell, Founder and President of Rockwell Group. “Every guest should be able to experience a restaurant with the same sense of independence, dignity, and discovery.” “At EmblemHealth, we believe community responsibility starts with working with community-based organizations to address unmet needs,” said Karen Ignagni, EmblemHealth CEO. “We are proud to support Melba’s Restaurant in prioritizing accessibility so every guest can enjoy a dignified dining experience. This initiative demonstrates our shared commitment to inclusion and individual empowerment.” “Working with Melba has been great,” said a spokesperson for Big Blind Ambition. “We’re thrilled that she wants to increase awareness and accessibility in the blind community by creating Braille menus. Not only does it give blind people the access to more restaurants, but it creates more opportunities for people that are blind to explore more Braille.” An initial Braille menu is planned to be distributed to Melba’s Harlem on October 1st, with full inventory of the combined Braille and large-print menus available by mid-October across both Melba’s Harlem and Melba’s Newark. Following the Harlem launch, the initiative will expand to Melba’s Grand Central, with Big Blind Ambition converting the location’s current menu into Braille. Newark’s formal introduction to the accessibility initiative will be announced separately at a later date, following that location’s opening. The project is a natural extension of Melba’s approach to hospitality, which has always extended beyond the restaurant’s food. Since opening Melba’s in Harlem in 2005, Wilson has built the restaurant into a community institution while maintaining a deep commitment to giving back. She regularly donates meals to local schools, prepares bereavement meals for families in need, supports local youth through mentorship and community events, and during the COVID-19 pandemic helped provide meals to more than 200,000 seniors. For Wilson, making Melba’s more accessible is another way of honoring the community that has supported the restaurant for more than two decades. Dunn Brothers Coffee, the Minneapolis-based coffee company known for roasting globally sourced coffee beans in small batches in-store daily, is entering Illinois while expanding its footprint in Iowa. The brand signed a development agreement with new franchise partners Beans & Rice, LLC, led by Kevin and Michelle Ramirez. The agreement includes locations in Davenport and Clinton, Iowa, and East Moline, Illinois, with the first shop projected to open in 2027. “We are avid coffee enthusiasts and love everything about Dunn, including seeing everything freshly done in-shop,” said Kevin Ramirez. “We believe in giving back to the areas that allow us to operate, and to give back consistently. Our upcoming coffee shops will allow us to do just that.” The Ramirezes, both Iowa natives, bring more than two decades of franchise experience to the brand. They currently operate multiple Jersey Mike’s Subs locations and previously spent 20 years as Arby’s franchisees. “After more than 20 years in franchising, we know what a strong brand partner looks like,” said Michelle Ramirez. “Dunn Brothers roasts its coffee right in the shop, which gives guests an experience they can’t find anywhere else, and the leadership team has supported us at every step. Those resolved identities can feed PAR Intelligence, which combines identity, transaction, and loyalty signals to help brands decide what to do next for each customer. “Identity resolution is becoming more challenging at the exact moment it is becoming more important,” said Savneet Singh, CEO of PAR Technology. “As consumer behaviors and payment technologies evolve, brands need a more durable way to recognize and understand their customers. Bridg’s enhanced platform is designed to provide that foundation. As contactless and mobile payments continue to gain adoption, many of the traditional signals retailers and marketers have relied on to identify their customers are becoming less available. West joins from Hi Noon Hospitality, where she served as vice president of operations. The Sicilian Butcher, the modern-casual restaurant celebrated for its house-made pastas, 5-foot charcuterie boards, and time-honored Sicilian recipes, has named hospitality veteran Nicole West as president. West brings more than 25 years of multi-unit restaurant leadership to the role and will guide the brand through its next phase of growth. Chef Joey Maggiore opened The Sicilian Butcher in Arizona in 2017 to honor his late father, Chef Tomaso, and carry on his treasured Sicilian recipes. Paired with sister concept The Sicilian Baker and its signature cannoli bar, the brand has built a loyal following. It now operates seven locations across Arizona, Tennessee, and Texas, with its Utah debut planned for 2027. The Maggiore Group partnered with Savory Fund in 2021 to bring its Sicilian table to new markets. West joins from Hi Noon Hospitality, where she served as vice president of operations. There she led five restaurants across three brands with about $40 million in annual revenue. Every location posted record sales, team turnover dropped significantly, and Pinyon Coastal Mediterranean in Scottsdale topped Yelp’s 2026 list of the best Mediterranean restaurants in the U.S. Before that, she spent a decade as CEO of New York Pizza Department, where she led 13 restaurants and 350 team members. She delivered year-over-year growth in sales and profitability and oversaw a full brand refresh. Earlier in her career she held operations leadership roles with Ziegler’s New York Pizza Department, Aramark, and Hillstone Restaurant Group. “Throughout my career, I’ve believed that great restaurant brands are built on exceptional food, genuine hospitality, and a culture that inspires people to be their best,” West said. “Leading a chef-driven, quality-focused brand like The Sicilian Butcher, alongside the amazing Chef Joey Maggiore, is a dream opportunity. Partnering with Savory Fund and its team of leaders and restaurateurs makes this chapter even more meaningful. Their passion for building great brands and investing in great people has me energized about what’s ahead. Here’s to great food, great people, and the magic that happens when you bring them together.” “Nicole cares about our guests and our team the same way we do,” said Joey Maggiore, chef and co-founder of The Maggiore Group with his wife and business partner Cristina Maggiore. “She’s famiglia now, and I can’t wait to see where we take this brand together.” “The Sicilian Butcher has incredible momentum, and Nicole is the right leader to build on it,” said Shauna K. Smith, managing director of Savory Fund. “Her operational strength paired with Chef Joey’s creativity sets the brand up for an exciting next stage of growth.” Beyond the restaurant, West founded #EveryKidDeserves, a nonprofit that provides school supplies and holiday gifts to Arizona foster children, serving 1,000 kids in 2024. Fifty years ago, a beloved family tradition became one of Capriotti’s most iconic sandwiches. Now, The Bobbie is getting a day of its own. On Wednesday, October 14, Capriotti’s Sandwich Shop will celebrate the inaugural Bobbie Day, honoring the original Thanksgiving sandwich inspired by Aunt Bobbie’s day-after-Thanksgiving creation and the generations of fans who have made it a Capriotti’s favorite. To celebrate, Capriotti’s Rewards Members can enjoy Buy One, Get One 50% Off all turkey subs* on October 14. The first 100 Rewards Members to make an in-shop purchase at participating locations that day will also receive a free, limited-edition Bobbie sticker, while supplies last. And because no Thanksgiving experience is complete without gravy, Capriotti’s is bringing it back for a limited time. Beginning on Bobbie Day and continuing through the end of the year, Rewards Members can receive one FREE Side of Gravy with any full-priced sub purchase*, perfect for dipping The Bobbie and adding even more Thanksgiving flavor to every bite. From Family Tradition to an American Sandwich Icon Long before The Bobbie appeared on a Capriotti’s menu, it began around the family table. Every Thanksgiving, the Capriotti family gathered with loved ones. The following day, Aunt Bobbie would turn the holiday leftovers into sandwiches layered with turkey, stuffing, cranberry sauce and mayo. The creation quickly became a family favorite. After Aunt Bobbie passed away, her family honored her memory by sharing the beloved creation with Capriotti’s guests. What began as a limited-time Thanksgiving offering became so popular that The Bobbie earned a permanent place on the menu. But what has made The Bobbie special for 50 years is not only the story behind it. It is how Capriotti’s makes it. Every night, Capriotti’s shops slow-roast whole Butterball® turkeys and hand-pull the turkey each morning before layering it with stuffing, cranberry sauce and mayo. Capriotti’s partnership with Butterball helps ensure The Bobbie begins with the high-quality turkey guests expect from a sandwich built around the flavors of Thanksgiving. “The Bobbie created a category that others have been chasing ever since. But there is a difference between making a Thanksgiving sandwich and making The Bobbie,” said Ashley Morris , CEO of Capriotti’s Sandwich Shop. “For 50 years, we’ve stayed true to the quality, care and tradition that made it an icon in the first place. articles.title: KFC Satisfies Snacking Crazy with New ‘Go Buckets’ Starting at $3.49
articles.titleKo: KFC Satisfies Snacking Crazy with New ‘Go Buckets’ Starting at $3.49
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The KFC bucket dates back to 1957. KFC is introducing Go Buckets, a new way to KFC that brings its signature Finger Lickin’ Good chicken to snacking occasions and moments beyond the traditional meal. Designed for on-the-go occasions, Go Buckets pair a choice of KFC chicken with fries or wedges, starting at just $3.49. The new menu addition comes as snacking plays a bigger role in how Americans eat throughout the day. In fact, 87% of consumers reported snacking outside traditional mealtimes, according to Datassential. At the same time, convenience continues to shape restaurant behavior, with nearly three out of four restaurant orders now taken to go (National Restaurant Association). “People want food to fit into their day, not the other way around,” said Melissa Cash, Chief Marketing Officer, KFC U.S. “Go Buckets open up a new snacking occasion for KFC, whether guests are grabbing one on the go or picking up a few to feed the group. We wanted to meet those changing habits by giving guests more for their money while making it easier to enjoy the KFC they know and love.” Each Go Bucket comes with a choice of four nuggets, two wings or one tender, with six combinations ranging from 16 to 18 grams of protein. And in a first for KFC, Go Buckets are designed to be easily handheld or fit in a standard car cupholder, making it easier to bring KFC wherever the day takes you. The KFC bucket dates back to 1957, when Colonel Harland Sanders and Pete Harman, KFC’s first franchise owner, began filling paper buckets with 14 pieces of Kentucky Fried Chicken, five rolls and a pint of gravy as a family meal to take home and share. Nearly 70 years later, Go Buckets give the iconic bucket a new additional job: making room for the moments between meals, too. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Rosati's Pizza has over 200 locations. Rosati’s Pizza is heading for the biggest development year in its 62-year history, and many of the franchisees driving the expansion have spent decades with the Chicago-born chain. The company, which has over 200 units nationwide, plans to open 11 restaurants within a 90-day stretch, helping Rosati’s set company records for annual openings and the percentage of its system operated by multi-unit franchisees. CEO Anthony Rosati says the surge has been led largely by existing operators. Some have been part of the system for 30 to 40 years and are adding restaurants as they find real estate and seek opportunities outside Rosati’s crowded home market. Chicago alone has more than 100 Rosati’s locations. The company gives operators larger territories than many restaurant chains, making available sites harder to find as the market fills in. That has encouraged some franchisees to look elsewhere. “The main driving forces are our existing franchisees. The unit economics are working for them, and it’s been a good time for them lately,” Rosati says. The expansion didn’t appear overnight. Development timelines gave Rosati’s visibility into its 2026 pipeline during the closing months of 2025, when franchisees were already working through site searches, lease negotiations, and restaurant buildouts. Rosati expects the momentum to continue. “We saw at the end of ’25 starting to round out that ’26 was gonna be a good year, but we had some of that momentum in ’25 too,” he says. “So it keeps pointing towards more growth. And I would say ’27 is probably going to be busier than ’26 the way we’re looking at right now.” Rosati’s believes its longevity has helped give franchisees confidence to keep investing. The family-owned chain traces its restaurant roots back more than a century and opened its first Rosati’s in 1964. The company has watched restaurant trends come and go during that span. Rosati pointed to the rise and retreat of fast-casual pizza and other concepts that expanded quickly before struggling with store-level economics. Pizza, he argues, has retained a different position with consumers as a family and community food. Rosati’s also competes in Chicago, one of the country’s deepest pizza markets. The brand won WGN Radio’s Chicago Pizza Madness tournament in 2025 and again in 2026. Value has become another advantage as restaurant prices have climbed. Rosati says franchisees have worked to maintain labor and food-cost targets despite inflation, and pizza can feed multiple people at a price that compares favorably with other restaurant occasions. Real estate is another piece of the growth equation. Rosati’s prefers end caps in high-traffic shopping areas, especially properties anchored by grocery stores or other major retailers. End caps can cost more, but the company sees value in extra signage, patio space, and street visibility. Second-generation restaurant spaces can make the economics even more attractive. Existing restaurant infrastructure such as grease traps, hoods, bathrooms, plumbing, and electrical systems can cut significant costs from a buildout. Rosati says savings can range from $10,000 to $200,000 depending on the site, reducing the debt a franchisee must carry and helping the restaurant reach breakeven sooner. Opening 11 stores within a short window also puts pressure on Rosati’s support infrastructure. They’ve raised families here, coached youth sports, cheered from the sidelines at school events and spent two decades gathering around tables across the Triangle with friends who became family. Malli is their way of setting a table for the community they now call home. articles.title: El Al Move into Hotels Saw 35,000+ Nights Booked in First Month Powered by Arbitrip Technology
articles.titleKo: El Al Move into Hotels Saw 35,000+ Nights Booked in First Month Powered by Arbitrip Technology
articles.originalSummary: Arbitrip , a leading travel technology platform transforming hotel booking through advanced AI, exclusive pricing, and elevated customer service, today announced strong early results from its landmark partnership with EL AL Airlines , following the launch of a fully white-labeled hotel booking platform embedded within EL AL’s digital ecosystem back in June. In its first month, the platform generated more than 35,000 hotel nights booked, while EL AL customers redeemed more than 130 million frequent flyer points on hotel stays. “The launch of the EL AL Travel platform is a major milestone in the implementation of the company’s long-term strategic plan, which aims to develop new growth engines and expand the range of options we offer our customers,” said Nadav Hanin, VP Marketing and Digital at EL AL . “The new platform will allow customers to book their entire vacation in one place and will enable members of the Matmid Frequent Flyer Club and FLY CARD holders to redeem and earn points and Diamonds on every part of their trip – from flights and hotels, and soon also attractions – and enjoy a complete and cost-effective travel experience.” “This partnership represents a new chapter in travel, and the response from EL AL customers in the first month demonstrates the demand for a more complete experience,” said Benny Yonovich, CEO and Co-founder of Arbitrip . “Travelers expect more than just booking functionality – they want relevance, value and service. More than 35,000 hotel nights booked in the first month shows what can happen when an airline combines the strength of its customer relationship and loyalty program with AI-driven personalization, exclusive pricing and full-service support.” The platform provides access to more than 1.5 million properties worldwide, with dedicated concierge services available for top-tier loyalty members. Meanwhile the new platform allows customers to book their entire vacation in one place and enables members of the Matmid Frequent Flyer Club and FLY CARD holders to redeem and earn points and Diamonds on every part of their trip – from flights and hotels, and soon also attractions – and enjoy a complete and cost-effective travel experience. At the core of the platform is Arbitrip’s advanced AI engine, which moves beyond traditional white-label solutions by dynamically tailoring hotel recommendations to each traveler. Rather than serving a uniform set of results, the system adapts to individual user profiles that include travel history, booking behavior, trip type, and seasonal patterns, helping ensure that passengers receive distinct and highly relevant options. A key advantage of the platform is access to Closed User Group (CUG) rates, unlocking highly competitive pricing not available to the general public. This allows travelers to access preferential hotel rates while avoiding the inflated pricing that can sometimes be associated with point redemptions. Beyond booking functionality, the partnership introduces a full-service agency experience within the airline environment. Travelers who book through the platform gain access to 24/7 support and personalized assistance, combining the efficiency of AI with human expertise. Launching initially with hotel bookings and with plans to expand into additional services such as car rentals and experiences, Arbitrip and EL AL will later develop the platform into a broader travel ecosystem.

articles.titleKo: Pretty Boy Tacos Launches First East London Residency with Little Fires
articles.originalSummary: East London is getting a new taco fix as London based, award winning duo, Pretty Boy Tacos take over the kitchen at Mezcal Bar and hi-fi lounge Little Fires, having begun their residency on Friday 2nd October , bringing their flavour packed take on tacos to the neighbourhood. Founded by two chefs and best friends with over a decade of experience in hospitality, Pretty Boy Tacos has built a reputation for inventive flavour combinations, quality ingredients and a playful approach to Mexican inspired food. The pair’s love affair with Mexican food began after travelling through Mexico, where they fell for the food, culture and people inspiring them to create a taco concept of their own. In Shoreditch, the menu at Little Fires puts Pretty Boy Tacos’ approach firmly front and centre, with tacos as the star of the show, featuring slow cooked Mole Mutton, combining spiced chimichurri, pickled red onion, crispy shallots and mango & habanero, crispy Baja Fish, topped with chipotle mayo, pickled cabbage slaw and jalapeños, smoky, tangy Achiote Grilled Chicken, with spring onion, sweet onion and pineapple salsa verde, and Cochinita Pibil, a traditional Yucatec Mayan slow roasted pork served with habanero, pickled red onion and coriander. Beyond tacos, the menu also features a line up of Mexican inspired small and large plates, including Prawn Ceviche with lime, coriander and red onion, Seared Scallop Aguachile with chorizo oil and tomatillos, Chile Relleno stuffed with adobo minced beef and cheese, and Carne Asada using grass-fed aged onglet with grilled onions, cabbage, tortillas and mole ketchup. The food is matched by Little Fires’ agave led drinks offering, with Margaritas, Palomas, tequila and mezcal cocktails, alongside a selection of mezcal flights. Highlights include the Mango Unchained, with passion fruit purée, mango brine, tequila, Ancho Reyes and lime, and the Añejo y Ploma, Little Fires’ take on an Old Fashioned using añejo tequila, joven mezcal and house bitters. At Little Fires, the Pretty Boy Tacos residency combines their energy with an open kitchen setting and Little Fires’ deep agave offering upstairs, while downstairs, The Listening Lounge runs late into the night. With tacos as their canvas, Pretty Boy Tacos combines classic techniques with unexpected flavours to create food that brings people together to celebrate. Born in London but built to travel, the duo have already taken their food to Amsterdam, Lisbon, Bali and New York, alongside across the capital and now in East London. Pretty Boy Tacos is in residence at Little Fires until January 2027, having begun on 2nd October.
koreanSummary: East London is getting a new taco fix as London based, award winning duo, Pretty Boy Tacos take over the kitchen at Mezcal Bar and hi-fi lounge Little Fires, having begun their residency on Friday 2nd October , bringing their flavour packed take on tacos to the neighbourhood.

Founded by two chefs and best friends with over a decade of experience in hospitality, Pretty Boy Tacos has built a reputation for inventive flavour combinations, quality ingredients and a playful approach to Mexican inspired food.

articles.title: ROAST Shoreditch Will Open at Virgin Hotels London-Shoreditch This October, Bringing the Celebrated British Restaurant to East London
articles.titleKo: ROAST Shoreditch Will Open at Virgin Hotels London-Shoreditch This October, Bringing the Celebrated British Restaurant to East London
articles.originalSummary: ROAST , the acclaimed Borough Market restaurant renowned for championing exceptional seasonal produce and market-fresh ingredients, is set to open its second London restaurant this October at Virgin Hotels London-Shoreditch . ROAST Shoreditch will build on more than two decades of success at Borough Market, bringing its distinctive approach to modern British dining to one of London’s most creative neighbourhoods. The new 135-cover restaurant will offer all-day dining from breakfast and leisurely brunches to long lunches, afternoon tea and dinner, alongside its signature Sunday Roast. At the heart of the menu will be ROAST’s longstanding commitment to outstanding British produce, partnering with trusted farmers, growers and artisan suppliers to create dishes that evolve with the seasons. Diners will find the ROAST classics, including breakfast and the Sunday roast, plus a handful of new dishes created for Shoreditch. A thoughtfully curated wine list and expertly crafted cocktails will complement the experience. The concept pays tribute to Shoreditch’s lesser-known horticultural history and its enduring connection to nearby Columbia Road Flower Market. In doing so, it creates a natural connection with ROAST’s own Borough Market origins, reflecting a shared appreciation of seasonality, craftsmanship and London’s historic market culture. The interiors are by London design agency 3Stories, which has reimagined ROAST for East London as a contemporary Victorian-inspired urban conservatory. Rather than recreate Borough Market, the design builds the ROAST experience around Shoreditch: decorative ironwork, botanical detailing and layered planting nod to the area’s horticultural past, while timber, marble, brass and antique mirrors carry over the warmth of the original. The 135-cover space takes in the main restaurant and bar, a light-filled orangery and a chef’s table. 3Stories has also evolved the ROAST identity for Shoreditch, drawing on Curtain Road, named after The Curtain, an Elizabethan playhouse of Shakespeare’s London. A Harlequin emblem now sits within the identity: a nod to that history and a marker for the Shoreditch restaurant. “Opening our second restaurant is a hugely exciting milestone for the business. Shoreditch feels like a natural evolution for ROAST – a neighbourhood with its own rich history of markets, makers and creativity that closely aligns with our own values. From the design of the space to the food on the plate, everything has been created to celebrate seasonality, craftsmanship and the exceptional quality of British produce. We can’t wait to welcome both local residents and hotel guests this October.” Marc Bevan, CEO of ROAST “ROAST has built a strong reputation around generous British food and warm, uncomplicated hospitality, which makes this partnership feel like a natural fit for Virgin Hotels London-Shoreditch. We’re excited to bring those two experiences together, with ROAST’s breadth of offering, from breakfast and brunch through to afternoon tea, dinner and, of course, its much-loved Sunday roast, complementing the energy and character of the hotel. Together, this aims to be a dining experience that feels genuinely at home in Shoreditch; somewhere hotel guests, locals and visitors alike can settle in, spend time and enjoy themselves.” Barry Vera, Director of Culinary & Beverage at Virgin Hotels Collection ROAST Shoreditch will become a new all-day dining anchor within Virgin Hotels London-Shoreditch, joining the hotel’s hi-fi listening lounge and bar, Hidden Grooves. Bringing together ROAST’s established approach to British food and hospitality with the hotel’s creative East London character, the restaurant has been conceived as a place for locals, London diners and hotel guests alike – whether dropping in for breakfast, meeting over lunch, settling in for dinner or gathering for a Sunday roast. ROAST Shoreditch has opened in October 2026 . Bookings are open now .

articles.title: How New Orleans Keeps Cocktail History Alive
articles.titleKo: How New Orleans Keeps Cocktail History Alive
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . At the Sazerac Bar, the most consequential shift is that guests increasingly arrive with knowledge of specific producers, additive-free tequila, single-barrel whiskey, amaros, and other niche categories. At the Sazerac Bar at The Roosevelt New Orleans, history isn’t tucked behind glass. It lives in the African walnut bar, the Art Deco murals, the silver pieces behind the bar—and, every night, in the rye, sugar, Peychaud’s bitters, absinthe rinse, and lemon oil that make up its namesake cocktail. The Sazerac isn’t simply a drink that shares the bar’s name. Its roots reach back to the Sazerac Coffee House, where, in the 1850s, bar owner Aaron Bird began importing Sazerac-de-Forge et Fils cognac and pairing it with Peychaud’s bitters. The original coffee house eventually closed, but the Sazerac Bar opened at The Roosevelt in 1938, cementing the cocktail’s connection to the hotel and the city’s larger drinking culture. For many guests, having a Sazerac at the Sazerac Bar is “almost like a pilgrimage,” says Matt Schulte, assistant food and beverage director at The Roosevelt New Orleans. “What I love is that after all these years, the drink itself remains remarkably simple,” he says. “There aren’t many places for a bartender to hide. Technique matters.” That kind of history can carry a lot of weight, he adds, but the bar isn’t frozen in time. “We’re not a museum,” Schulte says, noting that the philosophy behind the program is “to honor our history without being trapped by it.” That tension—between honoring a legacy and steering a business into the future—is a familiar dynamic for operators across New Orleans, a city with no shortage of long-running bars and restaurants. Take Tujague’s. Founded in 1856 in the French Quarter, it is New Orleans’ second-oldest restaurant and the country’s third-oldest continuously operating restaurant, according to Mark Latter, founder and CEO of Latter Hospitality. Latter took over Tujague’s in 2013, after his father and uncle had operated the historic restaurant since 1982. The restaurant is home to the Grasshopper, a sweet, mint-and-chocolate after-dinner cocktail made with green crème de menthe, white crème de cacao, and heavy cream. The drink was introduced in 1918 by Philip Guichet, part of the family that owned the restaurant at the time, after a cocktail competition in New York. “It’s still our leading-selling cocktail, which is surprising because it has a lot of cream and it’s a little heavier,” Latter says. For Tujague’s 170th anniversary this year, the restaurant is offering mini Grasshoppers for $1.70, giving first timers an easy entry point to the drink and its history. The team has also explored Grasshopper-inspired desserts, including pie, panna cotta, and cheesecake. Still, Tujague’s is a restaurant, not a nostalgia project. Its broader beverage program is built largely around small variations on familiar drinks, with an eye toward cocktails that work alongside dinner. “Whether it’s the food menu or the cocktail menu, we try to do a riff on classics,” Latter says. Its Iris 75, for instance, builds on the French 75 with purple Empress Gin. It’s a nod to the restaurant’s Krewe of Iris room, which honors the city’s oldest all-female Mardi Gras parade. At the Sazerac Bar, that line is drawn by recognizing which classics are better left alone. The Sazerac and Ramos Gin Fizz do not need an overhaul, Schulte says. Part of their appeal is experiencing them much as previous generations did. “When a classic is already extraordinary, we leave it alone and focus on executing it exceptionally well,” he says. “When we see an opportunity to take the DNA of a classic and tell a new story with it, that’s where our signatures come in.” For those signatures, Schulte says, creativity needs context. articles.title: Toast Launches IQ Team to Help Restaurants Manage Labor Costs
articles.titleKo: Toast Launches IQ Team to Help Restaurants Manage Labor Costs
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Toast, the global technology platform built for restaurant and retail businesses, introduced Toast IQ Team, a new labor management solution for restaurant and retail operators, alongside a significant expansion of Toast IQ Grow, the complete marketing solution Toast introduced earlier in 2026. From building schedules that help manage labor costs to turning great guest experiences into five-star reviews, Toast IQ Team and Toast IQ Grow mark another step toward an agentic platform that absorbs the hardest work of running a business and gives operators measurable proof that it’s working. Restaurant and retail operators juggle everything from scheduling and payroll to marketing, often on thin margins. Many are turning to AI for relief: nearly 9 in 10 restaurant operators surveyed (86%) are experimenting with AI for business purposes, according to Toast’s 2026 Voice of the Restaurant Survey .1 When those tools exist outside of the platforms operators normally use, they risk becoming one more burden to manage. Toast IQ Grow and Toast IQ Team are designed to work differently, with features integrated into the Toast platform, grounded in the user’s own sales, employee, and guest data—and with context on both the user’s business and the jobs to be done. Users get fast, deep insights so operators can take immediate, informed action, without sacrificing the judgment and oversight hospitality requires by keeping humans in the loop. That means less time on tedious work and more time running the businesses. “While every operator wants a packed house or a line out the door, higher volume often brings higher operational complexity,” said Mike Miller, Chief Product Officer at Toast. “We continue to build on our vision for the Toast IQ ecosystem to take on the heavy lifting for restaurants and retailers, especially in the heat of a busy shift. The enhancements to Toast IQ Grow are engineered to attract more guests to an operator’s front door and keep them coming back, while Toast IQ Team is designed to start tackling back office work that comes with that growth. Toast is building agentic solutions that deliver real outcomes.” Toast IQ Team: built to take on labor costs and keep teams happier Toast IQ Team is a new solution that combines forecasting, agentic scheduling and gamification features with payroll and tip management to help operators manage labor costs, run more productive shifts, and create a better employee experience. Scheduling is a high-stakes balancing act: too few people can hurt service, while too many can erode margins, and constantly changing staff availability, time-off and shift-swap requests only add to the challenge. That kind of complex, context-dependent work is exactly what Toast IQ is built to take on. Toast restaurants using the scheduling solution within Toast IQ Team averaged 41% fewer overtime hours per employee than those Toast restaurants not using it.2 Staff it right Sales forecasting [New | AI]: Uses an operator’s historical POS data to help operators plan staffing around anticipated demand, bringing more predictability to labor costs. Scheduling Agent [New | AI] (Beta): Builds a complete schedule in seconds based on employee availability, expected sales, and overtime risk. One of the most essential and time-consuming management tasks becomes a quick review-and-adjust process. Team Performance [New | AI]: Lets operators launch in-platform contests to help motivate staff around high-margin specials, with live leaderboards in MyToast, Toast’s mobile app for restaurant and retail employees. Protein has become part of how people take care of themselves every day, helping them feel satisfied and good about their choices so they can show up for everything on their plate. More than half of Americans say they’re actively trying to get more of it. At a time when bedazzling is having a moment as consumers are adding rhinestones to everyday objects and accessories, Smoothie King is giving protein the bedazzled treatment with the glow-up it deserves. Bringing together the growing conversation around protein and the bedazzling trend, the new offering gives guests a fun way to get the protein they’re looking for in a delicious smoothie, served in its prettiest form yet. The launch taps into the growing role protein plays in helping consumers feel ready for whatever the day brings, as well as the resurgence of bedazzling as a form of colorful self-expression. articles.title: Flash grilled: Tom Childs
articles.titleKo: Flash grilled: Tom Childs
articles.originalSummary: The head chef of Georgie’s Bar and Kerridge’s at Corinthia London on East London trendy chefs, Heston’s Tipsy Cake and banning QR codes in restaurants. What was your first industry job? At 13, I started out at my uncle’s butchers in Beltinge, Kent. Every Saturday, I would deep-clean all the fridges, then he would let me make a variety of sausages and prep whole chickens. If you weren’t in kitchens, what would you do? Most definitely a Premier League footballer. Cooking just pips it, though. What industry figure do you most admire, and why? Gary Rhodes. He led the change in the perception of British food, bringing British cooking into Michelin-level kitchens and giving it the respect it deserved. I believe British food has an unjust reputation for being poor, and Gary played a huge part in changing that. What’s your pet hate in the kitchen? All the East London trendy chefs using pastry cards to pick anything up off a chopping board. Sum up your cooking style in a single sentence… Modern British, ingredient-led, technically precise, but ultimately built around flavour and practicality. What’s the worst review you’ve ever had? On my last day at Paul Ainsworth at No.6, I cooked staff food. Part of it was burnt ends and beans. I cooked some brisket on the Big Green Egg and used far too many smoking chips. Emma Ainsworth took a bite, said it was vile and tasted like an ashtray. What advice would you give someone starting out in the industry? Work hard, listen, understand you are owed nothing. Go out and get what you want, make that phone call to that chef or restaurant, and surround yourself with people you admire. Which single item of kitchen equipment could you not live without? A chef’s knife. Great all-rounder. What would you choose to eat for your last meal? A large bowl of BBQ prawns, scallops and squid in garlic butter. 1kg côte de boeuf, French fries, béarnaise and red wine sauce. Sticky toffee pudding, vanilla ice cream and loads of toffee sauce.

articles.originalSummary: Ruth Hansom, chef-owner of Hansom Restaurant, has been named the UK’s National Chef of the Year by the Craft Guild of Chefs. Hansom was announced as the winner following the competition final at Le Cordon Bleu London yesterday (6 October). Scott John-Hodgson, executive head chef at Solstice & House of Tides by Kenny Atkinson, was named runner-up, while Tom Heywood, head chef and restaurant owner at Pignut & The Hare, took third place. The competition, which has been running for more than 50 years, saw 10 finalists compete in a live cook-off, judged across flavour, creativity, technical ability, working practices, presentation and performance under pressure. Chef patron at Moor Hall Mark Birchall chaired the judging panel, with Cherish Finden serving as chair of pastry.

articles.title: HME Launches Nitro Vision AI for Drive-Thru Operations
articles.titleKo: HME Launches Nitro Vision AI for Drive-Thru Operations
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . HME Hospitality & Specialty Communications (HSC), the leader in drive-thru communications and timing technology, announced the launch of Nitro Vision AI, a camera-based intelligence layer for the drive-thru. Nitro Vision AI helps restaurants move beyond timing alone to see what is happening across the lane, understand what matters, and get that understanding to the people who can act on it. The drive-thru has become a more dynamic operation. Mobile ordering, delivery, and multiple fulfillment paths create demand that shifts quickly across channels, which is why it’s more important than ever for operators to understand what’s happening across their operation. Total visibility is what gives them the context to improve every stage of the customer journey, and that is what Nitro Vision AI adds. Nitro Vision AI builds upon the ZOOM Nitro® Timer, using camera-first vision to recognize each vehicle by Nitro Vision AI also draws on the in-shift tools operators already use in ZOOM Nitro, including the bottleneck tracker, pre-menu threshold alerts, drive-off alerts, and POS integration that surfaces transaction details so crews can spot large orders and keep the line moving, and adds context from across the lane. Together with HME’s NEXEO | HDX™ platform, Nitro Vision AI creates a path for that information to reach crew members through the headsets they already wear, so crews can act while the car is still in the lane. Nitro Vision AI is privacy-conscious by design. It reads vehicle features without license plate recognition or biometric tracking, and it retains no personally identifiable information. By keeping the data accurate and the focus on the lane rather than the people in it, Nitro Vision AI is built to earn the trust of the teams who rely on it. “HME has spent decades helping operators measure the drive-thru. Nitro Vision AI moves us from measurement to intelligence. It brings lane measurement, communication, and now vision together in a way no one else in this space offers,” said Jason Bertellotti, President, HME Hospitality & Specialty Communications. Designed to grow with each restaurant, Nitro Vision AI is built to evolve as vision AI technology advances. To learn more or request a demonstration, visit qsr.hme.com/zoom/visionai. Skinny Louie plans to open three restaurants in October, adding locations in Lauderdale-by-the-Sea and Fort Lauderdale, Florida, and Brooklyn, New York. The Lauderdale-by-the-Sea restaurant, at 107A East Commercial Boulevard, is scheduled to open October 9 at 6 p.m. The Park Slope location, at 218 Flatbush Avenue, will follow on October 16. articles.title: T’s Brunch Bar to Open Fifth Location in Powder Springs, Georgia
articles.titleKo: T’s Brunch Bar to Open Fifth Location in Powder Springs, Georgia
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . T’s Brunch Bar, owned by restaurateur and serial entrepreneur, Teneshia Murray, is set to open their fifth location in Powder Springs (located in West Cobb County, 30 miles from Downtown Atlanta) in November 2026. This location, which continues to be Murray’s love letter to Atlanta’s classic brunch dishes, will open at 5780 Ch James Pkwy, Ste 110, Powder Springs, GA 30127 (formerly occupied by 1738 Restaurant Bar & Lounge (an African & American Fusion Restaurant). Known for a “day party” atmosphere accompanied by live weekend DJ sets, the restaurant has built a strong social media following around photogenic, large-format menu items, such as Crab Fingers, Fried Green Tomatoes, Biscuits & Oxtail Gravy, Seafood Deviled Eggs, Salmon Croquettes, Oxtail Omelets, Chicken & Waffles, Cinnamon Roll Pancakes, and more. The restaurant also went viral on social media for its Ultimate Brunch Tower, which includes waffles, grits, shrimp & grits, catfish nuggets, wings, shrimp, bacon, and crispy breakfast potatoes — all in one epic tower, stacked sky-high. With location five, Murray continues to expand her restaurant footprint, which includes locations in Midtown , Cumberland Mall , Douglasville , and College Park . T’s Brunch Bar-Powder Springs will join Jim ‘N Nicks BBQ, Chili’s Bar & Grill, and LongHorn Steakhouse , which are all within ten-mile radius – along the nearby Jimmy Lee Smith Parkway . “With this new space bordering West Cobb County (Powder Springs) and Paulding County (Hiram), we look forward to serving residents in both municipalities who want a shorter drive for our tasty food and festive experience,” says owner, Teneshia Murray-Butler. Murray plans to offer tasty burger options at this location, such as the Million Dollar Burger, which includes two all-beef premium patties, melted American and pepper jack cheeses, fried egg, lettuce, onion, tomato, bacon, pickles, house sauce and three onion rings (one inside of the burger and two on top of the burger). “With T’s Brunch Bar, we’re looking to expand throughout the Southeast,” says Teneshia Murray-Butler. “I’m so excited to join so thriving businesses in Powder Springs – we plan on bringing food, foot traffic and philanthropy to the area.” Drink items will include The Magic City (consisting of Crown Royal Peach, orange juice, and peach slurry, topped with champagne), the Smoked Pineapple Ginger Margarita, and ChataLata (coconut rum, Rumchata coco crème, tropical Juices) and Mimosa Flights (which includes blueberry lemon, strawberry lemongrass, white peach and pineapple mini mimosas). For T’s Brunch Bar, Murray spent years visiting brunch restaurants around Atlanta, doing research and taking mental notes of her favorite dishes to develop the menu. T’s Brunch Bar is 2,860 sq/ft and seats up to 100 people. The location will be open from seven days a week – Monday through Sunday from 9am – 3pm and Saturday and Sunday from 9am – 5pm. For more information, please visit: https://www.tsbrunchbaratl.com. The post T’s Brunch Bar to Open Fifth Location in Powder Springs, Georgia appeared first on FSR magazine .

articles.title: Gong cha Introduces New Horchata Lineup
articles.titleKo: Gong cha Introduces New Horchata Lineup
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Beginning October 13, participating U.S. stores will introduce the Horchata Milk Tea with Pearls, Horchata Coffee Bobaccino with Pearls and Horchata Tea Bobaccino with Pearls. This fall, Gong cha, the world’s leading bubble tea brand with nearly 2,200 locations in 32 international markets, is bringing the creamy, cinnamon-forward flavor of horchata to the bubble tea menu with three new limited time drinks. Beginning October 13, participating U.S. stores will introduce the Horchata Milk Tea with Pearls, Horchata Coffee Bobaccino with Pearls and Horchata Tea Bobaccino with Pearls. Available for a limited time and while supplies last, the new drinks pair the smooth, creamy flavor of horchata with Gong cha’s milk tea and blended Bobaccino formats, so guests should sip them before they’re gone. NEW Horchata Milk Tea with Pearls: Gong cha spices up its classic milk tea with the cozy, cinnamon-forward flavors of horchata. Served over ice with signature boba pearls and topped with creamy Milk Foam and a dusting of cinnamon, this smooth and comforting sip brings together layers of creamy, spiced flavor. NEW Horchata Coffee Bobaccino with Pearls: This blended take on horchata brings together cinnamon-forward horchata flavor and rich coffee in Gong cha’s frozen Bobaccino. Finished with boba pearls, creamy Milk Foam and a dusting of cinnamon on top, this indulgent drink delivers a rich and creamy combination of coffee and warm cinnamon flavor. NEW Horchata Tea Bobaccino with Pearls: Creamy, cinnamon-forward horchata flavor meets Gong cha’s rich tea in a smooth, blended Bobaccino. Finished with signature boba pearls, creamy Milk Foam and a dusting of cinnamon, this indulgent drink delivers a deliciously creamy way to enjoy the flavor of horchata . “We wanted to give guests multiple ways to enjoy the creamy, cinnamon-forward flavor of horchata at Gong cha,” said Jenn Leitner, Vice President, Brand & Marketing, The Americas for Gong cha. “Guests can keep it cool and refreshing with our Horchata Milk Tea or go blended with our Coffee or Tea Bobaccino. We wanted to give guests options, because when you find a flavor you love, one way to enjoy it is never enough.” Gong cha is celebrating its 20th anniversary! Throughout the year, the brand is unveiling special surprises and events. For more information about the anniversary, visit https://www.gong-cha.com/usa/us-en or follow them on social @gongchatea. Guests can maximize their Gong cha experience by downloading the Gong cha Tea app for iOS and Android. The app allows users to skip the line by ordering ahead, customize their beverages, and earn loyalty points. The post Gong cha Introduces New Horchata Lineup appeared first on QSR Magazine .
