articles.title: Dig Inn Names Dylan Mendelsohn Culinary Director, Launches Fall Menu
articles.titleKo: Dig Inn Names Dylan Mendelsohn Culinary Director, Launches Fall Menu
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The lineup signals a new look at fall. Dig Inn, the fast-casual restaurant known for scratch-made, seasonal cooking, has welcomed new Culinary Director Dylan Mendelsohn and launched Dig Inn’s fall menu, available now at all locations nationwide through the end of the year. The lineup signals a new look at fall, inspired by Mendelsohn’s commitment to innovative, scratch-made, vegetable-forward cooking. Former Director of Culinary at Life Alive Cafe and Eleven Madison Park alum, Mendelsohn brings a culinary sensibility that invokes an elevated but accessible menu spotlighting what the Northeast’s fall harvest has to offer. “The produce changes before the weather does, and this menu is our way of following its lead, pairing familiar fall flavors like Hudson Valley apples and Yukon mashed potatoes with something unexpected, like delicata squash and maple tahini,” said Mendelsohn. “Our kitchen is our second home, and nothing here comes from a shortcut: Every dish is roasted, dressed and prepared the way you’d want it done if you were cooking it for family.” The fall lineup includes: Autumn Farro with Butternut Squash: Cooked in-house daily, mixed with warm fall flavors like roasted butternut squash, citrus tahini, freshly chopped parsley and celery Brussels & Cabbage with Sweet Chili Crisp: Marinated daily and charred to order, tossed with Mr. Bing Chili Crisp Crunchy Roasted Red Beets: Roasted and peeled red beets paired with quinoa and housemade superseed crunch Delicata Squash with Maple Tahini: Tender delicata squash tossed with maple tahini and housemade superseed crunch Hudson Valley Apples with Chai Yogurt: Local Hudson Valley apples marinated in a chai yogurt and served Waldorf-style with dried cranberries, walnuts, mint, celery and cabbage Just a Really Good Salad: A mixture of expertly seasoned Gotham Greens lettuce, lemon, olive oil and herbs Lentil & Chickpea Salad with Feta: Fiber-packed salad of chickpeas, lentils, dried cranberries, feta and red cabbage Yukon Mashed Potatoes with Garlic & Parm: Yukon potatoes steamed and milled daily, with sharp flavors of garlic and parmesan, topped with chives For those looking to feed a group, Dig Inn’s fall lineup also includes two scratch-made family meals and matching catering packages. The Fall Family Meal pairs herb chicken with Brussels sprouts and cabbage in sweet chili crisp, delicata squash with maple tahini, and a lentil and chickpea salad with feta, while the Steak & Mash Family Meal brings char-grilled steak and mashed potatoes for the whole group to enjoy. Both are also available as catering packages – the Fall Catering Package and the Steak & Mash Catering Package – bringing the same scratch-cooked dishes to offices and gatherings in shareable form. Guests can order in-restaurant, through the Dig Inn app or online at www.diginn.com for pickup and delivery, earning Dig Inn Rewards points with every order. articles.title: Hangry Joe’s Names Brandon Wilhelm CEO
articles.titleKo: Hangry Joe’s Names Brandon Wilhelm CEO
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Brandon Wilhelm brings more than 20 years of franchise development experience to the role. Hangry Joe’s, the fast-growing hot chicken franchise with more than 90 locations, today announced the appointment of Brandon Wilhelm as Chief Executive Officer, effective immediately. He will lead the company’s next phase of growth, with a focus on strengthening franchisee support, expanding the brand’s footprint as they are poised to open 20 new locations, and investing in the marketing and operational infrastructure behind Hangry Joe’s continued expansion. Brandon Wilhelm brings more than 20 years of franchise development experience to the role. He spent nearly two decades developing Subway franchise territory across the Midwest as a Development Agent, eventually overseeing operations strategy for more than 500 quick-service restaurant locations and mentoring more than 140 franchisees, before joining the Hangry Joe’s system as a multi-unit franchisee and President of Hangry Development Texas. He currently serves on Hangry Joe’s Franchising’s Board of Directors and most recently served as the company’s Acting Chief Marketing Officer. Wilhelm holds a BBA from Baylor University and an MBA from Southern Methodist University. “My number one focus as CEO is franchisee profitability — reducing COGS, driving sales, and improving our franchise partners’ bottom lines. If we give our franchisees the support, marketing, and systems they need to thrive, this brand will grow organically and quickly. I was actually considering stepping away from the restaurant business altogether, until I tried Hangry Joe’s and fell in love with the food. We have the best chicken in the industry, and I believe the whole country needs to try it.” said Brandon Wilhelm, CEO of Hangry Joe’s. Under Brandon Wilhelm’s leadership, Hangry Joe’s will focus on four priorities. First and foremost, strengthening the profitability of its current franchised locations, ensuring existing franchisees have the support and unit economics to thrive. Second, bolstering the brand’s marketing and advertising investment to drive traffic and brand awareness system wide. Third, improving operational efficiency across the business to support franchisees more effectively. And finally, pursuing smart, disciplined restaurant development by pairing the right franchise owner with the right location, every time. “Brandon has been a trusted partner to this brand for years, and we couldn’t be more confident handing him the keys to our next chapter. His operational experience and genuine commitment to our franchisees make him exactly the right leader to take Hangry Joe’s forward.” said Mike Kim, Co-Founder, Hangry Joe’s Franchising. articles.title: Tom’s Watch Bar Launches Football Tailgate Series Across 12 Markets

articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Tom’s Watch Bar, the ultimate destination for sports viewing and entertainment, announced the launch of its flagship Football Tailgate series for the 2026 to 2027 football season in partnership with Xperience Hospitality, a national event production company specializing in high-energy sports tailgates. Across 12 of its venues, Tom’s Watch Bar will host more than 200 tailgates and pep rallies for both professional and college gamedays over the entire 18-week football season. The activation series will culminate with major tailgate experience for the national championship in February 2027 at all participating venues, including at Tom’s Watch Bar – Inglewood, Calif., located steps from SoFi Stadium where teams will compete in the Big Game. “We saw incredible success hosting tailgates with Xperience Hospitality on football gamedays in 2025, and we’re excited to formalize our partnership for the 2026 to 2027 season,” said Brooks Schaden, Tom’s Watch Bar Co-Founder and Co-CEO. “Tom’s Watch Bar is known for our community-driven atmosphere and stadium-like energy, where fans feel like they have a front row seat to watch their favorite teams compete. These pep rallies and tailgates extend that experience beyond our four walls. We’re taking a fan-first approach to elevate the traditional tailgate experience at scale to create a gameday experience that doesn’t stop at kickoff.” The Football Tailgate series will bring Tom’s Watch Bar’s signature gameday experiences beyond its venues into parking lots, plazas, bridges, and streets that, in some cases, will be steps from the stadiums and arenas where the games are being played. Tom’s Watch Bar will host Saturday pep rallies for college gameday in addition to tailgates every Sunday, giving football fans across the country a high-energy space to gather together, enjoy elevated tailgating dishes and beverages, and feel like they are in the middle of all the action. The Football Tailgate series is designed for Tom’s Watch Bar’s passionate, highly engaged fan base that includes more than four million annual guests. 68% of guests claim professional football as their favorite sport to watch. Over the 18-week football season, the series is expected to drive significant incremental traffic, attracting an estimated 145,000 additional guests to prime locations across 12 markets. Each week, football fans will have the opportunity to enjoy a curated, immersive sports-viewing experience as an extension of Tom’s Watch Bar signature watch parties. Tailgates and pep rallies will feature cornhole, photo opportunities, step-and-repeats, watch-along zones, and live DJ stages before, during, and after games. Fans can also enjoy Tom’s Watch Bar’s premium food and beverages throughout gameday. “Tom’s Watch Bar is known for delivering unrivaled, stadium-side gameday experiences, and this partnership will redefine the meaning of a tailgate,” said Scott McIntire, Xperience Hospitality CEO and Founder. “With our tailgate series, fans get a new way to enjoy and engage the 2026 football season, and we couldn’t be more thrilled to bring this transformative concept to life in partnership with the Tom’s Watch Bar team.” Current venues for Tom’s Watch Bar’s Football Tailgate Series include: Cincinnati, OH Denver, CO Houston, TX Indianapolis, IN Inglewood, CA Las Vegas, NV Los Angeles, CA Minneapolis, MN National Harbor, MD Phoenix, AZ Pittsburgh, PA Seattle, WA You can learn more about the Football Tailgate series at tomswatchbar.com The post Tom’s Watch Bar Launches Football Tailgate Series Across 12 Markets appeared first on FSR magazine .

articles.title: Canadian Concept Shark Club Finds its Opening in America’s Crowded Sports Bar Scene
articles.titleKo: Canadian Concept Shark Club Finds its Opening in America’s Crowded Sports Bar Scene
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . The Canadian-born sports bar sees room for U.S. growth with an elevated food program, flexible real estate strategy, and focus on hospitality. Shark Club’s second U.S. restaurant could prove to be much more than another dot on the map. The Canadian-born sports bar opened in Northlake, Texas, in August, seven years after making its U.S. debut in nearby Plano. The brand is operated by Northland Properties Corporation, which also owns the NHL’s Dallas Stars. The newest restaurant sits inside the Children’s Health StarCenter Multisport complex, a Dallas Stars-affiliated facility serving youth sports and community programming. According to Northland Restaurant Group president and CEO Alan Howie, the location illustrates how Shark Club can find its place in a crowded sports bar field and how its parent company can put the right restaurant into the right piece of real estate. The Northlake opening also gives Shark Club another foundation for U.S. expansion. “We’ve now got two, so we’ve doubled. Maybe we’ll double again,” Howie says. In addition to the two Texas-based locations, Shark Club has four units in Canada and two in the U.K. Northland isn’t committing to a specific unit target for Shark Club. The family-held company has flexibility to pursue real estate as opportunities emerge instead of promising a predetermined number of openings each year. Growth is still a priority. Northland owns a collection of restaurant concepts that covers a wide spectrum of dining occasions. Its portfolio includes Moxies, steakhouse concept Chop, Shark Club, and other brands. The company also owns Denny’s in Canada. That variety gives Northland options when developers or landlords bring potential sites to the company. Instead of finding real estate for a single restaurant concept, Northland can study a property and determine which member of its portfolio has the best fit. Northlake offered an unusually natural match for Shark Club. The Dallas Stars and Northland share an ownership group, and the multisport complex attracts families, athletes, coaches, and fans for hockey, basketball, volleyball, pickleball, and other activities. Howie says Northland considered its portfolio before settling on Shark Club for the complex. “Maybe Denny’s wasn’t the right one for that one, maybe Moxie’s wasn’t the right one for that one, but Shark Club definitely is because this would be people going to play sports and watch their kids play sports and hockey and basketball, all those sorts of things, and the Shark Club environment is the right one for that,” he says. Shark Club occupies roughly 5,000 square feet in Northlake and features 37 televisions, along with a patio overlooking pickleball courts. Its menu includes shareable appetizers, burgers, handhelds, entrees, beverages, late-night specials, and happy hour offerings. Food is a major piece of Northland’s effort to distinguish Shark Club from the field. Howie describes the concept as a sports bar backed by a premium-casual food program and elevated service. The basic requirements for competing in the category are straightforward. Guests expect plenty of televisions, quality sound, and cold beer. Howie believes the restaurant experience provides the separation. Each Shark Club has its own chef in addition to a general manager, a structure Northland also uses at Moxies and Chop. “The things that differentiate us, I think, is the environment and the food,” Howie says. That positioning connects with Shark Club’s “For All Fankind” message. Sports may be the catalyst for many visits, but Northland wants the concept to appeal to people who aren’t arriving solely to watch a game. A guest could be following football, hockey, or tennis, meeting friends, or simply looking for a meal. articles.title: Manhattan’s Piccola Cucina Restaurants Win Tripadvisor Best of the Best Honors
articles.titleKo: Manhattan’s Piccola Cucina Restaurants Win Tripadvisor Best of the Best Honors
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Manhattan’s Piccola Cucina Estiatorio and Piccola Cucina Osteria have been named among the United States’ premier dining destinations in the Tripadvisor Travelers’ Choice Awards Best of the Best, ranking #7 and #11 nationally. This exclusive honor places both establishments within the top 1% of more than 8 million global listings. Helmed by Chef Philip Guardione, the Piccola Cucina Group is a family of restaurants considered to be among the first to bring authentic Sicilian cuisine to Manhattan at a time when southern Italian fare was still emerging in the city’s culinary landscape. Today, the group welcomes diners from across the world, becoming both neighborhood staples as well as destinations for authentic, regionally-specific “ vero cibo siciliano ” for locals and visitors alike. Ranked #7 in the U.S., Piccola Cucina Estiatorio is nestled in the heart of Soho at 75 Thompson Street and beloved for its selection of fresh seafood and coastal Mediterranean dishes. Designed as a traditional Sicilian-style mercato inspired by Chef Guardione’s upbringing in Etna, diners can select their fish directly from the display, alongside classics like octopus caprese. Nearby at 196 Spring Street in Soho, Piccola Cucina Osteria, #11 in the U.S., is a celebration of Chef Guardione’s native Catania. Welcoming diners in a cozy, inviting space, its menu highlights housemade pasta, rustic preparations such as pane cunzato topped with primo sale cheese and anchovy; crowd-pleasing arancini catanese, and tableside tiramisu or cannoli for dessert. Piccola Cucina Group restaurants are renowned for their extensive wine program featuring an encyclopedic, 4,000-bottle wine cellar. The list spans more than 600 labels, with nearly 40% sourced from Sicily and a deep emphasis on Mount Etna, one of the most dynamic and celebrated wine regions in the world today. Every year, TripAdvisor awards travelers’ favorite destinations, hotels, restaurants, and things to do around the world, based on reviews and ratings collected over 12 months. The Travelers’ Choice Awards Best of the Best winners are decided by real travelers from all over, sharing real opinions and stories. The 2026 winners are a celebration of all the places travelers discovered. Piccola Cucina currently has seven locations spanning New York City, Montana, and Ibiza. The lineup features three Greek yogurt bowls at $10.99. Playa Bowls is rallying its shops and guests across the country around the superfruit behind its most recognizable bright pink menu items for a bigger purpose this Breast Cancer Awareness Month. From September 29 through November 2, Playa Bowls is partnering with the Breast Cancer Research Foundation (BCRF), donating a portion of its sales in support of the organization. Playa’s Pink Pitaya campaign supports BCRF’s work advancing breast cancer prevention, detection and treatment while also bringing attention to the role that better-for-you menu items play in supporting guests’ overall wellness. Beyond giving the campaign its vibrant pink hue, pitaya is a nutrient-rich superfruit that is high in essential vitamins and minerals, packed with antioxidants and highlighted as an anti-inflammatory booster. The campaign features three Playa favorites made with the brand’s signature Playa Pitaya base: the Electric Mermaid Bowl, Dragonberry Bowl and Pink Pitaya smoothie. Electric Mermaid Bowl: Naturally hydrating Playa Pitaya topped with blueberry flax granola, pineapple, fiber-rich mango and kiwi, coconut flakes and a drizzle of honey for a colorful, tropical combination that supports digestion. Dragonberry Bowl: Antioxidant- and Vitamin C-rich Playa Pitaya topped with blueberry flax granola, fresh strawberries, blueberries and a drizzle of honey, with prebiotics and fiber from pitaya to support a healthy gut. Pink Pitaya Smoothie: A smooth, vivid blend of Playa Pitaya and organic coconut milk that pairs antioxidant-rich, hydrating pitaya with electrolytes and healthy fats from coconut. Guests can support BCRF throughout the campaign by making a donation in shops, when ordering online, or through Playa Bowls’ dedicated BCRF fundraising page. The giveback efforts will then culminate on Pink Pitaya Giving Day on October 25, as Playa Bowls donates $2 from every pitaya bowl sold nationwide to the organization, giving guests another way to turn their favorite bowl into fuel for lifesaving breast cancer research. “Our vibrant pink Playa Pitaya is a natural connection during Breast Cancer Awareness Month and our mission to offer our guests a convenient way to incorporate more nutrient-rich, better-for-you food into their daily routines,” said Tim Hackbardt, chief marketing officer at Playa Bowls. “It is our goal to bring our Playa community together around them throughout October to help raise funds for BCRF and the lifesaving research it supports.” Founded by Evelyn H. Lauder in 1993, BCRF is one of the world’s leading breast cancer research organizations and the largest private funder of breast cancer research worldwide. The organization supports research spanning prevention, detection, treatment, metastatic disease and survivorship. To learn more about Playa Bowls, visit www.playabowls.com and follow along on Instagram , TikTok , and Facebook for the latest updates. articles.title: Uber to Acquire ezCater for $2.3 Billion
articles.titleKo: Uber to Acquire ezCater for $2.3 Billion
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Uber Eats couriers are expected to gain additional earning opportunities through catering orders. Uber is making a significant move into the catering business. The company announced Tuesday that it reached a $2.3 billion agreement to acquire ezCater, a platform for catering and workplace meals, in an all-cash transaction. The deal is expected to close in the coming months, pending regulatory approval and other customary closing conditions. The acquisition would combine ezCater’s business catering platform with Uber Eats and Uber for Business, giving Uber a larger foothold in a segment that can deliver high-value orders to restaurant partners. ezCater works with more than 140,000 restaurants nationwide and helps businesses manage food orders for meetings, events, and recurring workplace meals. Its technology also includes tools for managing orders and food spending, along with 24/7 customer support. Within the past year, chains like Five Guys, Denny’s, Mendocino Farms, and Mission BBQ have joined the ezCater platform. The company recorded more than $2.5 billion in gross bookings during the trailing 12 months, with growth in the high teens year-over-year. It is profitable on a non-GAAP operating income basis and is expected to be margin accretive to Uber. The size of ezCater’s transactions also sets the business apart from traditional restaurant delivery. Its average order value exceeds $400. “We’re thrilled to be joining forces with Uber. Our team is proud of what we’ve built — the leading platform for workplace catering, and a major growth channel for our restaurant partners,” ezCater CEO Nihad Rahman said in a statement. “We’re energized to bring our catering and B2B expertise to Uber’s global ecosystem of customers, merchants, and couriers.” For restaurants, Uber said the combination could provide access to larger orders and new customers. The deal also gives businesses another way to order group meals through Uber’s ecosystem, covering workplace meals, events, and social gatherings. Uber Eats couriers are expected to gain additional earning opportunities through catering orders as well. The transaction connects three pieces of the companies’ businesses. ezCater brings its catering and B2B expertise and restaurant network, Uber Eats contributes its consumer, restaurant, and delivery reach, and Uber for Business provides existing relationships with organizations of varying sizes. For ezCater, joining Uber offers an opportunity to put its catering technology and restaurant network in front of a much larger customer base. “Catering is a big business, and can be a huge revenue stream for restaurants,” Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi said in a statement. “Nihad and his incredible team have built an amazing platform. With Uber’s reach, we can bring that experience to millions more customers and help restaurants win more of these valuable orders.” The post Uber to Acquire ezCater for $2.3 Billion appeared first on FSR magazine .

articles.title: QSR Ad of the Month: Chick-fil-A Brings Waffles, and Nostalgia, to the Masses
articles.titleKo: QSR Ad of the Month: Chick-fil-A Brings Waffles, and Nostalgia, to the Masses
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Chick-fil-A put on its pajamas for this month’s spotlighted ad, a seasonal promotion for its new Chicken and Waffles sandwich. The ad’s throwback style conceals a canny bit of strategy for the restaurant chain: a move to expand the waffles window from morning to all-day bringing a southern brunch classic to all areas of the country. Waffles and syrup are for breakfast and the brand knows it. Its cast are dressed in pajamas and sleepwear with images of alarm clocks and breakfast tables throughout the ad, and dances which look very much like a set of morning exercises. But the sandwich being promoted with Chick-fil-A chicken joining the waffles is not just a morning proposition, and the ad makes sure viewers know it’s going to be available all day. It’s a win-win strategy for the brand. Promote a new menu item but also make both breakfast and daytime options more attractive for customers and what better way to do that than breakfast all day? The smart marketing extends to the creative elements of the ad, which embraces a very old school aesthetic of joyful dancing, clear product offers and even a brand new and highly catchy jingle, which could easily become a new distinctive asset for Chick-fil-A. You might be tempted to call it “newstalgia,” a trend Chick-fil-A tapped into earlier this year, or part of a trend, but this style of advertising is classic for a reason – it works. Ads like this don’t care whether they seem corny—not when they boast strong branding, clear messaging, and most of all entertainment, all things that moved the sales needle. System1’s Test Your Ad report shows that the old tricks still work. Chick-fil-A’s Chicken and Waffles ad scores a very strong 4.5-Star Rating, a measure that predicts long-term business effects and brand growth. That puts in the top 12 percent of all QSR and Coffee Shop ads. Where Chick-fil-A really shines is in another one of System1’s key metrics, Spike Rating, which predicts an ad’s potential for short-term sales boosts. The Exceptional Spike score is in the top 1 percent in the category—this ad has the potential to be sales dynamite. Why does it work so well? That classic feel puts it in the top tier on the two central components of Spike—the intensity of people’s emotional response to the ad, and their speed of recognition. Emotional intensity matters because whether people are amused or annoyed—and the Star Rating shows it’s mostly amused—the ad is causing a reaction. And Fast Fluency—quick recognition—is born from the early, strong branding. Brand well and get noticed—old school virtues that go together for Chick-fil-A as well as … chicken and waffles. articles.title: How Applebee’s and IHOP Gave Customers ‘Something They Didn’t Know They Wanted’

John Peyton, sitting at Dine Brands HQ in Pasadena, California, was some 8,000 miles away from where the first dual-branded IHOP and Applebee’s sprung up in Dubai. Being so far from corporate, he said, meant the franchisee could veer from the playbook and ask for permission later. Eagles Landing International Restaurants did just that as it designed and opened half a dozen “before we were even paying attention,” Peyton recalled. But, approval aside, he kept hearing positive things. A couple debuted in Mexico and Peyton hopped on a plane. “[I] came back and said to the team, this is a really big idea,” he said. “And we opened the first one a year ago, April.” Speaking at the Barclays Annual Global Consumer Staples Conference, Peyton walked through the much-talked-about model that’s provided Dine Brands a growth lane it hasn’t appreciated in a while. That overseas inspiration- turned-stateside launch outside San Antonio , has 45 open today, with 80 projected by year’s end. All but three are conversions, meaning the original restaurant (Applebee’s or IHOP) added the second. With close to 50 active, Dine Brands has been able to paint a steady economic impact for franchisees. It costs about $1 million to tack on (a bit more going from IHOP to Applebee’s thanks to the addition of a bar). And stores are seeing consistent revenue growth of 1.5 to 2.5X original gains. So, a $2 million IHOP becomes a $3 million combo. The most compelling note for Peyton, he explained, is nobody walked into HQ and suggested putting an IHOP and Applebee’s in the same building, “because no one [would] ever think of that.” Yet when examining tickets, two-thirds are items from both sides of the menu. In the morning, combo restaurants are selling pancakes and ribs. In the evening, they’re moving omelets and skillets. “And so, guests that are experiencing it are actually taking advantage of it,” Peyton said. “We’re giving them something they didn’t know they wanted. And we’ve got a very robust pipeline for next year as well.” He noted most combo stores are now serving Bloody Marys. Peyton was asked about the deliberation process going forward. As leases come up, or franchisee agreements spin, Dine Brands is hosting conversations 12–24 months in advance on what might be next. It covers the typical queries. Should the store move? Has the market changed over the decades? But now, if operators do elect to continue (94 percent of Dine Brands’ agreements are renewed, Peyton said), the notion of a renovation or combo could enter the debate. It’s likely that will happen more often in the years to come. Dine Brands projects 900 opportunities for IHOP-Applebee’s combo stores in the U.S. alone. Of those, 450 are new builds and 450 conversions (an existing brand adding the other). When the company devised the 900 number, Peyton said, as you’d imagine, it built a big model in Pasadena with ample assumptions, market conditions, population growth, and traffic factors. It ran figures with the idea it wouldn’t approve any restaurant in danger of cannibalizing another. If Dine Brands had, for instance, done so with 5–10 percent impact, it would have come up with 1,600 potential outlets instead of 900 (IHOP ended Q2 with 1,813 restaurants and Applebee’s 1,557). In other terms, a lot of franchisees can’t covert. An operator running an Applebee’s 2 miles from an IHOP won’t receive approval to do so. Dine Brands isn’t lacking for internal interest, however. Regarding this note, Peyton said things have not unfolded exactly as expected. The company’s initial hypothesis was it would need to build a batch to prove out the concept and demonstrate numbers for franchisees. The OREO Shake, OREO Cake and OREO Cake Shake are available nationwide at Portillo's locations beginning October 6, 2026, while supplies last. Portillo’s fans know the brand’s famous chocolate cake and cake shakes are simply out of this world. Now, as spooky season gets into full swing, Portillo’s is teaming up with the OREO brand to introduce a trio of new treats: the OREO Shake, OREO Cake and OREO Cake Shake. Available nationwide for a limited time starting October 6, this iconic collaboration gives guests even more flavor-packed menu items to complete their favorite Portillo’s meal. “At Portillo’s, innovation starts with understanding what our guests love, and amplifying it,” said Denise Lauer, Chief Marketing Officer of Portillo’s. “That’s why we’ve reimagined our dessert lineup with three distinctive offerings that bring together the rich flavors of our famous cake and shakes with the unmistakable taste of OREO cookies. We’re excited to introduce an iconic pairing that is both playful and perfectly indulgent, just in time for the Halloween season.” Portillo’s has built a loyal following around its desserts, with the brand’s beloved chocolate cake becoming one of the most talked-about items on the menu – the kind of treat guests build entire orders around. This new collaboration featuring OREO cookies gives fans three new ways to experience that spirit of indulgence: OREO Shake : Portillo’s creamy hand-spun vanilla shake, loaded with crushed OREO cookie pieces in every sip. OREO Cake : A delicate, moist white cake mixed with crushed OREO cookie pieces, iced with sweet OREO frosting and topped with OREO cookie pieces. OREO Cake Shake : A creamy hand-spun vanilla shake mixed with OREO Cake and topped with crushed OREO cookie pieces. The OREO Cake Shake draws its roots from one of Portillo’s signature creations: the original Chocolate Cake Shake, born from a simple idea – blend the brand’s famous cake right into a creamy shake. That creative twist quickly became a guest favorite in its own right, and decades later, the same spirit of invention shaped this collaboration, giving fans three brand-new ways to enjoy Portillo’s cake with one of the world’s most beloved cookies. “The OREO brand has always been about turning a delicious cookie into something people build memories around, and this collaboration with Portillo’s does exactly that,” said Matt Foley, Vice President, OREO. “Bringing our cookie into Portillo’s famous cake, in three different ways, gives fans a fresh, playful way to enjoy OREO cookies beyond the pack.” Portillo’s is also offering members of its Portillo’s Perks loyalty program a hauntingly delicious limited-time deal. articles.title: As New COO at Snooze, Amy Hom’s Leadership Playbook Starts With Listening
articles.titleKo: As New COO at Snooze, Amy Hom’s Leadership Playbook Starts With Listening
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Few operators have seen as many corners of the restaurant industry as Amy Hom. She’s helped run salad bowls at sweetgreen, burgers at Red Robin, and tapas at Barcelona Wine Bar. Now, she’s taking on pancake flights and mimosas. Hom stepped in as chief operating officer of Snooze Eatery on September 28, joining a brand known for its playful, retro-futuristic vibe and creative twists on breakfast classics. “I’m very intentional about the opportunities I choose … At this stage of my career, the question isn’t whether I’ve done the job before,” Hom says. “It’s where I can make a meaningful contribution, continue learning, help build what comes next, and have fun along the way.” In her conversations with CEO Josh Kern and the rest of Snooze’s leadership team, Hom led with curiosity. She wanted to understand the vision for the business, where they believed Snooze could go next, and how she could complement the strengths of the leaders already around the table. Join Hom and other women leaders at FSR and QSR’s annual WiRL Summit! Registration is now open here. “What excited me was the opportunity to help influence and grow the brand while protecting what already makes it special,” Hom adds. “I’m also genuinely looking forward to the journey with Josh and the team … work should be meaningful, challenging, and rewarding, but it should also be enjoyable.” With 72 locations in 10 states, Snooze is eyeing its next growth spurt, and Hom’s appointment reflects an investment in operational leadership. Her task is to lead restaurant operations and work closely with field leaders and teams across the organization. That means elevating hospitality, strengthening operational accountability, and making sure the restaurants have the tools and support to deliver an exceptional guest experience. Hom says consistency doesn’t mean conformity, and she’s certainly not coming in to flatten Snooze’s culture. She doesn’t believe culture and accountability should compete. Instead, she thinks the right operational strategy helps protect culture and creates more freedom for Snoozers. Some things, she says, should be non-negotiable: how the brand takes care of its Snoozers, the quality of its food, and how it treats guests. Leaders also need to be excruciatingly clear about standards. That level of clarity, she says, is part of caring deeply for others. “I don’t need Snooze to feel exactly the same. I want every Snooze to unmistakably feel like Snooze. The last thing I want to do is take the personality, fun, hospitality, and individuality out of our restaurants in the name of operational excellence,” Hom says. “I’ve always said, easy on people, tough on standards … operational discipline should remove unnecessary friction, so our people have more energy to do what they do best—take care of each other and our guests.” Hom has always believed that great operations start with great people, so her first 90 days will include a lot of time in restaurants listening. Her biggest responsibility right now, she says, is to learn the business from the Snoozers who live in it every day. She wants to hear what’s not working, what they need, and what gaps exist between the restaurant support center and the restaurants themselves. But she’s also listening for what’s working. Sometimes, she says, organizations spend so much time looking for problems that they miss chances to celebrate the small wins happening inside their restaurants every day. She’s listening for everything, but especially for patterns. After that, she says, she has a responsibility to close the loop and make sure teams feel heard and understand each decision, whether it’s a yes or a no. “One person saying something is feedback.
